```blyx
        if !bu_finite(at(edges, i)) { return false; }
        if i > 0 && at(edges, i) <= at(edges, i - 1) { return false; }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}
fn bu_find(edges: vector, x: f64) -> i64 {
    let mut low = 0;
    let mut high = len(edges);
    while low < high {
        let mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
        if x < at(edges, mid) { high = mid; } else { low = mid + 1; }
    }
    low
}
pub fn bu_bucket(edges: vector, x: f64) -> i64 {
    if !bu_valid(edges) || !bu_finite(x) { return -1; }
    bu_find(edges, x)
}
// The missing bucket is -1. All other buckets include the lower boundary.
pub fn bu_count(data: vector, edges: vector, bucket: i64) -> i64 {
    if !bu_valid(edges) || bucket < -1 || bucket > len(edges) { return -1; }
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(data) {
        let x = at(data, i);
        if bu_finite(x) {
            if bucket >= 0 && bu_find(edges, x) == bucket { count += 1; }
        } else {
            if bucket == -1 { count += 1; }
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    count
}
fn bu_label(edges: vector, i: i64) {
    if i == -1 { print!("Missing or non-finite"); return; }
    if len(edges) == 0 { print!("All finite values"); return; }
    if i == 0 { print!("Below "); print!(at(edges, 0)); return; }
    print!(at(edges, i - 1));
    if i == len(edges) { print!(" and above"); return; }
    print!(" to below "); print!(at(edges, i));
}
// Emit a semantic HTML fragment. Labels come from numeric edges.
pub fn bu_table(data: vector, edges: vector) -> bool {
    if !bu_valid(edges) { return false; }
    println!("<table><caption>Distribution of observations</caption>");
    println!("<thead><tr><th scope=\"col\">Interval</th><th scope=\"col\">Count</th><th scope=\"col\">Share</th></tr></thead><tbody>");
    let mut bucket = 0;
    while bucket <= len(edges) + 1 {
        let mut id = bucket;
        if bucket == len(edges) + 1 { id = -1; }
        let n = bu_count(data, edges, id);
        let mut total = len(data);
        if total == 0 { total = 1; }
        print!("<tr><th scope=\"row\">"); bu_label(edges, id);
        print!("</th><td>"); print!(n); print!("</td><td><meter aria-label=\"Share of all observations\" min=\"0\" max=\"");
        print!(total); print!("\" value=\""); print!(n); print!("\"></meter> ");
        print!(n); print!(" / "); print!(len(data)); println!("</td></tr>");
        bucket += 1;
    }
    println!("</tbody></table>");
    true
}

fn main() {
    let waits = [0, 4, 5, 8, 10, 12];
    let edges = [5, 10];
    println!(bu_count(waits, edges, 0));
    println!(bu_count(waits, edges, 1));
    println!(bu_count(waits, edges, 2));
}
```

Expected output

```
2
2
2
```

#### Practice

Change the cut points to 4 and 12. Where do the exact boundary observations go?

Hint

Change only the worked example’s input. The API table describes the output.

Solution

Values 4 and 12 move into the buckets beginning at those cut points.

Find

```blyx
let edges = [5, 10];
```

Replace with

```blyx
let edges = [4, 12];
```

Output after the change

```
1
4
1
```

### [Wren · Test an invoice and packing calculation](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/wren)

Run named checks and skips, compare floating-point measurements, and report a TAP 13 stream and a process exit status for CI.

#### The developer problem

A test that only prints an error can leave a build green. TAP defines a machine-readable result for each check and a plan stating how many results to expect. Wren couples that output to the number of failures.

[Test Anything Protocol, TAP 13 specification](https://testanything.org/tap-version-13-specification.html)

#### Run the project locally

The suite checks a decimal invoice total and a whole-box count, then records an offline printer as a skip. Change the expected box count to see the process exit with status 1. Install Blyx 0.2.1, Rust and a host linker, then run these commands.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-wren.git
cd blyx-wren
blyxc native-run project.blyx
```

[Full project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-wren/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Tagged source and downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-wren/releases/tag/v0.1.0)

#### Use the API

Start with wr_begin, pass the returned suite to each check or skip, then call process_exit(wr_end(suite)). The producer emits a trailing TAP plan. Names are truncated at a line break or # to keep the stream unambiguous. Relative tolerance ranges from zero to one. Inputs for measurements and tolerances must be finite.

| Function | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| wr_begin(), wr_check(suite, passed, label) | Import tap. Start a TAP stream and record numbered checks. |
| wr_skip(suite, label, detail), wr_end(suite) | Declare a skip and finish with a plan. wr_end returns 1 when a check failed. |
| wr_near(actual, expected, absolute, relative) | Compare using the larger of an absolute tolerance and a tolerance scaled by the larger input magnitude. |
| wr_start(), wr_record(suite, passed, skipped), wr_exit(suite) | Track total, failed and skipped cases without writing TAP output. |

#### Verify a change

Run the package checks from its release directory. Compare the browser example with its expected output, then change the input in the exercise below.

```
blyxc native-run tests.blyx
```

[Package and installation instructions](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/wren)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Blyx Wren 0.1.0, MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-wren/tree/v0.1.0
// Compare finite measurements using the larger of an absolute and relative tolerance.
pub fn wr_near(actual: f64, expected: f64, absolute: f64, relative: f64) -> bool {
    if actual - actual != 0.0 || expected - expected != 0.0 { return false; }
    if absolute - absolute != 0.0 || relative - relative != 0.0 || absolute < 0.0 || relative < 0.0 || relative > 1.0 { return false; }
    if actual == expected { return true; }
    let mut a = actual;
    let mut b = expected;
    if a < 0.0 { a = -a; }
    if b < 0.0 { b = -b; }
    let mut scale = a;
    if b > scale { scale = b; }
    let mut diff = actual - expected;
    if diff < 0.0 { diff = -diff; }
    if diff <= absolute { return true; }
    if relative == 0.0 { return false; }
    // Scaling first is only necessary when subtraction overflows.
    if diff - diff == 0.0 { return diff / scale <= relative; }
    let mut norm = actual / scale - expected / scale;
    if norm < 0.0 { norm = -norm; }
    norm <= relative
}
pub fn wr_start() -> vector { [0, 0, 0] }
pub fn wr_record(state: vector, passed: bool, skipped: bool) -> vector {
    if len(state) != 3 { return []; }
    let total = at(state, 0) + 1.0;
    let failed = at(state, 1);
    let skip = at(state, 2);
    if skipped { return [total, failed, skip + 1.0]; }
    if passed { return [total, failed, skip]; }
    [total, failed + 1.0, skip]
}
pub fn wr_exit(state: vector) -> i64 {
    if len(state) != 3 || at(state, 1) != 0.0 { return 1; }
    0
}

fn main() {
    let first = wr_record(wr_start(), wr_near(0.1 + 0.2, 0.3, 0.000001, 0.0), false);
    let second = wr_record(first, false, true);
    let result = wr_record(second, 2 * 2 == 5, false);
    println!(at(result, 0));
    println!(at(result, 1));
    println!(at(result, 2));
    println!(wr_exit(result));
}
```

Expected output

```
3
1
1
1
```

#### Practice

Correct the failing arithmetic check and predict the exit code.

Hint

Change only the worked example’s input. The API table describes the output.

Solution

The suite still contains three cases and one skip, with zero failures and status zero.

Find

```blyx
2 * 2 == 5
```

Replace with

```blyx
2 * 2 == 4
```

Output after the change

```
3
0
1
0
```

### [Weaver · Render a file chooser as SVG](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/weaver)

Lay out equal-width tiles on small or large viewports, distribute leftover pixels and map pointer coordinates back to an item.

#### The developer problem

A grid can draw a tile in one place and dispatch a click to its neighbor if painting and input code round dimensions differently. CSS Grid describes how tracks and gaps form a layout. Weaver uses one integer track calculation for both drawing and input.

[W3C, CSS Grid Layout Module Level 1](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-1/#grid-tracks)

#### Run the project locally

The example draws five file tiles in three columns. The final row has two items. Use the same geometry for touch or mouse hit testing when embedding the layout in a UI host. Install Blyx 0.2.1, Rust and a host linker, then run these commands.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-weaver.git
cd blyx-weaver
blyxc native-run project.blyx
```

[Full project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-weaver/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Tagged source and downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-weaver/releases/tag/v0.1.0) · [Open the generated example](https://www.blyx-lang.space/framework-examples/chooser.svg)

#### Use the API

Use integer logical pixels. Width, inset, gap, minimum width and row height support values up to 1,000,000. The column limit is 1–10,000, and a grid can address 1,000,000 items. Invalid geometry produces an empty rectangle or a missed hit. Right and bottom edges are exclusive. A narrow positive content area uses one column.

| Function | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| we_columns(width, inset, gap, minimum, limit) | Choose a responsive column count; zero indicates an empty or invalid content area. |
| we_rect(width, inset, gap, columns, rowHeight, index) | Return [x, y, width, height] in logical pixels. |
| we_hit(width, inset, gap, columns, rowHeight, count, x, y) | Find the item under a pointer. Gutters, empty cells and outside positions return −1. |

#### Verify a change

Run the package checks from its release directory. Compare the browser example with its expected output, then change the input in the exercise below.

```
blyxc native-run tests.blyx
```

[Package and installation instructions](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/weaver)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Blyx Weaver 0.1.0, MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-weaver/tree/v0.1.0
// Integer logical pixels. Layout and hit testing use the same track formula.
fn we_dimension(v: i64) -> bool { v >= 0 && v <= 1000000 }
pub fn we_columns(width: i64, inset: i64, gap: i64, minimum: i64, limit: i64) -> i64 {
    if !we_dimension(width) || !we_dimension(inset) || !we_dimension(gap) || !we_dimension(minimum) || minimum < 1 || limit < 1 || limit > 10000 { return 0; }
    let space = width - 2 * inset;
    if space < 1 { return 0; }
    let fit = (space + gap) / (minimum + gap);
    if fit < 1 { return 1; }
    if fit > limit { return limit; }
    fit
}
fn we_valid(width: i64, inset: i64, gap: i64, cols: i64, row_height: i64) -> bool {
    we_dimension(width) && we_dimension(inset) && we_dimension(gap) && we_dimension(row_height) && row_height > 0 && cols >= 1 && cols <= 10000 && width - 2 * inset - (cols - 1) * gap >= cols
}
fn we_left(space: i64, cols: i64, gap: i64, inset: i64, col: i64) -> i64 {
    let mut extra = col;
    if extra > space % cols { extra = space % cols; }
    inset + col * (space / cols + gap) + extra
}
pub fn we_rect(width: i64, inset: i64, gap: i64, cols: i64, row_height: i64, index: i64) -> vector {
    if !we_valid(width, inset, gap, cols, row_height) || index < 0 || index >= 1000000 { return []; }
    let col = index % cols;
    let space = width - 2 * inset - (cols - 1) * gap;
    let left = we_left(space, cols, gap, inset, col);
    let mut cell = space / cols;
    if col < space % cols { cell += 1; }
    [left, inset + (index / cols) * (row_height + gap), cell, row_height]
}
pub fn we_hit(width: i64, inset: i64, gap: i64, cols: i64, row_height: i64, count: i64, x: i64, y: i64) -> i64 {
    if !we_valid(width, inset, gap, cols, row_height) || count < 0 || count > 1000000 { return -1; }
    if x < inset || x >= width - inset || y < inset { return -1; }
    let row = (y - inset) / (row_height + gap);
    if row >= count || (y - inset) % (row_height + gap) >= row_height { return -1; }
    let space = width - 2 * inset - (cols - 1) * gap;
    let mut low = 0;
    let mut high = cols;
    while low + 1 < high {
        let mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
        if we_left(space, cols, gap, inset, mid) <= x { low = mid; } else { high = mid; }
    }
    let id = row * cols + low;
    if id >= count || x >= we_left(space, cols, gap, inset, low + 1) - gap { return -1; }
    id
}

fn main() {
    let columns = we_columns(320, 8, 8, 80, 6);
    let second = we_rect(320, 8, 8, columns, 48, 1);
    println!(columns);
    println!(at(second, 0));
    println!(we_hit(320, 8, 8, columns, 48, 5, 113, 19));
}
```

Expected output

```
3
112
1
```

#### Practice

Move the pointer four pixels left into the gutter. Which item receives it?

Hint

Change only the worked example’s input. The API table describes the output.

Solution

The coordinates fall between tracks, so the result is −1.

Find

```blyx
5, 113, 19
```

Replace with

```blyx
5, 109, 19
```

Output after the change

```
3
112
-1
```

### [Dipper · Import a two-column notes file](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/dipper)

Parse quoted CSV records, preserve embedded line breaks, and validate a row width before consuming a file.

#### The developer problem

Splitting each line on commas changes both field contents and record counts when a field contains a quoted comma or newline. RFC 4180 describes the quoting and doubled-quote rules that the Dipper parser uses.

[RFC 4180, Common Format and MIME Type for CSV Files](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4180#section-2)

#### Run the project locally

The importer preserves a literal quote in the first note and an embedded newline in the second. Give it a UTF-8 CSV file to check its width before reading the note column. Install Blyx 0.2.1, Rust and a host linker, then run these commands.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-dipper.git
cd blyx-dipper
blyxc native-run project.blyx
```

[Full project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-dipper/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Tagged source and downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-dipper/releases/tag/v0.1.0)

#### Use the API

Parse a UTF-8 string in memory. Delimiters are commas. Records accept CRLF, LF or CR; embedded quoted newlines preserve their original bytes. Spaces are data. A malformed quote discards partial results. Empty input contains zero rows; a blank line holds one empty cell. di_bad_row applies a caller-supplied column count.

| Function | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| di_parse(input), di_ok(records) | Import csv. Parse into F-prefixed field events and R end-of-row events. A lone E-prefixed event describes a syntax error. |
| di_cell(records, row, column) | Return one string for a present cell, including an empty cell; an absent cell returns an empty list. |
| di_bad_row(records, width) | Return the first zero-based row of the wrong width, −1 for success or −2 for a parse or argument error. |
| di_transition(state, token), di_shape(tokens) | Walk the portable quote state machine. A valid stream yields [rows, fields]. |

#### Verify a change

Run the package checks from its release directory. Compare the browser example with its expected output, then change the input in the exercise below.

```
blyxc native-run tests.blyx
```

[Package and installation instructions](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/dipper)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Blyx Dipper 0.1.0, MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-dipper/tree/v0.1.0
// States: field start (0), bare (1), quoted (2), after closing quote (3).
// Tokens: nonempty text (0), comma (1), quote (2), record break (3).
pub fn di_transition(state: i64, token: i64) -> i64 {
    if state < 0 || state > 3 || token < 0 || token > 3 { return -1; }
    if state == 2 {
        if token == 2 { return 3; }
        return 2;
    }
    if token == 1 || token == 3 { return 0; }
    if token == 2 {
        if state == 0 || state == 3 { return 2; }
        return -1;
    }
    if state == 3 { return -1; }
    1
}
pub fn di_complete(state: i64) -> bool { state == 0 || state == 1 || state == 3 }
// For a token stream, report [rows, fields], or [] on malformed input.
pub fn di_shape(tokens: vector) -> vector {
    let mut state = 0;
    let mut rows = 0;
    let mut fields = 0;
    let mut pending = false;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(tokens) {
        let value = at(tokens, i);
        let mut kind = 0;
        while kind < 4 && at([kind], 0) != value { kind += 1; }
        let next = di_transition(state, kind);
        if next < 0 { return []; }
        pending = true;
        if state != 2 {
            if kind == 1 { fields += 1; }
            if kind == 3 { fields += 1; rows += 1; pending = false; }
        }
        state = next;
        i += 1;
    }
    if !di_complete(state) { return []; }
    if pending { fields += 1; rows += 1; }
    [rows, fields]
}

fn main() {
    // Tokens for a quoted field containing a comma followed by a second field.
    let shape = di_shape([2, 0, 1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 3]);
    println!(at(shape, 0));
    println!(at(shape, 1));
    println!(len(di_shape([2, 0])));
}
```

Expected output

```
1
2
0
```

#### Practice

Append a third field before the final record break.

Hint

Change only the worked example’s input. The API table describes the output.

Solution

The extra delimiter is outside quotes, so the row now has three fields.

Find

```blyx
[2, 0, 1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 3]
```

Replace with

```blyx
[2, 0, 1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 1, 0, 3]
```

Output after the change

```
1
3
0
```

### [Kestrel · Replay a bouncing ball across a stalled frame](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/kestrel)

Run a bounded number of simulation ticks per rendered frame, carry fractional frame time and interpolate a moving object between updates.

#### The developer problem

Rendering at a changing frame rate can change simulation speed. A long pause can also produce a burst of catch-up work. Godot’s physics interpolation guide explains the separate clocks. Kestrel makes the carry, interpolation fraction and discarded time visible to the application.

[Godot Engine, Introduction to physics interpolation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/physics/interpolation/physics_interpolation_introduction.html)

#### Run the project locally

Feed the same five frame times into a fixed-step ball simulation. One 100 ms stall exceeds the catch-up limit. The replay reports positions and the number of milliseconds discarded. Install Blyx 0.2.1, Rust and a host linker, then run these commands.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-kestrel.git
cd blyx-kestrel
blyxc native-run project.blyx
```

[Full project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-kestrel/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Tagged source and downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-kestrel/releases/tag/v0.1.0)

#### Use the API

Use whole milliseconds from 0 to 1,000,000,000, a positive step and a remainder smaller than that step. max_steps is 1–1,000,000. The clock returns an empty vector for invalid input. A frame cap discards whole ticks only. The simulation takes frame durations from the caller so a replay needs no wall clock.

| Function | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| ke_clock(carry, elapsed, step, max_steps) | Return [updates, remainder_ms, discarded_ms, interpolation_fraction]. Feed remainder_ms into the next frame. |
| ke_lerp(previous, current, fraction) | Interpolate a render position between the last two simulated positions. |
| ke_bounce(position, velocity, dt, low, high) | Advance one object on a bounded 1D track. The result holds position and velocity, including repeated wall crossings. |

#### Verify a change

Run the package checks from its release directory. Compare the browser example with its expected output, then change the input in the exercise below.

```
blyxc native-run tests.blyx
```

[Package and installation instructions](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/kestrel)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Blyx Kestrel 0.1.0, MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-kestrel/tree/v0.1.0
fn ke_time(ms: f64) -> bool {
    ms >= 0.0 && ms <= 1000000000.0 && ms % 1.0 == 0.0
}
// Return [fixed updates, carried milliseconds, dropped milliseconds, render alpha].
pub fn ke_clock(carry: f64, elapsed: f64, step: f64, max_steps: i64) -> vector {
    if !ke_time(step) || step == 0.0 || !ke_time(elapsed) || !ke_time(carry) || carry >= step || max_steps < 1 || max_steps > 1000000 { return []; }
    let total = carry + elapsed;
    let next = total % step;
    let available = (total - next) / step;
    let mut updates = available;
    let limit = at([max_steps], 0);
    if updates > limit { updates = limit; }
    [updates, next, (available - updates) * step, next / step]
}
pub fn ke_lerp(previous: f64, current: f64, alpha: f64) -> f64 {
    (1.0 - alpha) * previous + alpha * current
}
// Advance an object along a bounded one-dimensional track with elastic walls.
// At an exact wall the stored velocity points inward for the next update.
pub fn ke_bounce(position: f64, velocity: f64, dt: f64, low: f64, high: f64) -> vector {
    if !(low < high && position >= low && position <= high && dt >= 0.0) { return []; }
    let span = high - low;
    let period = 2.0 * span;
    let travel = (position - low) + velocity * dt;
    if period - period != 0.0 || travel - travel != 0.0 { return []; }
    let mut phase = travel % period;
    if phase < 0.0 { phase += period; }
    let mut speed = velocity;
    if speed < 0.0 { speed = -speed; }
    if phase == 0.0 { return [low, speed]; }
    if phase == span { return [high, -speed]; }
    if phase < span { return [low + phase, velocity]; }
    [high - (phase - span), -velocity]
}

fn main() {
    let frame = ke_clock(5.0, 50.0, 10.0, 3);
    println!(at(frame, 0));
    println!(at(frame, 1));
    println!(at(frame, 2));
    println!(at(frame, 3));
}
```

Expected output

```
3
5
20
0.5
```

#### Practice

Increase the catch-up limit from three ticks to five. What happens to the carry?

Hint

Change only the worked example’s input. The API table describes the output.

Solution

All five whole ticks run; the remaining five milliseconds still set the render fraction to 0.5.

Find

```blyx
50.0, 10.0, 3
```

Replace with

```blyx
50.0, 10.0, 5
```

Output after the change

```
5
5
0
0.5
```

### [Heron · Audit a sensor heartbeat trace](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/heron)

Track one sensor feed’s accepted messages, duplicate sequence numbers, out-of-order arrivals and missed deadlines.

#### The developer problem

A replayed packet can make an idle sensor appear healthy if every arrival resets its last-seen timer. ROS 2 distinguishes delivery and deadline policies. Heron lets an application choose a freshness deadline and updates that timer only when it accepts a new sample.

[ROS 2, Quality of service settings](https://docs.ros.org/en/jazzy/Concepts/Intermediate/About-Quality-of-Service-Settings.html)

#### Run the project locally

Replay sequence and local receipt-time pairs. The bundled trace contains a duplicate, a two-ID gap and one out-of-order delivery. You can feed your own two-column headerless trace into the same program. Install Blyx 0.2.1, Rust and a host linker, then run these commands.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-heron.git
cd blyx-heron
blyxc native-run project.blyx
```

[Full project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-heron/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Tagged source and downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-heron/releases/tag/v0.1.0)

#### Use the API

Maintain one state per sensor. Use a monotonically increasing integer sequence and a monotonic local receipt clock in milliseconds, both at most 2^53−1. Reset the state when the sensor restarts or its sequence wraps. The gap counter records skipped IDs at acceptance time. Late arrivals do not reduce it. This release monitors application data and exposes its state to the host.

| Function | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| he_start(), he_observe(state, sequence, receipt_ms) | Initialize or update [last sequence, last receipt, accepted, duplicates, out of order, skipped IDs]. |
| he_age(state, now) | Return milliseconds since the latest accepted observation, or −1 when unavailable. |
| he_status(state, now, deadline) | Return unseen, current, late or invalid. A reading remains current exactly at its deadline. |

#### Verify a change

Run the package checks from its release directory. Compare the browser example with its expected output, then change the input in the exercise below.

```
blyxc native-run tests.blyx
```

[Package and installation instructions](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/heron)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Blyx Heron 0.1.0, MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-heron/tree/v0.1.0
// [last sequence, receipt ms, accepted, duplicates, out of order, skipped IDs].
pub fn he_start() -> vector { [-1, -1, 0, 0, 0, 0] }
fn he_integer(n: f64) -> bool { n >= 0.0 && n <= 9007199254740991.0 && n % 1.0 == 0.0 }
pub fn he_observe(state: vector, sequence: f64, receipt: f64) -> vector {
    if len(state) != 6 || !he_integer(sequence) || !he_integer(receipt) { return []; }
    let last = at(state, 0);
    let stamp = at(state, 1);
    let accepted = at(state, 2);
    let duplicate = at(state, 3);
    let late = at(state, 4);
    let gaps = at(state, 5);
    if sequence < last || receipt < stamp { return [last, stamp, accepted, duplicate, late + 1.0, gaps]; }
    if sequence == last { return [last, stamp, accepted, duplicate + 1.0, late, gaps]; }
    let mut missing = 0.0;
    if last >= 0.0 { missing = sequence - last - 1.0; }
    [sequence, receipt, accepted + 1.0, duplicate, late, gaps + missing]
}
pub fn he_age(state: vector, now: f64) -> f64 {
    if len(state) != 6 || at(state, 1) < 0.0 || !he_integer(now) || now < at(state, 1) { return -1.0; }
    now - at(state, 1)
}
pub fn he_status(state: vector, now: f64, deadline: f64) -> str {
    if len(state) != 6 || !he_integer(now) || !he_integer(deadline) { return "invalid"; }
    if at(state, 0) < 0.0 { return "unseen"; }
    let age = he_age(state, now);
    if age < 0.0 { return "invalid"; }
    if age > deadline { return "late"; }
    "current"
}

fn main() {
    let first = he_observe(he_start(), 10.0, 100.0);
    let next = he_observe(first, 13.0, 120.0);
    let repeated = he_observe(next, 13.0, 145.0);
    println!(at(repeated, 5));
    println!(at(repeated, 3));
    println!(he_status(repeated, 151.0, 30.0));
}
```

Expected output

```
2
1
late
```

#### Practice

Check the feed exactly 30 ms after its last accepted receipt.

Hint

Change only the worked example’s input. The API table describes the output.

Solution

Age equals the deadline, so the feed is current. It becomes late one millisecond later.

Find

```blyx
151.0, 30.0
```

Replace with

```blyx
150.0, 30.0
```

Output after the change

```
2
1
current
```

## Workflow recipes

### [Oriole · Decide when a reviewed revision can go live](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/oriole)

Decide whether a scheduled revision can go live after independent review.

#### Decide when a reviewed revision can go live

A scheduled revision can reach its start time while a second approval is still missing. Track both conditions against the same clock. At tick 12 two distinct reviewers have approved the revision. A duplicate approval cannot replace the second reviewer.

[Wagtail, scheduled publishing](https://guide.wagtail.org/en/concepts/scheduled-publishing/)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-oriole.git
cd blyx-oriole
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 12 10 20 "4,4,8" 2
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-oriole/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [publish now, lifecycle phase, approvals missing, ticks to next transition]. The caller supplies the clock and persists the revision. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| now | exact signed integer |
| opens | exact signed integer |
| closes | exact signed integer |
| reviewers | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| required | positive exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[ReleaseWindow](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/releasewindow) · [ReviewQuorum](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/reviewquorum) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/oriole)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Oriole 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-oriole/tree/v0.1.0

fn releasewindow_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn releasewindow_compute(now: f64, opens: f64, closes: f64) -> vector {
    if closes <= opens {
        return [];
    }
    if now < opens {
        return [0, opens - now];
    }
    if now < closes {
        return [1, closes - now];
    }
    [2, 0]
}

// Locate a clock tick within a scheduled publication window.
// Returns [phase, ticks until the next change]. Phase 0 is scheduled, 1 is live and 2 is expired. The closing tick is exclusive.
pub fn releasewindow_locate(now: f64, opens: f64, closes: f64) -> vector {
    if !(now >= -9007199254740991.0 && now <= 9007199254740991.0 && now % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(opens >= -9007199254740991.0 && opens <= 9007199254740991.0 && opens % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(closes >= -9007199254740991.0 && closes <= 9007199254740991.0 && closes % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = releasewindow_compute(now, opens, closes);
    if !releasewindow_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn reviewquorum_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn reviewquorum_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn reviewquorum_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn reviewquorum_compute(reviewers: vector, required: f64) -> vector {
    let mut unique = 0.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(reviewers) {
        let mut j = 0;
        while j < i && at(reviewers, j) != at(reviewers, i) {
            j += 1;
        }
        if j == i {
            unique += 1.0;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [unique, reviewquorum_max2(0.0, required - unique)]
}

// Count independent reviewers and calculate outstanding approvals.
// Returns [unique reviewer IDs, approvals still required]. A repeated ID contributes once.
pub fn reviewquorum_tally(reviewers: vector, required: f64) -> vector {
    if !reviewquorum_counts(reviewers) { return []; }
    if !(required >= 1.0 && required <= 9007199254740991.0 && required % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = reviewquorum_compute(reviewers, required);
    if !reviewquorum_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn oriole_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn oriole_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn oriole_compute(now: f64, opens: f64, closes: f64, reviewers: vector, required: f64) -> vector {
    let window = releasewindow_locate(now, opens, closes);
    let votes = reviewquorum_tally(reviewers, required);
    if len(window) == 0 || len(votes) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut publish = 0;
    if at(window, 0) == 1.0 && at(votes, 1) == 0.0 {
        publish = 1;
    }
    [publish, at(window, 0), at(votes, 1), at(window, 1)]
}

// Decide whether a scheduled revision can go live after independent review.
// Returns [publish now, lifecycle phase, approvals missing, ticks to next transition]. The caller supplies the clock and persists the revision.
pub fn oriole_decide(now: f64, opens: f64, closes: f64, reviewers: vector, required: f64) -> vector {
    if !(now >= -9007199254740991.0 && now <= 9007199254740991.0 && now % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(opens >= -9007199254740991.0 && opens <= 9007199254740991.0 && opens % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(closes >= -9007199254740991.0 && closes <= 9007199254740991.0 && closes % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !oriole_counts(reviewers) { return []; }
    if !(required >= 1.0 && required <= 9007199254740991.0 && required % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = oriole_compute(now, opens, closes, reviewers, required);
    if !oriole_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let now = 12.0;
    let opens = 10.0;
    let closes = 20.0;
    let reviewers = [4, 4, 8];
    let required = 2.0;
    let result = oriole_decide(now, opens, closes, reviewers, required);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
1
1
0
8
```

#### Practice

Change reviewers = [4, 4]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [publish now, lifecycle phase, approvals missing, ticks to next transition]. The caller supplies the clock and persists the revision.

Solution

The result vector is [0, 1, 1, 8]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let reviewers = [4, 4, 8];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let reviewers = [4, 4];
```

Output after the change

```
0
1
1
8
```

### [Avocet · Reorder stock after reservations](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/avocet)

Plan replenishment after existing reservations and supplier lot sizes.

#### Reorder stock after reservations

Reservations can exhaust a shelf before a reorder calculation runs. Lot-size rounding must include existing backorders. Seven units are on hold. Three units remain free, so buying two lots of four brings free stock to eleven.

[Odoo, reordering rules](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/18.0/applications/inventory_and_mrp/inventory/warehouses_storage/replenishment/reordering_rules.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-avocet.git
cd blyx-avocet
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 10 "3,4" 8 4
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-avocet/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [available, existing shortage, purchase units, projected free units]. Target is the desired free stock after all holds. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| onhand | nonnegative exact integer |
| holds | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| target | nonnegative exact integer |
| lot | positive exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[StockLedger](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/stockledger) · [LotRound](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/lotround) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/avocet)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Avocet 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-avocet/tree/v0.1.0

fn stockledger_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn stockledger_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn stockledger_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn stockledger_compute(onhand: f64, holds: vector) -> vector {
    let used = sum(holds);
    if used > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    [stockledger_max2(0.0, onhand - used), stockledger_max2(0.0, used - onhand)]
}

// Reconcile on-hand inventory with individual outstanding reservations.
// Returns [available units, overcommitted units]. Reservations are nonnegative whole units.
pub fn stockledger_balance(onhand: f64, holds: vector) -> vector {
    if !(onhand >= 0.0 && onhand <= 9007199254740991.0 && onhand % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !stockledger_counts(holds) { return []; }
    let result = stockledger_compute(onhand, holds);
    if !stockledger_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn lotround_ceilpos(value: f64) -> f64 {
    let rest = value % 1.0;
    if rest > 0.0 {
        return value - rest + 1.0;
    }
    value
}

fn lotround_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn lotround_compute(need: f64, lot: f64) -> vector {
    let lots = lotround_ceilpos(need / lot);
    let units = lots * lot;
    if units > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    [lots, units, units - need]
}

// Round a shortage to a supplier's whole purchase lots.
// Returns [lots to order, supplied units, surplus]. A zero shortage orders zero lots.
pub fn lotround_order(need: f64, lot: f64) -> vector {
    if !(need >= 0.0 && need <= 9007199254740991.0 && need % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(lot >= 1.0 && lot <= 9007199254740991.0 && lot % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = lotround_compute(need, lot);
    if !lotround_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn avocet_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn avocet_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn avocet_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn avocet_compute(onhand: f64, holds: vector, target: f64, lot: f64) -> vector {
    let stock = stockledger_balance(onhand, holds);
    if len(stock) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let missing = avocet_max2(0.0, target - at(stock, 0) + at(stock, 1));
    let order = lotround_order(missing, lot);
    if len(order) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(stock, 0), at(stock, 1), at(order, 1), at(stock, 0) - at(stock, 1) + at(order, 1)]
}

// Plan replenishment after existing reservations and supplier lot sizes.
// Returns [available, existing shortage, purchase units, projected free units]. Target is the desired free stock after all holds.
pub fn avocet_plan(onhand: f64, holds: vector, target: f64, lot: f64) -> vector {
    if !(onhand >= 0.0 && onhand <= 9007199254740991.0 && onhand % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !avocet_counts(holds) { return []; }
    if !(target >= 0.0 && target <= 9007199254740991.0 && target % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(lot >= 1.0 && lot <= 9007199254740991.0 && lot % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = avocet_compute(onhand, holds, target, lot);
    if !avocet_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let onhand = 10.0;
    let holds = [3, 4];
    let target = 8.0;
    let lot = 4.0;
    let result = avocet_plan(onhand, holds, target, lot);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
3
0
8
11
```

#### Practice

Change onhand = 2.0, holds = [5], target = 4.0, lot = 3.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [available, existing shortage, purchase units, projected free units]. Target is the desired free stock after all holds.

Solution

The result vector is [0, 3, 9, 6]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx

```

Replace with

```blyx
    let onhand = 2.0;
```

Find

```blyx
    let holds = [3, 4];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let holds = [5];
```

Find

```blyx
    let target = 8.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let target = 4.0;
```

Find

```blyx
    let lot = 4.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let lot = 3.0;
```

Output after the change

```

3
9

```

### [Ibis · Reconcile split invoice payments](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/ibis)

Reconcile an invoice with split payments in integer minor units.

#### Reconcile split invoice payments

Partial payments and overpayments must remain distinguishable when an invoice is reconciled. Two invoice lines total 300 minor units. The payments total 325, leaving 25 as credit.

[GnuCash, accounts receivable](https://www.gnucash.org/docs/v5/C/gnucash-guide/bus_ar.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.1 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-ibis.git
cd blyx-ibis
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "2,1" "125,50" "200,125"
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-ibis/blob/v0.1.1/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [subtotal, applied payment, open balance, credit]. Use a single currency and already-posted amounts. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| units | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| prices | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| payments | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[LineAmount](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/lineamount) · [CashMatch](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/cashmatch) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/ibis)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Ibis 0.1.1 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-ibis/tree/v0.1.1

fn lineamount_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn lineamount_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn lineamount_compute(units: vector, prices: vector) -> vector {
    if len(units) != len(prices) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut total = 0.0;
    let mut lines = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(units) {
        let q = at(units, i);
        let price = at(prices, i);
        if q > 0.0 && price > (9007199254740991.0 - total) / q {
            return [];
        }
        total += q * price;
        if q > 0.0 {
            lines += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [total, lines]
}

// Extend paired invoice quantities and prices in integer minor units.
// Returns [subtotal, nonzero lines]. Rejects unmatched columns and totals beyond exact integer representation.
pub fn lineamount_subtotal(units: vector, prices: vector) -> vector {
    if !lineamount_counts(units) { return []; }
    if !lineamount_counts(prices) { return []; }
    let result = lineamount_compute(units, prices);
    if !lineamount_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn cashmatch_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn cashmatch_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn cashmatch_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn cashmatch_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn cashmatch_compute(due: f64, payments: vector) -> vector {
    let paid = sum(payments);
    if paid > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    [cashmatch_min2(paid, due), cashmatch_max2(0.0, due - paid), cashmatch_max2(0.0, paid - due)]
}

// Apply posted payments and preserve customer credit separately.
// Returns [applied, still due, overpayment] in a single currency's minor units.
pub fn cashmatch_apply(due: f64, payments: vector) -> vector {
    if !(due >= 0.0 && due <= 9007199254740991.0 && due % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !cashmatch_counts(payments) { return []; }
    let result = cashmatch_compute(due, payments);
    if !cashmatch_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn ibis_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn ibis_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn ibis_compute(units: vector, prices: vector, payments: vector) -> vector {
    let lines = lineamount_subtotal(units, prices);
    if len(lines) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let settle = cashmatch_apply(at(lines, 0), payments);
    if len(settle) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(lines, 0), at(settle, 0), at(settle, 1), at(settle, 2)]
}

// Reconcile an invoice with split payments in integer minor units.
// Returns [subtotal, applied payment, open balance, credit]. Use a single currency and already-posted amounts.
pub fn ibis_reconcile(units: vector, prices: vector, payments: vector) -> vector {
    if !ibis_counts(units) { return []; }
    if !ibis_counts(prices) { return []; }
    if !ibis_counts(payments) { return []; }
    let result = ibis_compute(units, prices, payments);
    if !ibis_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let units = [2, 1];
    let prices = [125, 50];
    let payments = [200, 125];
    let result = ibis_reconcile(units, prices, payments);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
300
300
0
25
```

#### Practice

Change units = [2], prices = [10], payments = [4]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [subtotal, applied payment, open balance, credit]. Use a single currency and already-posted amounts.

Solution

The result vector is [20, 4, 16, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

```blyx
    let units = [2, 1];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let units = [2];
```

Find

```blyx
    let prices = [125, 50];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let prices = [10];
```

Find

```blyx
    let payments = [200, 125];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let payments = [4];
```

Output after the change

```

4
16
0
```

### [Pipit · Resume a batch after a failed command](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/pipit)

Plan the next CLI batch from child exit codes and a failure allowance.

#### Resume a batch after a failed command

A batch script can erase an earlier error when the last child exits successfully. Use the whole exit trace to decide whether work should continue. One of three commands failed with exit code 3. The configured allowance permits two further commands.

[Python, subprocess exit status](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.CompletedProcess.returncode)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-pipit.git
cd blyx-pipit
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0,3,0" 8 2 1
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-pipit/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [next offset, next count, failures, first nonzero exit]. The next count becomes zero once failures exceed the allowance. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| codes | Vector of: whole byte in [0,255] |
| total | nonnegative exact integer |
| batch | positive exact integer |
| tolerance | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[ExitPolicy](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/exitpolicy) · [BatchQuota](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/batchquota) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/pipit)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Pipit 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-pipit/tree/v0.1.0

fn exitpolicy_bytes(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 255.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn exitpolicy_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn exitpolicy_compute(codes: vector) -> vector {
    let mut failures = 0;
    let mut first = -1;
    let mut code = 0.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(codes) {
        if at(codes, i) != 0.0 {
            if first < 0 {
                first = i;
                code = at(codes, i);
            }
            failures += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [failures, code, first]
}

// Summarize portable process exit codes without losing the first failure.
// Returns [failed commands, first nonzero exit code, first failing index]. An all-success run uses index -1.
pub fn exitpolicy_summarize(codes: vector) -> vector {
    if !exitpolicy_bytes(codes) { return []; }
    let result = exitpolicy_compute(codes);
    if !exitpolicy_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn batchquota_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn batchquota_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn batchquota_compute(done: f64, total: f64, limit: f64) -> vector {
    if done > total {
        return [];
    }
    let take = batchquota_min2(limit, total - done);
    [done, take, total - done - take]
}

// Bound the next batch of an interrupted command.
// Returns [next offset, batch length, remaining after batch]. A finished batch has zero length.
pub fn batchquota_allow(done: f64, total: f64, limit: f64) -> vector {
    if !(done >= 0.0 && done <= 9007199254740991.0 && done % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(total >= 0.0 && total <= 9007199254740991.0 && total % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(limit >= 1.0 && limit <= 9007199254740991.0 && limit % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = batchquota_compute(done, total, limit);
    if !batchquota_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn pipit_num(value: i64) -> f64 {
    at([value], 0)
}

fn pipit_bytes(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 255.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn pipit_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn pipit_compute(codes: vector, total: f64, batch: f64, tolerance: f64) -> vector {
    let status = exitpolicy_summarize(codes);
    let next = batchquota_allow(pipit_num(len(codes)), total, batch);
    if len(next) == 0 || len(status) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut count = at(next, 1);
    if at(status, 0) > tolerance {
        count = 0.0;
    }
    [at(next, 0), count, at(status, 0), at(status, 1)]
}

// Plan the next CLI batch from child exit codes and a failure allowance.
// Returns [next offset, next count, failures, first nonzero exit]. The next count becomes zero once failures exceed the allowance.
pub fn pipit_continue_batch(codes: vector, total: f64, batch: f64, tolerance: f64) -> vector {
    if !pipit_bytes(codes) { return []; }
    if !(total >= 0.0 && total <= 9007199254740991.0 && total % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(batch >= 1.0 && batch <= 9007199254740991.0 && batch % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(tolerance >= 0.0 && tolerance <= 9007199254740991.0 && tolerance % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = pipit_compute(codes, total, batch, tolerance);
    if !pipit_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let codes = [0, 3, 0];
    let total = 8.0;
    let batch = 2.0;
    let tolerance = 1.0;
    let result = pipit_continue_batch(codes, total, batch, tolerance);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
3
2
1
3
```

#### Practice

Change codes = [0, 3], tolerance = 0.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [next offset, next count, failures, first nonzero exit]. The next count becomes zero once failures exceed the allowance.

Solution

The result vector is [2, 0, 1, 3]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let codes = [0, 3, 0];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let codes = [0, 3];
```

Find

```blyx
    let tolerance = 1.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let tolerance = 0.0;
```

Output after the change

```
2
0
1
3
```

### [Nuthatch · Keep terminal help visible after a resize](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/nuthatch)

Wrap a message and preserve a valid scroll position after resizing a terminal.

#### Keep terminal help visible after a resize

After a terminal becomes wider, the old scroll offset can leave an otherwise valid help screen blank. Four words each occupy their own line. A scroll request past the end selects the last two visible lines.

[Python, text wrapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/textwrap.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-nuthatch.git
cd blyx-nuthatch
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "4,4,4,4" 6 99 2
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-nuthatch/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [wrapped line count, first visible line, exclusive end, last line width]. The host supplies display-cell widths for its font. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| widths | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| columns | positive exact integer |
| start | nonnegative exact integer |
| height | positive exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[WordRows](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/wordrows) · [ViewPortion](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/viewportion) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/nuthatch)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Nuthatch 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-nuthatch/tree/v0.1.0

fn wordrows_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn wordrows_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn wordrows_compute(widths: vector, columns: f64) -> vector {
    let mut lines = 0;
    let mut used = 0.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(widths) {
        let width = at(widths, i);
        if width == 0.0 || width > columns {
            return [];
        }
        if used == 0.0 || used + 1.0 + width > columns {
            lines += 1;
            used = width;
        } else {
            used += 1.0 + width;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [lines, used]
}

// Count greedy terminal lines from premeasured word widths.
// Returns [lines, last line width]. One display cell separates words. Empty input uses zero lines; zero-width and oversize words are rejected.
pub fn wordrows_measure(widths: vector, columns: f64) -> vector {
    if !wordrows_counts(widths) { return []; }
    if !(columns >= 1.0 && columns <= 9007199254740991.0 && columns % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = wordrows_compute(widths, columns);
    if !wordrows_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn viewportion_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn viewportion_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn viewportion_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn viewportion_compute(rows: f64, start: f64, height: f64) -> vector {
    let first = viewportion_min2(start, viewportion_max2(0.0, rows - height));
    let end = viewportion_min2(rows, first + height);
    [first, end, rows - end]
}

// Clamp a terminal scroll offset to a filled viewport.
// Returns [first visible row, exclusive end row, rows hidden below]. A short document starts at zero.
pub fn viewportion_slice(rows: f64, start: f64, height: f64) -> vector {
    if !(rows >= 0.0 && rows <= 9007199254740991.0 && rows % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(start >= 0.0 && start <= 9007199254740991.0 && start % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(height >= 1.0 && height <= 9007199254740991.0 && height % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = viewportion_compute(rows, start, height);
    if !viewportion_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn nuthatch_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn nuthatch_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn nuthatch_compute(widths: vector, columns: f64, start: f64, height: f64) -> vector {
    let flow = wordrows_measure(widths, columns);
    if len(flow) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let view = viewportion_slice(at(flow, 0), start, height);
    if len(view) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(flow, 0), at(view, 0), at(view, 1), at(flow, 1)]
}

// Wrap a message and preserve a valid scroll position after resizing a terminal.
// Returns [wrapped line count, first visible line, exclusive end, last line width]. The host supplies display-cell widths for its font.
pub fn nuthatch_layout(widths: vector, columns: f64, start: f64, height: f64) -> vector {
    if !nuthatch_counts(widths) { return []; }
    if !(columns >= 1.0 && columns <= 9007199254740991.0 && columns % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(start >= 0.0 && start <= 9007199254740991.0 && start % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(height >= 1.0 && height <= 9007199254740991.0 && height % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = nuthatch_compute(widths, columns, start, height);
    if !nuthatch_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let widths = [4, 4, 4, 4];
    let columns = 6.0;
    let start = 99.0;
    let height = 2.0;
    let result = nuthatch_layout(widths, columns, start, height);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
4
2
4
4
```

#### Practice

Change widths = [2, 2], columns = 5.0, start = 0.0, height = 3.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [wrapped line count, first visible line, exclusive end, last line width]. The host supplies display-cell widths for its font.

Solution

The result vector is [1, 0, 1, 5]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

```blyx

```

Replace with

```blyx

```

Find

```blyx
    let columns = 6.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let columns = 5.0;
```

```blyx

```

Replace with

```blyx
    let start = 0.0;
```

```blyx
    let height = 2.0;
```



### [Turnstone · Restart an interrupted chunked file job](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/turnstone)

Resume a chunked file job from acknowledged checkpoints.

#### Restart an interrupted chunked file job

A resumed batch can skip the final partial chunk when it treats a repeated acknowledgement as new progress. Ten bytes form three chunks of width four. The repeated checkpoint for chunk zero leaves the two-byte final chunk to process.

[Python, batching iterables](https://docs.python.org/3/library/itertools.html#itertools.batched)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-turnstone.git
cd blyx-turnstone
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 10 4 "0,0,1"
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-turnstone/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [next offset, byte count, remaining chunks, replayed checkpoints]. Offsets use half-open ranges. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| size | nonnegative exact integer |
| width | positive exact integer |
| checkpoints | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[ChunkSpan](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/chunkspan) · [ResumeIndex](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/resumeindex) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/turnstone)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Turnstone 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-turnstone/tree/v0.1.0

fn chunkspan_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn chunkspan_ceilpos(value: f64) -> f64 {
    let rest = value % 1.0;
    if rest > 0.0 {
        return value - rest + 1.0;
    }
    value
}

fn chunkspan_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn chunkspan_compute(size: f64, width: f64, index: f64) -> vector {
    let count = chunkspan_ceilpos(size / width);
    if index > count {
        return [];
    }
    let first = chunkspan_min2(size, index * width);
    [first, chunkspan_min2(size, first + width), count]
}

// Locate a fixed-width chunk including the final partial chunk.
// Returns [start, exclusive end, chunk count]. Index equal to chunk count marks completion.
pub fn chunkspan_bounds(size: f64, width: f64, index: f64) -> vector {
    if !(size >= 0.0 && size <= 9007199254740991.0 && size % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(width >= 1.0 && width <= 9007199254740991.0 && width % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(index >= 0.0 && index <= 9007199254740991.0 && index % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = chunkspan_compute(size, width, index);
    if !chunkspan_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn resumeindex_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn resumeindex_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn resumeindex_compute(checkpoints: vector, count: f64) -> vector {
    let mut next = 0.0;
    let mut repeats = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(checkpoints) {
        let mark = at(checkpoints, i);
        if mark >= count || mark > next {
            return [];
        }
        if mark == next {
            next += 1.0;
        } else {
            repeats += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [next, repeats]
}

// Recover the first unfinished chunk from an ordered checkpoint log.
// Returns [next chunk, replay count]. Duplicate checkpoints are accepted. A forward gap or out-of-range ID invalidates the log.
pub fn resumeindex_prefix(checkpoints: vector, count: f64) -> vector {
    if !resumeindex_counts(checkpoints) { return []; }
    if !(count >= 0.0 && count <= 9007199254740991.0 && count % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = resumeindex_compute(checkpoints, count);
    if !resumeindex_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn turnstone_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn turnstone_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn turnstone_compute(size: f64, width: f64, checkpoints: vector) -> vector {
    let first = chunkspan_bounds(size, width, 0.0);
    if len(first) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let progress = resumeindex_prefix(checkpoints, at(first, 2));
    if len(progress) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let chunk = chunkspan_bounds(size, width, at(progress, 0));
    [at(chunk, 0), at(chunk, 1) - at(chunk, 0), at(chunk, 2) - at(progress, 0), at(progress, 1)]
}

// Resume a chunked file job from acknowledged checkpoints.
// Returns [next offset, byte count, remaining chunks, replayed checkpoints]. Offsets use half-open ranges.
pub fn turnstone_resume(size: f64, width: f64, checkpoints: vector) -> vector {
    if !(size >= 0.0 && size <= 9007199254740991.0 && size % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(width >= 1.0 && width <= 9007199254740991.0 && width % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !turnstone_counts(checkpoints) { return []; }
    let result = turnstone_compute(size, width, checkpoints);
    if !turnstone_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let size = 10.0;
    let width = 4.0;
    let checkpoints = [0, 0, 1];
    let result = turnstone_resume(size, width, checkpoints);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
8
2
1
1
```

#### Practice

Change checkpoints = [0, 1, 2]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [next offset, byte count, remaining chunks, replayed checkpoints]. Offsets use half-open ranges.

Solution

The result vector is [10, 0, 0, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let checkpoints = [0, 0, 1];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let checkpoints = [0, 1, 2];
```

Output after the change

