```
0
0
0
```

### [Osprey · Score detections at the edge of a camera frame](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/osprey)

Score a detection against a reference after clipping both to the camera frame.

#### Score detections at the edge of a camera frame

An out-of-frame detection can change IoU even when the visible pixels agree. Clip both boxes before evaluating their overlap. Clipping the predicted box gives four visible intersection pixels and a union of eight. IoU reaches the inclusive 0.5 threshold.

[OpenCV, rectangle coordinates](https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d2/d44/classcv_1_1Rect__.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-osprey.git
cd blyx-osprey
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "-2,0,2,2" "0,0,4,2" 4 4 0.5
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-osprey/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [visible IoU, matched, visible intersection area]. Match requires positive overlap and a score at least equal to the threshold. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| pred | Vector of: finite number |
| truth | Vector of: finite number |
| width | positive finite number |
| height | positive finite number |
| threshold | probability in [0,1] |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[BoxOverlap](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/boxoverlap) · [BoxClip](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/boxclip) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/osprey)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Osprey 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-osprey/tree/v0.1.0

fn boxoverlap_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn boxoverlap_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn boxoverlap_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn boxoverlap_compute(a: vector, b: vector) -> vector {
    if len(a) != 4 || len(b) != 4 {
        return [];
    }
    let aw = at(a, 2) - at(a, 0);
    let ah = at(a, 3) - at(a, 1);
    let bw = at(b, 2) - at(b, 0);
    let bh = at(b, 3) - at(b, 1);
    if aw <= 0.0 || ah <= 0.0 || bw <= 0.0 || bh <= 0.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let w = boxoverlap_max2(0.0, boxoverlap_min2(at(a, 2), at(b, 2)) - boxoverlap_max2(at(a, 0), at(b, 0)));
    let h = boxoverlap_max2(0.0, boxoverlap_min2(at(a, 3), at(b, 3)) - boxoverlap_max2(at(a, 1), at(b, 1)));
    let hit = w * h;
    let combined = aw * ah + bw * bh - hit;
    if combined <= 0.0 {
        return [];
    }
    [hit, combined, hit / combined]
}

// Measure intersection and union of two axis-aligned image boxes.
// Each rectangle is [left, top, right, bottom]. Returns [intersection area, union area, IoU]. Zero-area boxes and reversed edges are rejected.
pub fn boxoverlap_measure(a: vector, b: vector) -> vector {
    if !boxoverlap_finite(a) { return []; }
    if !boxoverlap_finite(b) { return []; }
    let result = boxoverlap_compute(a, b);
    if !boxoverlap_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn boxclip_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn boxclip_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn boxclip_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn boxclip_compute(box: vector, width: f64, height: f64) -> vector {
    if len(box) != 4 {
        return [];
    }
    let left = boxclip_max2(0.0, at(box, 0));
    let top = boxclip_max2(0.0, at(box, 1));
    let right = boxclip_min2(width, at(box, 2));
    let bottom = boxclip_min2(height, at(box, 3));
    if right <= left || bottom <= top {
        return [];
    }
    [left, top, right, bottom]
}

// Clip a detection rectangle to the visible image.
// Returns the visible [left, top, right, bottom] in continuous pixel-edge coordinates. An empty intersection is invalid.
pub fn boxclip_inside(box: vector, width: f64, height: f64) -> vector {
    if !boxclip_finite(box) { return []; }
    if !(width > 0.0 && width - width == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(height > 0.0 && height - height == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = boxclip_compute(box, width, height);
    if !boxclip_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn osprey_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn osprey_compute(pred: vector, truth: vector, width: f64, height: f64, threshold: f64) -> vector {
    let pbox = boxclip_inside(pred, width, height);
    let tbox = boxclip_inside(truth, width, height);
    let scores = boxoverlap_measure(pbox, tbox);
    if len(scores) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut matched = 0;
    if at(scores, 0) > 0.0 && at(scores, 2) >= threshold {
        matched = 1;
    }
    [at(scores, 2), matched, at(scores, 0)]
}

// Score a detection against a reference after clipping both to the camera frame.
// Returns [visible IoU, matched, visible intersection area]. Match requires positive overlap and a score at least equal to the threshold.
pub fn osprey_compare(pred: vector, truth: vector, width: f64, height: f64, threshold: f64) -> vector {
    if !osprey_finite(pred) { return []; }
    if !osprey_finite(truth) { return []; }
    if !(width > 0.0 && width - width == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(height > 0.0 && height - height == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(threshold >= 0.0 && threshold <= 1.0) { return []; }
    let result = osprey_compute(pred, truth, width, height, threshold);
    if !osprey_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let pred = [-2, 0, 2, 2];
    let truth = [0, 0, 4, 2];
    let width = 4.0;
    let height = 4.0;
    let threshold = 0.5;
    let result = osprey_compare(pred, truth, width, height, threshold);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0.5
1
4
```

#### Practice

Change pred = [0, 0, 1, 1], truth = [1, 0, 2, 1], threshold = 0.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [visible IoU, matched, visible intersection area]. Match requires positive overlap and a score at least equal to the threshold.

Solution

The result vector is [0, 0, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let pred = [-2, 0, 2, 2];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let pred = [0, 0, 1, 1];
```

Find

```blyx
    let truth = [0, 0, 4, 2];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let truth = [1, 0, 2, 1];
```

Find

```blyx
    let threshold = 0.5;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let threshold = 0.0;
```

Output after the change

```
0
0
0
```

### [Warbler · Distinguish a clipped transient from a sustained overload](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/warbler)

Flag sustained clipping while reporting the energy of an audio frame.

#### Distinguish a clipped transient from a sustained overload

Identical peak readings can represent a single transient or a sustained overload. Inspect run length alongside frame energy. Two adjacent full-scale samples breach the one-sample allowance. Separating them with silence changes the alert.

[librosa, frame energy](https://librosa.org/doc/0.11.0/generated/librosa.feature.rms.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.1 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-warbler.git
cd blyx-warbler
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "1,-1,0,0" 1 1
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-warbler/blob/v0.1.1/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [peak, mean square, longest clipped run, alert]. Alert means the longest run exceeded the allowed number of samples. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| samples | Vector of: finite number |
| ceiling | positive finite number |
| allowed | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[FrameSignal](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/framesignal) · [ClipRuns](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/clipruns) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/warbler)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Warbler 0.1.1 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-warbler/tree/v0.1.1

fn framesignal_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn framesignal_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn framesignal_num(value: i64) -> f64 {
    at([value], 0)
}

fn framesignal_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn framesignal_compute(samples: vector) -> vector {
    if len(samples) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut peak = 0.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(samples) {
        peak = framesignal_max2(peak, framesignal_absolute(at(samples, i)));
        i += 1;
    }
    [peak, dot(samples, samples) / framesignal_num(len(samples))]
}

// Measure peak amplitude and mean-square energy of a signal frame.
// Returns [peak absolute amplitude, mean square]. Empty frames are invalid. Supply amplitudes in a common linear scale.
pub fn framesignal_level(samples: vector) -> vector {
    if !framesignal_finite(samples) { return []; }
    let result = framesignal_compute(samples);
    if !framesignal_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn clipruns_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn clipruns_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn clipruns_compute(samples: vector, ceiling: f64) -> vector {
    let mut total = 0;
    let mut run = 0;
    let mut longest = 0;
    let mut runs = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(samples) {
        if clipruns_absolute(at(samples, i)) >= ceiling {
            if run == 0 {
                runs += 1;
            }
            run += 1;
            total += 1;
            if run > longest {
                longest = run;
            }
        } else {
            run = 0;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [total, longest, runs]
}

// Count overloaded samples and the longest continuous run.
// Returns [samples at or above the absolute ceiling, longest run, run count]. Equality counts as a clipped sample.
pub fn clipruns_count(samples: vector, ceiling: f64) -> vector {
    if !clipruns_finite(samples) { return []; }
    if !(ceiling > 0.0 && ceiling - ceiling == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = clipruns_compute(samples, ceiling);
    if !clipruns_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn warbler_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn warbler_compute(samples: vector, ceiling: f64, allowed: f64) -> vector {
    let signal = framesignal_level(samples);
    let clips = clipruns_count(samples, ceiling);
    if len(signal) == 0 || len(clips) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut alert = 0;
    if at(clips, 1) > allowed {
        alert = 1;
    }
    [at(signal, 0), at(signal, 1), at(clips, 1), alert]
}

// Flag sustained clipping while reporting the energy of an audio frame.
// Returns [peak, mean square, longest clipped run, alert]. Alert means the longest run exceeded the allowed number of samples.
pub fn warbler_meter(samples: vector, ceiling: f64, allowed: f64) -> vector {
    if !warbler_finite(samples) { return []; }
    if !(ceiling > 0.0 && ceiling - ceiling == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(allowed >= 0.0 && allowed <= 9007199254740991.0 && allowed % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = warbler_compute(samples, ceiling, allowed);
    if !warbler_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let samples = [1, -1, 0, 0];
    let ceiling = 1.0;
    let allowed = 1.0;
    let result = warbler_meter(samples, ceiling, allowed);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
1
0.5
2
1
```

#### Practice

Change samples = [1, 0, -1, 0]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [peak, mean square, longest clipped run, alert]. Alert means the longest run exceeded the allowed number of samples.

Solution

The result vector is [1, 0.5, 1, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let samples = [1, -1, 0, 0];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let samples = [1, 0, -1, 0];
```

Output after the change

```
1
0.5
1
0
```

### [Linnet · Bridge short pauses in a speech-activity trace](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/linnet)

Summarize speech-activity intervals from a precomputed frame-level envelope.

#### Bridge short pauses in a speech-activity trace

A brief pause inside an utterance can split a segment. Accept a caller-selected gap and preserve the original time axis. With ten milliseconds per frame, a one-frame gap stays inside a segment. A two-frame gap starts another segment.

[librosa, splitting a signal into active intervals](https://librosa.org/doc/0.11.0/generated/librosa.effects.split.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.1 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-linnet.git
cd blyx-linnet
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0,3,0,3,0,0,3" 1 1 10
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-linnet/blob/v0.1.1/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [first active millisecond, exclusive active end, segment count, retained active-or-bridged milliseconds]. A silent trace returns [-1,-1,0,0]. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| levels | Vector of: nonnegative finite number |
| threshold | nonnegative finite number |
| gap | nonnegative exact integer |
| frame_ms | positive finite number |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[ActivitySpan](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/activityspan) · [GapHold](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/gaphold) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/linnet)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Linnet 0.1.1 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-linnet/tree/v0.1.1

fn activityspan_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn activityspan_magnitudes(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn activityspan_compute(levels: vector, threshold: f64) -> vector {
    let mut first = -1;
    let mut end = -1;
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(levels) {
        if at(levels, i) > threshold {
            if first < 0 {
                first = i;
            }
            end = i + 1;
            count += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [first, end, count]
}

// Locate active frames in a sequence of nonnegative signal levels.
// Returns [first active index, exclusive final active index, active frames]. Silence returns [-1,-1,0]. Activity is strictly above threshold.
pub fn activityspan_bounds(levels: vector, threshold: f64) -> vector {
    if !activityspan_magnitudes(levels) { return []; }
    if !(threshold >= 0.0 && threshold - threshold == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = activityspan_compute(levels, threshold);
    if !activityspan_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn gaphold_num(value: i64) -> f64 {
    at([value], 0)
}

fn gaphold_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn gaphold_magnitudes(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn gaphold_compute(levels: vector, threshold: f64, gap: f64) -> vector {
    let mut last = -1;
    let mut segments = 0;
    let mut bridged = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(levels) {
        if at(levels, i) > threshold {
            let silent = i - last - 1;
            if last < 0 || gaphold_num(silent) > gap {
                segments += 1;
            } else {
                bridged += silent;
            }
            last = i;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [segments, bridged]
}

// Count activity segments while bridging short internal silences.
// Returns [segments, bridged silent frames]. Leading and trailing silence are excluded. A gap exactly equal to the allowance is bridged.
pub fn gaphold_segments(levels: vector, threshold: f64, gap: f64) -> vector {
    if !gaphold_magnitudes(levels) { return []; }
    if !(threshold >= 0.0 && threshold - threshold == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(gap >= 0.0 && gap <= 9007199254740991.0 && gap % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = gaphold_compute(levels, threshold, gap);
    if !gaphold_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn linnet_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn linnet_magnitudes(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn linnet_compute(levels: vector, threshold: f64, gap: f64, frame_ms: f64) -> vector {
    let span = activityspan_bounds(levels, threshold);
    let segments = gaphold_segments(levels, threshold, gap);
    if len(span) == 0 || len(segments) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    if at(span, 0) < 0.0 {
        return [-1, -1, 0, 0];
    }
    [at(span, 0) * frame_ms, at(span, 1) * frame_ms, at(segments, 0), (at(span, 2) + at(segments, 1)) * frame_ms]
}

// Summarize speech-activity intervals from a precomputed frame-level envelope.
// Returns [first active millisecond, exclusive active end, segment count, retained active-or-bridged milliseconds]. A silent trace returns [-1,-1,0,0].
pub fn linnet_segment(levels: vector, threshold: f64, gap: f64, frame_ms: f64) -> vector {
    if !linnet_magnitudes(levels) { return []; }
    if !(threshold >= 0.0 && threshold - threshold == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(gap >= 0.0 && gap <= 9007199254740991.0 && gap % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(frame_ms > 0.0 && frame_ms - frame_ms == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = linnet_compute(levels, threshold, gap, frame_ms);
    if !linnet_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let levels = [0, 3, 0, 3, 0, 0, 3];
    let threshold = 1.0;
    let gap = 1.0;
    let frame_ms = 10.0;
    let result = linnet_segment(levels, threshold, gap, frame_ms);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
10
70
2
40
```

#### Practice

Change levels = [0, 0], gap = 2.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [first active millisecond, exclusive active end, segment count, retained active-or-bridged milliseconds]. A silent trace returns [-1,-1,0,0].

Solution

The result vector is [-1, -1, 0, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx

```

Replace with

```blyx
    let levels = [0, 0];
```

Find

```blyx
    let gap = 1.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let gap = 2.0;
```

```
0
0
```

### [Curlew · Cover a survey that crosses a grid origin](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/curlew)

Plan grid tiles covering every observation in a projected point survey.

#### Cover a survey that crosses a grid origin

Truncating a negative coordinate toward zero puts a survey point in the wrong tile. Include both extrema and use mathematical floor. A point at east -1 lies in column -1 with two-unit cells. Both end tiles count toward the coverage area.

[Shapely, geometry bounds](https://shapely.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/shapely.bounds.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-curlew.git
cd blyx-curlew
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "-1,4" "1,3" 2
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-curlew/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [first column, first row, last column, last row, tile count]. Both bounds are inclusive; coordinates must already use the same projected CRS. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| east | Vector of: finite number |
| north | Vector of: finite number |
| cell | positive finite number |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[GeoBounds](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/geobounds) · [GridCover](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/gridcover) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/curlew)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Curlew 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-curlew/tree/v0.1.0

fn geobounds_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn geobounds_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn geobounds_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn geobounds_compute(east: vector, north: vector) -> vector {
    if len(east) == 0 || len(east) != len(north) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut west = at(east, 0);
    let mut right = west;
    let mut south = at(north, 0);
    let mut top = south;
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(east) {
        west = geobounds_min2(west, at(east, i));
        right = geobounds_max2(right, at(east, i));
        south = geobounds_min2(south, at(north, i));
        top = geobounds_max2(top, at(north, i));
        i += 1;
    }
    [west, south, right, top]
}

// Find a projected planar extent from paired point coordinates.
// Returns [west, south, east, north]. A single point has a zero-area extent. Supply a common planar CRS for both axes.
pub fn geobounds_extent(east: vector, north: vector) -> vector {
    if !geobounds_finite(east) { return []; }
    if !geobounds_finite(north) { return []; }
    let result = geobounds_compute(east, north);
    if !geobounds_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn gridcover_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn gridcover_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn gridcover_floorreal(value: f64) -> f64 {
    let trunc = value - value % 1.0;
    if trunc > value {
        return trunc - 1.0;
    }
    trunc
}

fn gridcover_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn gridcover_compute(box: vector, cell: f64) -> vector {
    if len(box) != 4 || at(box, 0) > at(box, 2) || at(box, 1) > at(box, 3) {
        return [];
    }
    let a = at(box, 0) / cell;
    let b = at(box, 1) / cell;
    let c = at(box, 2) / cell;
    let d = at(box, 3) / cell;
    if gridcover_max2(gridcover_max2(gridcover_absolute(a), gridcover_absolute(b)), gridcover_max2(gridcover_absolute(c), gridcover_absolute(d))) > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    [gridcover_floorreal(a), gridcover_floorreal(b), gridcover_floorreal(c), gridcover_floorreal(d)]
}

// Find grid indices containing both extrema of a closed planar extent.
// Returns [min column, min row, max column, max row]. Grid origin is (0,0); exact upper-boundary points belong to the next cell.
pub fn gridcover_cells(box: vector, cell: f64) -> vector {
    if !gridcover_finite(box) { return []; }
    if !(cell > 0.0 && cell - cell == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = gridcover_compute(box, cell);
    if !gridcover_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn curlew_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn curlew_compute(east: vector, north: vector, cell: f64) -> vector {
    let box = geobounds_extent(east, north);
    let cells = gridcover_cells(box, cell);
    if len(cells) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let count = (at(cells, 2) - at(cells, 0) + 1.0) * (at(cells, 3) - at(cells, 1) + 1.0);
    if count > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(cells, 0), at(cells, 1), at(cells, 2), at(cells, 3), count]
}

// Plan grid tiles covering every observation in a projected point survey.
// Returns [first column, first row, last column, last row, tile count]. Both bounds are inclusive; coordinates must already use the same projected CRS.
pub fn curlew_tile(east: vector, north: vector, cell: f64) -> vector {
    if !curlew_finite(east) { return []; }
    if !curlew_finite(north) { return []; }
    if !(cell > 0.0 && cell - cell == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = curlew_compute(east, north, cell);
    if !curlew_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let east = [-1, 4];
    let north = [1, 3];
    let cell = 2.0;
    let result = curlew_tile(east, north, cell);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
-1
0
2
1
8
```

#### Practice

Change east = [0], north = [0], cell = 1.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [first column, first row, last column, last row, tile count]. Both bounds are inclusive; coordinates must already use the same projected CRS.

Solution

The result vector is [0, 0, 0, 0, 1]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let east = [-1, 4];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let east = [0];
```

Find

```blyx
    let north = [1, 3];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let north = [0];
```

Find

```blyx
    let cell = 2.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let cell = 1.0;
```

Output after the change

```
0
0
0
0
1
```

### [Egret · Compare abundance and diversity in a field survey](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/egret)

Summarize richness, singletons and dominance in an ecological field survey.

#### Compare abundance and diversity in a field survey

Two surveys can have the same species count and very different abundance patterns. Report diversity alongside observed richness. Two equally abundant taxa give Simpson dominance 0.5 and an effective count of two.

[scikit-bio, Simpson dominance](https://scikit.bio/docs/latest/generated/skbio.diversity.alpha.dominance.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-egret.git
cd blyx-egret
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "2,0,2"
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-egret/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [individuals, observed taxa, singletons, dominance, effective taxa]. An entirely empty survey has no diversity estimate. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| counts | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[Richness](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/richness) · [Dominance](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/dominance) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/egret)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Egret 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-egret/tree/v0.1.0

fn richness_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn richness_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn richness_compute(counts: vector) -> vector {
    let mut taxa = 0;
    let mut singles = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(counts) {
        let x = at(counts, i);
        if x > 0.0 {
            taxa += 1;
        }
        if x == 1.0 {
            singles += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    let total = sum(counts);
    if total > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    [taxa, singles, total]
}

// Count observed taxa and singletons from an abundance vector.
// Returns [observed taxa, singletons, individuals]. Zero-count categories do not increase richness.
pub fn richness_observe(counts: vector) -> vector {
    if !richness_counts(counts) { return []; }
    let result = richness_compute(counts);
    if !richness_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn dominance_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn dominance_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn dominance_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn dominance_compute(counts: vector) -> vector {
    let total = sum(counts);
    if total == 0.0 || total > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut concentration = 0.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(counts) {
        let share = at(counts, i) / total;
        concentration += share * share;
        i += 1;
    }
    [concentration, dominance_max2(0.0, 1.0 - concentration)]
}

// Compute Simpson dominance and its complement from abundance counts.
// Returns [sum of squared relative abundances, Gini–Simpson diversity]. Uses sampling with replacement. Empty surveys have no proportions.
pub fn dominance_simpson(counts: vector) -> vector {
    if !dominance_counts(counts) { return []; }
    let result = dominance_compute(counts);
    if !dominance_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn egret_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn egret_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn egret_compute(counts: vector) -> vector {
    let detail = richness_observe(counts);
    let conc = dominance_simpson(counts);
    if len(detail) == 0 || len(conc) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(detail, 2), at(detail, 0), at(detail, 1), at(conc, 0), 1.0 / at(conc, 0)]
}

// Summarize richness, singletons and dominance in an ecological field survey.
// Returns [individuals, observed taxa, singletons, dominance, effective taxa]. An entirely empty survey has no diversity estimate.
pub fn egret_survey(counts: vector) -> vector {
    if !egret_counts(counts) { return []; }
    let result = egret_compute(counts);
    if !egret_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let counts = [2, 0, 2];
    let result = egret_survey(counts);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
4
2
0
0.5
2
```

#### Practice

Change counts = [1]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [individuals, observed taxa, singletons, dominance, effective taxa]. An entirely empty survey has no diversity estimate.

Solution

The result vector is [1, 1, 1, 1, 1]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let counts = [2, 0, 2];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let counts = [1];
```

Output after the change

```
1
1
1
1
1
```

### [Tanager · Audit a directed graph export](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/tanager)

Audit a directed edge list before interpreting a vertex's degree.

#### Audit a directed graph export

Duplicated edge rows and loops change degree in a multigraph. Surface those counts before downstream graph analysis. A duplicate edge inflates degree and a self-loop contributes to both directions. The simple-graph flag records either condition.

[NetworkX, graph degree](https://networkx.org/documentation/stable/reference/classes/generated/networkx.Graph.degree.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-tanager.git
cd blyx-tanager
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "1,1,2" "2,2,2" 2
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-tanager/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [incoming, outgoing, graph-wide duplicate edges, graph-wide loops, simple graph flag]. Duplicate detection uses quadratic time for short edge lists. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| starts | Vector of: exact signed integer |
| ends | Vector of: exact signed integer |
| node | exact signed integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[GraphDegree](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/graphdegree) · [EdgeAudit](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/edgeaudit) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/tanager)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Tanager 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-tanager/tree/v0.1.0

fn graphdegree_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn graphdegree_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn graphdegree_compute(starts: vector, ends: vector, node: f64) -> vector {
    if len(starts) != len(ends) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut incoming = 0;
    let mut outgoing = 0;
    let mut loops = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(starts) {
        if at(starts, i) == node {
            outgoing += 1;
        }
        if at(ends, i) == node {
            incoming += 1;
        }
        if at(starts, i) == node && at(ends, i) == node {
            loops += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [incoming, outgoing, loops]
}

// Count incoming and outgoing edges at a named numeric vertex.
// Returns [incoming, outgoing, incident self-loops] for a directed multigraph. Each loop adds one to each direction.
pub fn graphdegree_at_node(starts: vector, ends: vector, node: f64) -> vector {
    if !graphdegree_integers(starts) { return []; }
    if !graphdegree_integers(ends) { return []; }
    if !(node >= -9007199254740991.0 && node <= 9007199254740991.0 && node % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = graphdegree_compute(starts, ends, node);
    if !graphdegree_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn edgeaudit_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn edgeaudit_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn edgeaudit_compute(starts: vector, ends: vector) -> vector {
    if len(starts) != len(ends) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut dup = 0;
    let mut loops = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(starts) {
        if at(starts, i) == at(ends, i) {
            loops += 1;
        }
        let mut j = 0;
        while j < i {
            if at(starts, i) == at(starts, j) && at(ends, i) == at(ends, j) {
                dup += 1;
                break;
            }
            j += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [dup, loops, len(starts) - dup]
}

// Audit exact repeated directed edges and self-loops.
// Returns [duplicate occurrences beyond the first, self-loop occurrences, unique directed edges]. Reversed edges are distinct.
pub fn edgeaudit_duplicates(starts: vector, ends: vector) -> vector {
    if !edgeaudit_integers(starts) { return []; }
    if !edgeaudit_integers(ends) { return []; }
    let result = edgeaudit_compute(starts, ends);
    if !edgeaudit_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn tanager_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn tanager_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn tanager_compute(starts: vector, ends: vector, node: f64) -> vector {
    let degree = graphdegree_at_node(starts, ends, node);
    let audit = edgeaudit_duplicates(starts, ends);
    if len(degree) == 0 || len(audit) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut simple = 0;
    if at(audit, 0) == 0.0 && at(audit, 1) == 0.0 {
        simple = 1;
    }
    [at(degree, 0), at(degree, 1), at(audit, 0), at(audit, 1), simple]
}

// Audit a directed edge list before interpreting a vertex's degree.
// Returns [incoming, outgoing, graph-wide duplicate edges, graph-wide loops, simple graph flag]. Duplicate detection uses quadratic time for short edge lists.
pub fn tanager_inspect(starts: vector, ends: vector, node: f64) -> vector {
    if !tanager_integers(starts) { return []; }
    if !tanager_integers(ends) { return []; }
    if !(node >= -9007199254740991.0 && node <= 9007199254740991.0 && node % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = tanager_compute(starts, ends, node);
    if !tanager_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let starts = [1, 1, 2];
    let ends = [2, 2, 2];
    let node = 2.0;
    let result = tanager_inspect(starts, ends, node);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
3
1
1
1
0
```

#### Practice

Change starts = [1, 2], ends = [2, 1], node = 1.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [incoming, outgoing, graph-wide duplicate edges, graph-wide loops, simple graph flag]. Duplicate detection uses quadratic time for short edge lists.

Solution

The result vector is [1, 1, 0, 0, 1]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find


### [Merganser · Measure a loss that recovered before the final observation](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/merganser)

Report drawdown depth and time below the running peak for a historical series.

#### Measure a loss that recovered before the final observation

A recovered account can finish near its starting value while hiding a long underwater spell. Keep depth and duration visible together. The sample falls from 100 to 75 and recovers. Its depth meets the limit but its time below peak exceeds the duration limit.

[QuantConnect, backtest reports](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/lean-cli/reports)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-merganser.git
cd blyx-merganser
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "100,80,75,100" 0.25 1
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-merganser/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [deepest fractional loss, peak index, trough index, longest underwater spell, limit breached]. Durations count observations, not calendar days. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| equity | Vector of: positive finite number |
| depth_limit | probability in [0,1] |
| duration_limit | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[DrawDepth](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/drawdepth) · [UnderWater](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/underwater) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/merganser)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Merganser 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-merganser/tree/v0.1.0

fn drawdepth_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn drawdepth_positive(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value > 0.0 && value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn drawdepth_compute(equity: vector) -> vector {
    if len(equity) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut high = at(equity, 0);
    let mut peak = 0;
    let mut best = 0.0;
    let mut start = 0;
    let mut bottom = 0;
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(equity) {
        let x = at(equity, i);
        if x >= high {
            high = x;
            peak = i;
        } else {
            let depth = 1.0 - x / high;
            if depth > best {
                best = depth;
                start = peak;
                bottom = i;
            }
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [best, start, bottom]
}

// Measure the deepest historical peak-to-trough equity decline.
// Returns [maximum fractional drawdown, peak index, trough index]. Uses the first trough at the maximum and the most recent equal peak.
pub fn drawdepth_deepest(equity: vector) -> vector {
    if !drawdepth_positive(equity) { return []; }
    let result = drawdepth_compute(equity);
    if !drawdepth_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn underwater_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn underwater_positive(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value > 0.0 && value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn underwater_compute(equity: vector) -> vector {
    if len(equity) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut high = at(equity, 0);
    let mut run = 0;
    let mut longest = 0;
    let mut recover = 0;
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(equity) {
        let x = at(equity, i);
        if x >= high {
            run = 0;
            high = x;
            recover = i;
        } else {
            run += 1;
            if run > longest {
                longest = run;
            }
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [longest, run, recover]
}

// Measure how long an equity series stayed below its running peak.
// Returns [longest consecutive underwater observations, current run, last recovered index]. A return exactly to the prior peak ends a run.
pub fn underwater_duration(equity: vector) -> vector {
    if !underwater_positive(equity) { return []; }
    let result = underwater_compute(equity);
    if !underwater_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn merganser_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn merganser_positive(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value > 0.0 && value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn merganser_compute(equity: vector, depth_limit: f64, duration_limit: f64) -> vector {
    let depth = drawdepth_deepest(equity);
    let time = underwater_duration(equity);
    if len(depth) == 0 || len(time) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut flag = 0;
    if at(depth, 0) > depth_limit || at(time, 0) > duration_limit {
        flag = 1;
    }
    [at(depth, 0), at(depth, 1), at(depth, 2), at(time, 0), flag]
}

// Report drawdown depth and time below the running peak for a historical series.
// Returns [deepest fractional loss, peak index, trough index, longest underwater spell, limit breached]. Durations count observations, not calendar days.
pub fn merganser_report(equity: vector, depth_limit: f64, duration_limit: f64) -> vector {
    if !merganser_positive(equity) { return []; }
    if !(depth_limit >= 0.0 && depth_limit <= 1.0) { return []; }
    if !(duration_limit >= 0.0 && duration_limit <= 9007199254740991.0 && duration_limit % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = merganser_compute(equity, depth_limit, duration_limit);
    if !merganser_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let equity = [100, 80, 75, 100];
    let depth_limit = 0.25;
    let duration_limit = 1.0;
    let result = merganser_report(equity, depth_limit, duration_limit);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0.25
0
2
2
1
```

#### Practice

Change equity = [4, 2, 4], depth_limit = 0.5. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [deepest fractional loss, peak index, trough index, longest underwater spell, limit breached]. Durations count observations, not calendar days.

Solution

The result vector is [0.5, 0, 1, 1, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx

```

Replace with

```blyx
    let equity = [4, 2, 4];
```

Find

```blyx
    let depth_limit = 0.25;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let depth_limit = 0.5;
```

Output after the change

```

0
1
1
0
```

### [Pintail · Measure turnover between two weight snapshots](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/pintail)

Compare long-only portfolio snapshots under a one-way turnover budget.

#### Measure turnover between two weight snapshots

Netting buys against sells can hide turnover in an allocation comparison. Keep gross directional changes and the one-way budget explicit. Moving a quarter of the portfolio between two assets requires 0.25 one-way turnover. A 0.125 cap leaves 0.125 excess.

[Cvxportfolio, turnover constraints](https://www.cvxportfolio.com/en/1.2.0/constraints.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-pintail.git
cd blyx-pintail
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0.75,0.25" "0.5,0.5" 0.125
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-pintail/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [largest drift index, absolute asset drift, one-way turnover, excess over the budget]. Inputs are aligned historical or hypothetical weights, including cash if applicable. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| current | Vector of: probability in [0,1] |
| target | Vector of: probability in [0,1] |
| turnover_cap | probability in [0,1] |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[WeightDrift](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/weightdrift) · [Turnover](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/turnover) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/pintail)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Pintail 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-pintail/tree/v0.1.0

fn weightdrift_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn weightdrift_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn weightdrift_probabilities(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 1.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn weightdrift_compute(current: vector, target: vector) -> vector {
    if len(current) == 0 || len(current) != len(target) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut winner = 0;
    let mut delta = at(current, 0) - at(target, 0);
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(current) {
        let d = at(current, i) - at(target, i);
        if weightdrift_absolute(d) > weightdrift_absolute(delta) {
            winner = i;
            delta = d;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [winner, delta, weightdrift_absolute(delta)]
}

// Find the largest per-asset deviation between two weight vectors.
// Returns [index, signed current minus target weight, absolute deviation]. First index wins an absolute tie.
pub fn weightdrift_largest(current: vector, target: vector) -> vector {
    if !weightdrift_probabilities(current) { return []; }
    if !weightdrift_probabilities(target) { return []; }
    let result = weightdrift_compute(current, target);
    if !weightdrift_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn turnover_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn turnover_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn turnover_probabilities(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 1.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn turnover_compute(current: vector, target: vector) -> vector {
    if len(current) != len(target) || turnover_absolute(sum(current) - 1.0) > 0.000000001 || turnover_absolute(sum(target) - 1.0) > 0.000000001 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut buys = 0.0;
    let mut sells = 0.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(current) {
        let d = at(target, i) - at(current, i);
        if d > 0.0 {
            buys += d;
        } else {
            sells -= d;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [(buys + sells) / 2.0, buys, sells]
}

// Calculate one-way turnover for two fully allocated long-only weight vectors.
// Returns [one-way turnover, total weight increases, total weight decreases]. Each portfolio must sum to one within 1e-9.
pub fn turnover_one_way(current: vector, target: vector) -> vector {
    if !turnover_probabilities(current) { return []; }
    if !turnover_probabilities(target) { return []; }
    let result = turnover_compute(current, target);
    if !turnover_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn pintail_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn pintail_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn pintail_probabilities(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 1.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn pintail_compute(current: vector, target: vector, turnover_cap: f64) -> vector {
    let drift = weightdrift_largest(current, target);
    let trades = turnover_one_way(current, target);
    if len(drift) == 0 || len(trades) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(drift, 0), at(drift, 2), at(trades, 0), pintail_max2(0.0, at(trades, 0) - turnover_cap)]
}

// Compare long-only portfolio snapshots under a one-way turnover budget.
// Returns [largest drift index, absolute asset drift, one-way turnover, excess over the budget]. Inputs are aligned historical or hypothetical weights, including cash if applicable.
pub fn pintail_compare(current: vector, target: vector, turnover_cap: f64) -> vector {
    if !pintail_probabilities(current) { return []; }
    if !pintail_probabilities(target) { return []; }
    if !(turnover_cap >= 0.0 && turnover_cap <= 1.0) { return []; }
    let result = pintail_compute(current, target, turnover_cap);
    if !pintail_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let current = [0.75, 0.25];
    let target = [0.5, 0.5];
    let turnover_cap = 0.125;
    let result = pintail_compare(current, target, turnover_cap);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0
0.25
0.25
0.125
```

#### Practice

Hint

Returns [largest drift index, absolute asset drift, one-way turnover, excess over the budget]. Inputs are aligned historical or hypothetical weights, including cash if applicable.

Solution

The result vector is [0, 0, 0, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx

```

Replace with

```blyx
    let current = [1];
```

Find

```blyx
    let target = [0.5, 0.5];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let target = [1];
```

Find

```blyx
    let turnover_cap = 0.125;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let turnover_cap = 0.0;
```

```
0
0
0
0
```

### [Siskin · Find a funding gap inside an otherwise positive cash schedule](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/siskin)

Inspect a cash-flow schedule for shortfalls that disappear by the closing date.

#### Find a funding gap inside an otherwise positive cash schedule

A positive closing balance can conceal a mid-period reserve breach. Replay the signed flows in order. The closing balance is 25, but two period ends fall below the reserve and the worst gap is 15.

[GnuCash, cash flow reporting](https://www.gnucash.org/docs/v5/C/gnucash-manual/report-classes.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-siskin.git
cd blyx-siskin
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 20 "-15,-10,30" 10
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-siskin/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [closing balance, low-water balance, first deficient period, deficient periods, period-end funding gap]. Flows must be in date order. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| opening | exact signed integer |
| flows | Vector of: exact signed integer |
| reserve | exact signed integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[CashLadder](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/cashladder) · [FloorBreach](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/floorbreach) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/siskin)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Siskin 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-siskin/tree/v0.1.0

fn cashladder_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn cashladder_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn cashladder_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn cashladder_compute(opening: f64, flows: vector) -> vector {
    let mut cash = opening;
    let mut low = cash;
    let mut idx = -1;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(flows) {
        cash += at(flows, i);
        if cashladder_absolute(cash) > 9007199254740991.0 {
            return [];
        }
        if cash < low {
            low = cash;
            idx = i;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [cash, low, idx]
}

// Find closing and lowest balances along an ordered cash-flow schedule.
// Returns [closing, lowest balance including opening, first low index]. Opening uses index -1. Use a single currency's minor units.
pub fn cashladder_balance(opening: f64, flows: vector) -> vector {
    if !(opening >= -9007199254740991.0 && opening <= 9007199254740991.0 && opening % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !cashladder_integers(flows) { return []; }
    let result = cashladder_compute(opening, flows);
    if !cashladder_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn floorbreach_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn floorbreach_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn floorbreach_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn floorbreach_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn floorbreach_compute(opening: f64, flows: vector, reserve: f64) -> vector {
    let mut cash = opening;
    let mut first = -1;
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut gap = 0.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(flows) {
        cash += at(flows, i);
        if floorbreach_absolute(cash) > 9007199254740991.0 {
            return [];
        }
        if cash < reserve {
            if first < 0 {
                first = i;
            }
            count += 1;
            gap = floorbreach_max2(gap, reserve - cash);
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [first, count, gap]
}

// Locate the first reserve breach and count all deficient period ends.
// Returns [first deficient period, deficient periods, largest shortfall]. The opening balance initializes the trace; only period ends are counted.
pub fn floorbreach_trace(opening: f64, flows: vector, reserve: f64) -> vector {
    if !(opening >= -9007199254740991.0 && opening <= 9007199254740991.0 && opening % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !floorbreach_integers(flows) { return []; }
    if !(reserve >= -9007199254740991.0 && reserve <= 9007199254740991.0 && reserve % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = floorbreach_compute(opening, flows, reserve);
    if !floorbreach_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn siskin_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn siskin_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn siskin_compute(opening: f64, flows: vector, reserve: f64) -> vector {
    let ladder = cashladder_balance(opening, flows);
    let risk = floorbreach_trace(opening, flows, reserve);
    if len(ladder) == 0 || len(risk) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(ladder, 0), at(ladder, 1), at(risk, 0), at(risk, 1), at(risk, 2)]
}

// Inspect a cash-flow schedule for shortfalls that disappear by the closing date.
// Returns [closing balance, low-water balance, first deficient period, deficient periods, period-end funding gap]. Flows must be in date order.
pub fn siskin_project(opening: f64, flows: vector, reserve: f64) -> vector {
    if !(opening >= -9007199254740991.0 && opening <= 9007199254740991.0 && opening % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !siskin_integers(flows) { return []; }
    if !(reserve >= -9007199254740991.0 && reserve <= 9007199254740991.0 && reserve % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = siskin_compute(opening, flows, reserve);
    if !siskin_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let opening = 20.0;
    let flows = [-15, -10, 30];
    let reserve = 10.0;
    let result = siskin_project(opening, flows, reserve);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
-5
0
2
15
```

Returns [closing balance, low-water balance, first deficient period, deficient periods, period-end funding gap]. Flows must be in date order.

Solution

The result vector is [10, 0, -1, 0, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.


