### [Sandpiper · Schedule redelivery after a lease expires](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/sandpiper)

Schedule a deterministic redelivery after both lease expiry and retry backoff.

#### Schedule redelivery after a lease expires

Redelivery before a worker's lease expires can duplicate work. Make retry time depend on both the lease and the attempt count. The eight-tick lease ends at tick 18. A four-tick backoff makes tick 22 the earliest eligible retry.

[Amazon SQS, visibility timeout](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-visibility-timeout.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-sandpiper.git
cd blyx-sandpiper
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 10 8 19 2 16 1
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-sandpiper/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [ready, ticks to eligibility, retry delay]. Delay begins when the lease expires. The queue host owns acknowledgement and delivery. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| issued | nonnegative exact integer |
| ttl | positive exact integer |
| now | nonnegative exact integer |
| base | positive exact integer |
| ceiling | positive exact integer |
| attempt | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[LeaseClock](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/leaseclock) · [RetryDelay](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/retrydelay) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/sandpiper)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Sandpiper 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-sandpiper/tree/v0.1.0

fn leaseclock_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn leaseclock_compute(issued: f64, ttl: f64, now: f64) -> vector {
    if now < issued {
        return [];
    }
    let age = now - issued;
    if age < ttl {
        return [1, ttl - age, 0];
    }
    [0, 0, age - ttl]
}

// Classify a message lease against a single monotonic clock.
// Returns [active, remaining ticks, overdue ticks]. A lease expires exactly at its TTL; clocks earlier than issuance are invalid.
pub fn leaseclock_remaining(issued: f64, ttl: f64, now: f64) -> vector {
    if !(issued >= 0.0 && issued <= 9007199254740991.0 && issued % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(ttl >= 1.0 && ttl <= 9007199254740991.0 && ttl % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(now >= 0.0 && now <= 9007199254740991.0 && now % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = leaseclock_compute(issued, ttl, now);
    if !leaseclock_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn retrydelay_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn retrydelay_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn retrydelay_compute(base: f64, ceiling: f64, attempt: f64) -> vector {
    if ceiling < base {
        return [];
    }
    let mut delay = base;
    let mut i = 0.0;
    while i < attempt && delay < ceiling {
        delay = retrydelay_min2(ceiling, delay * 2.0);
        i += 1.0;
    }
    if delay == ceiling {
        return [delay, 1];
    }
    [delay, 0]
}

// Compute saturating exponential retry delays without unbounded exponentiation.
// Returns [delay ticks, cap reached]. Attempt zero uses the base. Ceilings below base are invalid.
pub fn retrydelay_capped(base: f64, ceiling: f64, attempt: f64) -> vector {
    if !(base >= 1.0 && base <= 9007199254740991.0 && base % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(ceiling >= 1.0 && ceiling <= 9007199254740991.0 && ceiling % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(attempt >= 0.0 && attempt <= 9007199254740991.0 && attempt % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = retrydelay_compute(base, ceiling, attempt);
    if !retrydelay_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn sandpiper_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn sandpiper_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn sandpiper_compute(issued: f64, ttl: f64, now: f64, base: f64, ceiling: f64, attempt: f64) -> vector {
    let clock = leaseclock_remaining(issued, ttl, now);
    let delay = retrydelay_capped(base, ceiling, attempt);
    if len(clock) == 0 || len(delay) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let wait = sandpiper_max2(0.0, at(clock, 1) + at(delay, 0) - at(clock, 2));
    if wait == 0.0 {
        return [1, 0, at(delay, 0)];
    }
    [0, wait, at(delay, 0)]
}

// Schedule a deterministic redelivery after both lease expiry and retry backoff.
// Returns [ready, ticks to eligibility, retry delay]. Delay begins when the lease expires. The queue host owns acknowledgement and delivery.
pub fn sandpiper_redeliver(issued: f64, ttl: f64, now: f64, base: f64, ceiling: f64, attempt: f64) -> vector {
    if !(issued >= 0.0 && issued <= 9007199254740991.0 && issued % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(ttl >= 1.0 && ttl <= 9007199254740991.0 && ttl % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(now >= 0.0 && now <= 9007199254740991.0 && now % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(base >= 1.0 && base <= 9007199254740991.0 && base % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(ceiling >= 1.0 && ceiling <= 9007199254740991.0 && ceiling % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(attempt >= 0.0 && attempt <= 9007199254740991.0 && attempt % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = sandpiper_compute(issued, ttl, now, base, ceiling, attempt);
    if !sandpiper_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let issued = 10.0;
    let ttl = 8.0;
    let now = 19.0;
    let base = 2.0;
    let ceiling = 16.0;
    let attempt = 1.0;
    let result = sandpiper_redeliver(issued, ttl, now, base, ceiling, attempt);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0
3
4
```

#### Practice

Change now = 22.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [ready, ticks to eligibility, retry delay]. Delay begins when the lease expires. The queue host owns acknowledgement and delivery.

Solution

The result vector is [1, 0, 4]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let now = 19.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let now = 22.0;
```

Output after the change

```
1
0
4
```

### [Petrel · Decide whether a queued request can afford to wait](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/petrel)

Admit an immediate charge or report the wait a request can afford.

#### Decide whether a queued request can afford to wait

Charging a delayed request immediately can remove capacity from unrelated work. Return the wait separately from the updated balance. The bucket has four tokens and needs eight. At two tokens per tick the charge fits the two-tick deadline.

[IETF RFC 2697, token buckets](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2697)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-petrel.git
cd blyx-petrel
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 2 10 2 1 8 2
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-petrel/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [charge now, balance after immediate decision, feasible by deadline, wait]. Deferred work consumes no tokens until resubmitted. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| tokens | nonnegative finite number |
| capacity | positive finite number |
| rate | positive finite number |
| elapsed | nonnegative finite number |
| cost | positive finite number |
| deadline | nonnegative finite number |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[TokenBucket](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/tokenbucket) · [WaitBudget](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/waitbudget) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/petrel)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Petrel 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-petrel/tree/v0.1.0

fn tokenbucket_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn tokenbucket_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn tokenbucket_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn tokenbucket_compute(tokens: f64, capacity: f64, rate: f64, elapsed: f64) -> vector {
    if tokens > capacity {
        return [];
    }
    let grown = tokens + rate * elapsed;
    [tokenbucket_min2(capacity, grown), tokenbucket_max2(0.0, grown - capacity)]
}

// Refill a rate bucket up to its burst capacity.
// Returns [available tokens, refill discarded at capacity]. Tokens, capacity and rate use the same work unit.
pub fn tokenbucket_refill(tokens: f64, capacity: f64, rate: f64, elapsed: f64) -> vector {
    if !(tokens >= 0.0 && tokens - tokens == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(capacity > 0.0 && capacity - capacity == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(rate > 0.0 && rate - rate == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(elapsed >= 0.0 && elapsed - elapsed == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = tokenbucket_compute(tokens, capacity, rate, elapsed);
    if !tokenbucket_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn waitbudget_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn waitbudget_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn waitbudget_compute(tokens: f64, capacity: f64, rate: f64, cost: f64, deadline: f64) -> vector {
    if tokens > capacity {
        return [];
    }
    if cost > capacity {
        return [0, -1];
    }
    let wait = waitbudget_max2(0.0, (cost - tokens) / rate);
    if wait <= deadline {
        return [1, wait];
    }
    [0, wait]
}

// Compute the wait required for a token charge within a relative deadline.
// Returns [admissible by deadline, required wait]. A charge above capacity has no feasible wait and returns [0,-1].
pub fn waitbudget_admit(tokens: f64, capacity: f64, rate: f64, cost: f64, deadline: f64) -> vector {
    if !(tokens >= 0.0 && tokens - tokens == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(capacity > 0.0 && capacity - capacity == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(rate > 0.0 && rate - rate == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(cost > 0.0 && cost - cost == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(deadline >= 0.0 && deadline - deadline == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = waitbudget_compute(tokens, capacity, rate, cost, deadline);
    if !waitbudget_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn petrel_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn petrel_compute(tokens: f64, capacity: f64, rate: f64, elapsed: f64, cost: f64, deadline: f64) -> vector {
    let bucket = tokenbucket_refill(tokens, capacity, rate, elapsed);
    if len(bucket) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let available = at(bucket, 0);
    let plan = waitbudget_admit(available, capacity, rate, cost, deadline);
    if len(plan) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    if at(plan, 1) == 0.0 {
        return [1, available - cost, 1, 0];
    }
    [0, available, at(plan, 0), at(plan, 1)]
}

// Admit an immediate charge or report the wait a request can afford.
// Returns [charge now, balance after immediate decision, feasible by deadline, wait]. Deferred work consumes no tokens until resubmitted.
pub fn petrel_admit(tokens: f64, capacity: f64, rate: f64, elapsed: f64, cost: f64, deadline: f64) -> vector {
    if !(tokens >= 0.0 && tokens - tokens == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(capacity > 0.0 && capacity - capacity == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(rate > 0.0 && rate - rate == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(elapsed >= 0.0 && elapsed - elapsed == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(cost > 0.0 && cost - cost == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(deadline >= 0.0 && deadline - deadline == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = petrel_compute(tokens, capacity, rate, elapsed, cost, deadline);
    if !petrel_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let tokens = 2.0;
    let capacity = 10.0;
    let rate = 2.0;
    let elapsed = 1.0;
    let cost = 8.0;
    let deadline = 2.0;
    let result = petrel_admit(tokens, capacity, rate, elapsed, cost, deadline);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0
4
1
2
```

#### Practice

Change elapsed = 4.0, deadline = 0.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [charge now, balance after immediate decision, feasible by deadline, wait]. Deferred work consumes no tokens until resubmitted.

Solution

The result vector is [1, 2, 1, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let elapsed = 1.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let elapsed = 4.0;
```

Find

```blyx
    let deadline = 2.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let deadline = 0.0;
```

Output after the change

```
1
2
1
0
```

### [Fulmar · Commit offsets without skipping unfinished deliveries](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/fulmar)

Choose a contiguous commit offset from an out-of-order delivery trace.

#### Commit offsets without skipping unfinished deliveries

Committing the largest acknowledged offset can skip a message that is still in flight. Advance only through a contiguous prefix. Acknowledging offsets 4 and 6 advances the cursor only to 5. Offset 6 can remain acknowledged until 5 completes.

[RabbitMQ, consumer acknowledgements](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/confirms)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-fulmar.git
cd blyx-fulmar
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "4,6,5,6" "4,6" 4
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-fulmar/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [next commit, observed gaps, stale deliveries, per-trace high water]. Acknowledgements at or beyond start must refer to delivered offsets in this trace. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| delivered | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| acked | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| start | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[OffsetGap](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/offsetgap) · [AckPrefix](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/ackprefix) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/fulmar)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Fulmar 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-fulmar/tree/v0.1.0

fn offsetgap_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn offsetgap_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn offsetgap_compute(offsets: vector, start: f64) -> vector {
    let mut next = start;
    let mut gaps = 0.0;
    let mut stale = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(offsets) {
        let x = at(offsets, i);
        if x < next {
            stale += 1;
        } else {
            gaps += x - next;
            if x == 9007199254740991.0 {
                return [];
            }
            next = x + 1.0;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [gaps, stale, next]
}

// Audit an ordered offset trace against an expected starting value.
// Returns [forward gaps counted at first observation, stale or replayed deliveries, next high-water offset]. Late arrivals do not erase earlier gaps.
pub fn offsetgap_scan(offsets: vector, start: f64) -> vector {
    if !offsetgap_counts(offsets) { return []; }
    if !(start >= 0.0 && start <= 9007199254740991.0 && start % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = offsetgap_compute(offsets, start);
    if !offsetgap_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn ackprefix_hasid(values: vector, key: f64) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        if at(values, i) == key {
            return true;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    false
}

fn ackprefix_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn ackprefix_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn ackprefix_compute(acked: vector, start: f64) -> vector {
    let mut next = start;
    while ackprefix_hasid(acked, next) {
        if next == 9007199254740991.0 {
            return [];
        }
        next += 1.0;
    }
    [next, next - start]
}

// Find the longest contiguous acknowledgement prefix in unordered deliveries.
// Returns [next unacknowledged offset, advanced count]. Duplicate acknowledgements never advance the cursor twice.
pub fn ackprefix_advance(acked: vector, start: f64) -> vector {
    if !ackprefix_counts(acked) { return []; }
    if !(start >= 0.0 && start <= 9007199254740991.0 && start % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = ackprefix_compute(acked, start);
    if !ackprefix_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn fulmar_hasid(values: vector, key: f64) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        if at(values, i) == key {
            return true;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    false
}

fn fulmar_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn fulmar_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn fulmar_compute(delivered: vector, acked: vector, start: f64) -> vector {
    let seen = offsetgap_scan(delivered, start);
    if len(seen) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(acked) {
        let key = at(acked, i);
        if key >= start && !fulmar_hasid(delivered, key) {
            return [];
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    let prefix = ackprefix_advance(acked, start);
    if len(prefix) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(prefix, 0), at(seen, 0), at(seen, 1), at(seen, 2)]
}

// Choose a contiguous commit offset from an out-of-order delivery trace.
// Returns [next commit, observed gaps, stale deliveries, per-trace high water]. Acknowledgements at or beyond start must refer to delivered offsets in this trace.
pub fn fulmar_checkpoint(delivered: vector, acked: vector, start: f64) -> vector {
    if !fulmar_counts(delivered) { return []; }
    if !fulmar_counts(acked) { return []; }
    if !(start >= 0.0 && start <= 9007199254740991.0 && start % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = fulmar_compute(delivered, acked, start);
    if !fulmar_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let delivered = [4, 6, 5, 6];
    let acked = [4, 6];
    let start = 4.0;
    let result = fulmar_checkpoint(delivered, acked, start);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
5
1
2
7
```

#### Practice

Change delivered = [2, 3], acked = [3, 2], start = 2.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [next commit, observed gaps, stale deliveries, per-trace high water]. Acknowledgements at or beyond start must refer to delivered offsets in this trace.

Solution

The result vector is [4, 0, 0, 4]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let delivered = [4, 6, 5, 6];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let delivered = [2, 3];
```

Find

```blyx
    let acked = [4, 6];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let acked = [3, 2];
```

Find

```blyx
    let start = 4.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let start = 2.0;
```

```
0
0
4
```

### [Waxwing · Budget an expanded GraphQL field plan](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/waxwing)

Check the depth and weighted resolver cost of an expanded GraphQL field plan.

#### Budget an expanded GraphQL field plan

A flat query can cost more than a deep one when list fields fan out. Evaluate expanded cost and depth independently. The plan is only two levels deep, but its visit-weighted work is 17 against a budget of 15.

[GraphQL, demand control](https://graphql.org/learn/security/)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-waxwing.git
cd blyx-waxwing
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "1,2,2" "1,3,2" "1,4,2" 3 15
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-waxwing/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [admitted, maximum depth, total work, costliest field index]. Supply resolved aliases, fragments and list visit estimates from your parser. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| depths | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| units | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| visits | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| max_depth | positive exact integer |
| budget | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[QueryDepth](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/querydepth) · [FieldCost](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/fieldcost) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/waxwing)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Waxwing 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-waxwing/tree/v0.1.0

fn querydepth_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn querydepth_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn querydepth_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn querydepth_compute(depths: vector) -> vector {
    let mut prev = 0.0;
    let mut high = 0.0;
    let mut roots = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(depths) {
        let d = at(depths, i);
        if d < 1.0 || d > prev + 1.0 {
            return [];
        }
        if d == 1.0 {
            roots += 1;
        }
        high = querydepth_max2(high, d);
        prev = d;
        i += 1;
    }
    [high, roots, len(depths)]
}

// Validate a preorder field-depth trace from an expanded query plan.
// Returns [maximum depth, root fields, total fields]. Depth starts at one. A child can descend only one level; siblings and ascent are allowed.
pub fn querydepth_shape(depths: vector) -> vector {
    if !querydepth_counts(depths) { return []; }
    let result = querydepth_compute(depths);
    if !querydepth_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn fieldcost_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn fieldcost_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn fieldcost_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn fieldcost_compute(units: vector, visits: vector) -> vector {
    if len(units) != len(visits) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut total = 0.0;
    let mut largest = -1.0;
    let mut idx = -1;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(units) {
        let cost = at(units, i) * at(visits, i);
        if cost > 9007199254740991.0 - total {
            return [];
        }
        total += cost;
        if cost > largest {
            largest = cost;
            idx = i;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [total, idx, fieldcost_max2(0.0, largest)]
}

// Estimate expanded resolver work using per-field costs and visit counts.
// Returns [total work, costliest field index, largest single field contribution]. Empty input uses index -1. Inputs come from the host query planner.
pub fn fieldcost_weighted(units: vector, visits: vector) -> vector {
    if !fieldcost_counts(units) { return []; }
    if !fieldcost_counts(visits) { return []; }
    let result = fieldcost_compute(units, visits);
    if !fieldcost_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn waxwing_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn waxwing_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn waxwing_compute(depths: vector, units: vector, visits: vector, max_depth: f64, budget: f64) -> vector {
    if len(depths) != len(units) || len(depths) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let shape = querydepth_shape(depths);
    let cost = fieldcost_weighted(units, visits);
    if len(shape) == 0 || len(cost) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut allow = 0;
    if at(shape, 0) <= max_depth && at(cost, 0) <= budget {
        allow = 1;
    }
    [allow, at(shape, 0), at(cost, 0), at(cost, 1)]
}

// Check the depth and weighted resolver cost of an expanded GraphQL field plan.
// Returns [admitted, maximum depth, total work, costliest field index]. Supply resolved aliases, fragments and list visit estimates from your parser.
pub fn waxwing_budget(depths: vector, units: vector, visits: vector, max_depth: f64, budget: f64) -> vector {
    if !waxwing_counts(depths) { return []; }
    if !waxwing_counts(units) { return []; }
    if !waxwing_counts(visits) { return []; }
    if !(max_depth >= 1.0 && max_depth <= 9007199254740991.0 && max_depth % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(budget >= 0.0 && budget <= 9007199254740991.0 && budget % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = waxwing_compute(depths, units, visits, max_depth, budget);
    if !waxwing_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let depths = [1, 2, 2];
    let units = [1, 3, 2];
    let visits = [1, 4, 2];
    let max_depth = 3.0;
    let budget = 15.0;
    let result = waxwing_budget(depths, units, visits, max_depth, budget);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0
2
17
1
```

Solution


Replace with


Find

```blyx
    let units = [1, 3, 2];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let units = [2, 3];
```

Find

```blyx
    let visits = [1, 4, 2];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let visits = [1, 2];
```

Find

```blyx
    let max_depth = 3.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let max_depth = 2.0;
```

Find

```blyx
    let budget = 15.0;
```

Replace with



### [Martin · Fit a retry into an RPC deadline](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/martin)

Decide whether another RPC attempt fits the remaining end-to-end deadline.

#### Fit a retry into an RPC deadline

Resetting a timeout at each hop lets a retry outlive its caller. Subtract already-spent time and the coming backoff. Fifty ticks have elapsed and ten are reserved for backoff. An idempotent retry has forty ticks available.

[gRPC, deadline propagation](https://grpc.io/docs/guides/deadlines/)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-martin.git
cd blyx-martin
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 100 "20,30" 10 35 14 1 1 3
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-martin/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [retry now or after wait, attempt budget after wait, attempts left]. The minimum is the shortest useful child duration. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| budget | nonnegative finite number |
| stages | Vector of: nonnegative finite number |
| wait | nonnegative finite number |
| minimum | positive finite number |
| status | nonnegative exact integer |
| idempotent | nonnegative exact integer |
| attempts | nonnegative exact integer |
| limit | positive exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[DeadlinePath](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/deadlinepath) · [StatusRetry](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/statusretry) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/martin)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Martin 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-martin/tree/v0.1.0

fn deadlinepath_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn deadlinepath_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn deadlinepath_magnitudes(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn deadlinepath_compute(budget: f64, stages: vector, reserve: f64) -> vector {
    let elapsed = sum(stages);
    let left = budget - elapsed - reserve;
    [deadlinepath_max2(0.0, left), deadlinepath_max2(0.0, -left), elapsed]
}

// Propagate a parent time budget across elapsed RPC stages.
// Returns [usable child budget, overrun after reserve, elapsed total]. Durations use one clock unit.
pub fn deadlinepath_remaining(budget: f64, stages: vector, reserve: f64) -> vector {
    if !(budget >= 0.0 && budget - budget == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !deadlinepath_magnitudes(stages) { return []; }
    if !(reserve >= 0.0 && reserve - reserve == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = deadlinepath_compute(budget, stages, reserve);
    if !deadlinepath_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn statusretry_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn statusretry_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn statusretry_compute(status: f64, idempotent: f64, attempts: f64, max_attempts: f64) -> vector {
    if idempotent > 1.0 || status > 16.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let left = statusretry_max2(0.0, max_attempts - attempts);
    if idempotent == 1.0 && left > 0.0 && (status == 14.0 || status == 4.0) {
        return [1, left];
    }
    [0, left]
}

// Check a conservative retry policy for selected gRPC status codes.
// Returns [retry eligible, attempts remaining]. Retries require an idempotent operation, a remaining attempt, and status 14 (UNAVAILABLE) or 4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED). Status is in 0–16.
pub fn statusretry_classify(status: f64, idempotent: f64, attempts: f64, max_attempts: f64) -> vector {
    if !(status >= 0.0 && status <= 9007199254740991.0 && status % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(idempotent >= 0.0 && idempotent <= 9007199254740991.0 && idempotent % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(attempts >= 0.0 && attempts <= 9007199254740991.0 && attempts % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(max_attempts >= 1.0 && max_attempts <= 9007199254740991.0 && max_attempts % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = statusretry_compute(status, idempotent, attempts, max_attempts);
    if !statusretry_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn martin_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn martin_magnitudes(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn martin_compute(budget: f64, stages: vector, wait: f64, minimum: f64, status: f64, idempotent: f64, attempts: f64, limit: f64) -> vector {
    let time = deadlinepath_remaining(budget, stages, wait);
    let policy = statusretry_classify(status, idempotent, attempts, limit);
    if len(time) == 0 || len(policy) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut retry = 0;
    if at(policy, 0) == 1.0 && at(time, 0) >= minimum {
        retry = 1;
    }
    [retry, at(time, 0), at(policy, 1)]
}

// Decide whether another RPC attempt fits the remaining end-to-end deadline.
// Returns [retry now or after wait, attempt budget after wait, attempts left]. The minimum is the shortest useful child duration.
pub fn martin_retry(budget: f64, stages: vector, wait: f64, minimum: f64, status: f64, idempotent: f64, attempts: f64, limit: f64) -> vector {
    if !(budget >= 0.0 && budget - budget == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !martin_magnitudes(stages) { return []; }
    if !(wait >= 0.0 && wait - wait == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(minimum > 0.0 && minimum - minimum == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(status >= 0.0 && status <= 9007199254740991.0 && status % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(idempotent >= 0.0 && idempotent <= 9007199254740991.0 && idempotent % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(attempts >= 0.0 && attempts <= 9007199254740991.0 && attempts % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(limit >= 1.0 && limit <= 9007199254740991.0 && limit % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = martin_compute(budget, stages, wait, minimum, status, idempotent, attempts, limit);
    if !martin_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let budget = 100.0;
    let stages = [20, 30];
    let wait = 10.0;
    let minimum = 35.0;
    let status = 14.0;
    let idempotent = 1.0;
    let attempts = 1.0;
    let limit = 3.0;
    let result = martin_retry(budget, stages, wait, minimum, status, idempotent, attempts, limit);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
1
40
2
```

#### Practice

Change budget = 60.0, stages = [50], wait = 8.0, minimum = 5.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [retry now or after wait, attempt budget after wait, attempts left]. The minimum is the shortest useful child duration.

Solution

The result vector is [0, 2, 2]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx

```

Replace with

```blyx
    let budget = 60.0;
```

Find

```blyx
    let stages = [20, 30];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let stages = [50];
```

Find

```blyx
    let wait = 10.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let wait = 8.0;
```

Find

```blyx
    let minimum = 35.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let minimum = 5.0;
```

```
0
2
2
```

### [Kinglet · Serve a byte range at end of file](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/kinglet)

Plan a full or single-range HTTP response against a known representation size.

#### Serve a byte range at end of file

An inclusive last byte becomes a read length with a plus one. Handle suffixes, empty resources and unsatisfied offsets explicitly. A request for bytes 90 through 200 of a 100-byte resource returns ten bytes beginning at 90.

[IETF RFC 9110, byte ranges](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-14.1.2)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-kinglet.git
cd blyx-kinglet
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 100 1 90 200
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-kinglet/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [status, body offset, body length, full length]. Mode 0 sends the full body, 1 uses first/last, 2 uses first as a suffix count. Header parsing and multipart ranges belong to the host. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| size | nonnegative exact integer |
| mode | nonnegative exact integer |
| first | nonnegative exact integer |
| last | exact signed integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[ByteRange](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/byterange) · [SuffixRange](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/suffixrange) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/kinglet)

#### Checkpoint slices across shard boundaries

Pass the tensor length in elements, element width in bytes, maximum elements per file, first requested element, element count and zero-based part number. The CLI prints the number of affected shards, the shard index and the local first byte, byte length and inclusive last byte. Query each part and concatenate its bytes in that order. Shards are consecutive, headerless, fixed-width payloads with a possibly shorter last file. Add your format’s payload offset before reading a containerized file. The command calculates intervals and leaves storage I/O and integrity checks to the caller. File-relative byte counts must fit signed 64-bit integers.

```
kinglet range 2199023255552 2 1073741824 1099511627774 5 0
kinglet range 2199023255552 2 1073741824 1099511627774 5 1
```

[Kinglet native downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-kinglet/releases/tag/v0.2.0) · [Input formats, compiler revision and API example](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-kinglet/blob/v0.2.0/SCALE.md) · [Read the experiment and download measurements](https://www.blyx-lang.space/articles/training-in-factors)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Kinglet 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-kinglet/tree/v0.1.0

fn byterange_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn byterange_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn byterange_compute(size: f64, first: f64, last: f64) -> vector {
    if last < -1.0 || (last != -1.0 && last < first) {
        return [];
    }
    if first >= size {
        return [0, 0, 0];
    }
    let mut end = size - 1.0;
    if last >= 0.0 {
        end = byterange_min2(end, last);
    }
    [1, first, end - first + 1.0]
}

// Resolve a single inclusive HTTP byte range to an offset and length.
// Returns [satisfiable, offset, length]. Set last to -1 for an open-ended range. A syntactically reversed range is invalid.
pub fn byterange_resolve(size: f64, first: f64, last: f64) -> vector {
    if !(size >= 0.0 && size <= 9007199254740991.0 && size % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(first >= 0.0 && first <= 9007199254740991.0 && first % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(last >= -9007199254740991.0 && last <= 9007199254740991.0 && last % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = byterange_compute(size, first, last);
    if !byterange_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn suffixrange_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn suffixrange_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn suffixrange_compute(size: f64, suffix: f64) -> vector {
    if suffix == 0.0 || size == 0.0 {
        return [0, 0, 0];
    }
    let count = suffixrange_min2(size, suffix);
    [1, size - count, count]
}

// Resolve an HTTP suffix-byte specification without negative offsets.
// Returns [satisfiable, offset, length]. A suffix longer than the entity selects the full entity. Zero bytes or an empty entity produce an unsatisfied range.
pub fn suffixrange_resolve(size: f64, suffix: f64) -> vector {
    if !(size >= 0.0 && size <= 9007199254740991.0 && size % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(suffix >= 0.0 && suffix <= 9007199254740991.0 && suffix % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = suffixrange_compute(size, suffix);
    if !suffixrange_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn kinglet_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn kinglet_compute(size: f64, mode: f64, first: f64, last: f64) -> vector {
    if mode == 0.0 {
        return [200, 0, size, size];
    }
    let mut range = byterange_resolve(size, first, last);
    if mode == 2.0 {
        range = suffixrange_resolve(size, first);
    }
    if mode > 2.0 || len(range) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    if at(range, 0) == 0.0 {
        return [416, 0, 0, size];
    }
    [206, at(range, 1), at(range, 2), size]
}

// Plan a full or single-range HTTP response against a known representation size.
// Returns [status, body offset, body length, full length]. Mode 0 sends the full body, 1 uses first/last, 2 uses first as a suffix count. Header parsing and multipart ranges belong to the host.
pub fn kinglet_respond(size: f64, mode: f64, first: f64, last: f64) -> vector {
    if !(size >= 0.0 && size <= 9007199254740991.0 && size % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(mode >= 0.0 && mode <= 9007199254740991.0 && mode % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(first >= 0.0 && first <= 9007199254740991.0 && first % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(last >= -9007199254740991.0 && last <= 9007199254740991.0 && last % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = kinglet_compute(size, mode, first, last);
    if !kinglet_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let size = 100.0;
    let mode = 1.0;
    let first = 90.0;
    let last = 200.0;
    let result = kinglet_respond(size, mode, first, last);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```

90
10
100
```

Hint

Solution


Replace with



### [Barnowl · Find clock reversals and gaps in an audit export](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/barnowl)

Inspect a supplied audit export for sequence gaps, replays and clock reversals.

#### Find clock reversals and gaps in an audit export

Sorting an export by timestamp can conceal a clock rollback. Audit receipt order and sequence continuity as separate signals. The sample skips sequence 41, repeats 42 and ends with a backward clock step. The result identifies the reversed row.

[OpenTelemetry, logs data model](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/logs/data-model/)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-barnowl.git
cd blyx-barnowl
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "40,42,42" "10,14,12"
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-barnowl/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [gap count, nonadvancing IDs, backward clock steps, first reversed row, clean flag]. Preserve original receipt order; a gap is an observation for investigation. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| ids | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| times | Vector of: exact signed integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[EventOrder](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/eventorder) · [AuditGaps](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/auditgaps) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/barnowl)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Barnowl 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-barnowl/tree/v0.1.0

fn eventorder_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn eventorder_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn eventorder_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn eventorder_compute(times: vector) -> vector {
    let mut backward = 0;
    let mut biggest = 0.0;
    let mut first = -1;
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(times) {
        let step = at(times, i - 1) - at(times, i);
        if step > 0.0 {
            if first < 0 {
                first = i;
            }
            backward += 1;
            biggest = eventorder_max2(biggest, step);
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [backward, biggest, first]
}

// Locate time-order anomalies in a log stream in receipt order.
// Returns [adjacent clock reversals, largest backward step, first reversal index]. Equal timestamps preserve order.
pub fn eventorder_scan(times: vector) -> vector {
    if !eventorder_integers(times) { return []; }
    let result = eventorder_compute(times);
    if !eventorder_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn auditgaps_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn auditgaps_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn auditgaps_compute(ids: vector) -> vector {
    if len(ids) == 0 {
        return [0, 0, -1];
    }
    let mut high = at(ids, 0);
    let mut holes = 0.0;
    let mut replay = 0;
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(ids) {
        let id = at(ids, i);
        if id <= high {
            replay += 1;
        } else {
            holes += id - high - 1.0;
            high = id;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [holes, replay, high]
}

// Count forward gaps and nonadvancing IDs in an audit export.
// Returns [missing at first observation, nonadvancing rows, highest observed ID]. The first row establishes the baseline; the empty sentinel is -1.
pub fn auditgaps_sequence(ids: vector) -> vector {
    if !auditgaps_counts(ids) { return []; }
    let result = auditgaps_compute(ids);
    if !auditgaps_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn barnowl_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn barnowl_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn barnowl_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn barnowl_compute(ids: vector, times: vector) -> vector {
    if len(ids) != len(times) {
        return [];
    }
    let seq = auditgaps_sequence(ids);
    let clock = eventorder_scan(times);
    if len(seq) == 0 || len(clock) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut clean = 0;
    if at(seq, 0) == 0.0 && at(seq, 1) == 0.0 && at(clock, 0) == 0.0 {
        clean = 1;
    }
    [at(seq, 0), at(seq, 1), at(clock, 0), at(clock, 2), clean]
}

// Inspect a supplied audit export for sequence gaps, replays and clock reversals.
// Returns [gap count, nonadvancing IDs, backward clock steps, first reversed row, clean flag]. Preserve original receipt order; a gap is an observation for investigation.
pub fn barnowl_audit(ids: vector, times: vector) -> vector {
    if !barnowl_counts(ids) { return []; }
    if !barnowl_integers(times) { return []; }
    let result = barnowl_compute(ids, times);
    if !barnowl_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let ids = [40, 42, 42];
    let times = [10, 14, 12];
    let result = barnowl_audit(ids, times);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
1
1
1
2
0
```

#### Practice

Change ids = [1, 2], times = [4, 4]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [gap count, nonadvancing IDs, backward clock steps, first reversed row, clean flag]. Preserve original receipt order; a gap is an observation for investigation.

Solution

The result vector is [0, 0, 0, -1, 1]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let ids = [40, 42, 42];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let ids = [1, 2];
```

Find

```blyx
    let times = [10, 14, 12];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let times = [4, 4];
```

Output after the change

```
0
0
0
-1
1
```

### [Harrier · Apply freshness policy to a verified session](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/harrier)

Apply time and assurance policy to a session after upstream identity verification.

#### Apply freshness policy to a verified session

A still-valid token can represent an old or insufficiently verified session. Apply application policy after the identity provider has verified the token. The verified session is eight ticks old and meets the required assurance level. The expiration boundary remains exclusive.

[IETF RFC 7519, registered claims](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7519.html#section-4.1)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-harrier.git
cd blyx-harrier
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 100 90 110 0 2 2 92 10
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-harrier/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [policy accepted, claims time accepted, assurance/freshness accepted, session age]. Use only after the host has authenticated and verified the issuer, audience and signature. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| now | exact signed integer |
| begins | exact signed integer |
| expires | exact signed integer |
| skew | nonnegative exact integer |
| observed | nonnegative exact integer |
| required | nonnegative exact integer |
| auth_time | exact signed integer |
| max_age | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[ClaimClock](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/claimclock) · [AssuranceLevel](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/assurancelevel) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/harrier)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Harrier 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-harrier/tree/v0.1.0

fn claimclock_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn claimclock_compute(now: f64, begins: f64, expires: f64, skew: f64) -> vector {
    if expires <= begins {
        return [];
    }
    let early = begins - now;
    let late = now - expires;
    if early > skew {
        return [0, early, 0];
    }
    if late >= skew {
        return [0, 0, late];
    }
    [1, 0, 0]
}

// Evaluate activation and expiration bounds on previously verified claims.
// Returns [time accepted, early ticks, expired ticks]. Expiration is exclusive and applies symmetric caller-supplied clock tolerance.
pub fn claimclock_check(now: f64, begins: f64, expires: f64, skew: f64) -> vector {
    if !(now >= -9007199254740991.0 && now <= 9007199254740991.0 && now % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(begins >= -9007199254740991.0 && begins <= 9007199254740991.0 && begins % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(expires >= -9007199254740991.0 && expires <= 9007199254740991.0 && expires % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(skew >= 0.0 && skew <= 9007199254740991.0 && skew % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = claimclock_compute(now, begins, expires, skew);
    if !claimclock_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn assurancelevel_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn assurancelevel_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn assurancelevel_compute(observed: f64, required: f64, auth_time: f64, now: f64, max_age: f64) -> vector {
    if auth_time > now {
        return [];
    }
    let age = now - auth_time;
    let gap = assurancelevel_max2(0.0, required - observed);
    if gap == 0.0 && age <= max_age {
        return [1, age, 0];
    }
    [0, age, gap]
}

// Check session freshness and an application-defined ordered assurance level.
// Returns [meets both, age, missing assurance levels]. A future authentication time is invalid; equality at the age limit is accepted.
pub fn assurancelevel_policy(observed: f64, required: f64, auth_time: f64, now: f64, max_age: f64) -> vector {
    if !(observed >= 0.0 && observed <= 9007199254740991.0 && observed % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(required >= 0.0 && required <= 9007199254740991.0 && required % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(auth_time >= -9007199254740991.0 && auth_time <= 9007199254740991.0 && auth_time % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(now >= -9007199254740991.0 && now <= 9007199254740991.0 && now % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(max_age >= 0.0 && max_age <= 9007199254740991.0 && max_age % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = assurancelevel_compute(observed, required, auth_time, now, max_age);
    if !assurancelevel_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn harrier_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn harrier_compute(now: f64, begins: f64, expires: f64, skew: f64, observed: f64, required: f64, auth_time: f64, max_age: f64) -> vector {
    let claim = claimclock_check(now, begins, expires, skew);
    let level = assurancelevel_policy(observed, required, auth_time, now, max_age);
    if len(claim) == 0 || len(level) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(claim, 0) * at(level, 0), at(claim, 0), at(level, 0), at(level, 1)]
}

// Apply time and assurance policy to a session after upstream identity verification.
// Returns [policy accepted, claims time accepted, assurance/freshness accepted, session age]. Use only after the host has authenticated and verified the issuer, audience and signature.
pub fn harrier_session(now: f64, begins: f64, expires: f64, skew: f64, observed: f64, required: f64, auth_time: f64, max_age: f64) -> vector {
    if !(now >= -9007199254740991.0 && now <= 9007199254740991.0 && now % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(begins >= -9007199254740991.0 && begins <= 9007199254740991.0 && begins % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(expires >= -9007199254740991.0 && expires <= 9007199254740991.0 && expires % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(skew >= 0.0 && skew <= 9007199254740991.0 && skew % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(observed >= 0.0 && observed <= 9007199254740991.0 && observed % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(required >= 0.0 && required <= 9007199254740991.0 && required % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(auth_time >= -9007199254740991.0 && auth_time <= 9007199254740991.0 && auth_time % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(max_age >= 0.0 && max_age <= 9007199254740991.0 && max_age % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = harrier_compute(now, begins, expires, skew, observed, required, auth_time, max_age);
    if !harrier_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let now = 100.0;
    let begins = 90.0;
    let expires = 110.0;
    let skew = 0.0;
    let observed = 2.0;
    let required = 2.0;
    let auth_time = 92.0;
    let max_age = 10.0;
    let result = harrier_session(now, begins, expires, skew, observed, required, auth_time, max_age);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
1
1
1
8
```

#### Practice

Change now = 110.0, auth_time = 105.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [policy accepted, claims time accepted, assurance/freshness accepted, session age]. Use only after the host has authenticated and verified the issuer, audience and signature.

Solution

The result vector is [0, 0, 1, 5]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let now = 100.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let now = 110.0;
```

Find

```blyx
    let auth_time = 92.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let auth_time = 105.0;
```

Output after the change

```
0
0
1
5
```

### [Plover · Gate an alert on short and long error windows](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/plover)

Gate alerts on error-budget burn in both a short and a long window.

#### Gate an alert on short and long error windows

A brief burst or stale long-window average can trigger a noisy alert on its own. Require both windows to cross the selected burn threshold. The short window burns four times its error budget and the long window burns twice. Both reach the selected threshold.

[Google SRE Workbook, alerting on SLOs](https://sre.google/workbook/alerting-on-slos/)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-plover.git
cd blyx-plover
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 2 10 10 100 0.05 2
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-plover/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [alert, short burn, long burn, long-window excess failures]. The short window must be a subset of the long window, including its good events. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| fast_bad | nonnegative exact integer |
| fast_total | positive exact integer |
| slow_bad | nonnegative exact integer |
| slow_total | positive exact integer |
| allowed | positive finite number |
| trigger | positive finite number |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[SloBurn](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/sloburn) · [BudgetLeft](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/budgetleft) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/plover)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Plover 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-plover/tree/v0.1.0

fn sloburn_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn sloburn_compute(bad: f64, total: f64, allowed: f64) -> vector {
    if bad > total || allowed > 1.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let rate = bad / total;
    [rate, rate / allowed]
}

// Normalize observed failures by an allowed error fraction.
// Returns [observed error fraction, burn multiple]. The allowed error fraction is greater than zero and at most one.
pub fn sloburn_rate(bad: f64, total: f64, allowed: f64) -> vector {
    if !(bad >= 0.0 && bad <= 9007199254740991.0 && bad % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(total >= 1.0 && total <= 9007199254740991.0 && total % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(allowed > 0.0 && allowed - allowed == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = sloburn_compute(bad, total, allowed);
    if !sloburn_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn budgetleft_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn budgetleft_floorpos(value: f64) -> f64 {
    value - value % 1.0
}

fn budgetleft_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn budgetleft_compute(bad: f64, total: f64, allowance: f64) -> vector {
    if bad > total {
        return [];
    }
    let capacity = budgetleft_floorpos(total * allowance);
    [capacity, budgetleft_max2(0.0, capacity - bad), budgetleft_max2(0.0, bad - capacity)]
}

// Account for whole allowed failures in an observed window.
// Returns [whole failures permitted, remaining, excess]. Rounds the nonnegative product of sample count and allowance down.
pub fn budgetleft_events(bad: f64, total: f64, allowance: f64) -> vector {
    if !(bad >= 0.0 && bad <= 9007199254740991.0 && bad % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(total >= 0.0 && total <= 9007199254740991.0 && total % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(allowance >= 0.0 && allowance <= 1.0) { return []; }
    let result = budgetleft_compute(bad, total, allowance);
    if !budgetleft_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn plover_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn plover_compute(fast_bad: f64, fast_total: f64, slow_bad: f64, slow_total: f64, allowed: f64, trigger: f64) -> vector {
    if fast_total > slow_total || fast_bad > slow_bad || fast_total - fast_bad > slow_total - slow_bad {
        return [];
    }
    let fast = sloburn_rate(fast_bad, fast_total, allowed);
    let slow = sloburn_rate(slow_bad, slow_total, allowed);
    let balance = budgetleft_events(slow_bad, slow_total, allowed);
    if len(fast) == 0 || len(slow) == 0 || len(balance) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut alert = 0;
    if at(fast, 1) >= trigger && at(slow, 1) >= trigger {
        alert = 1;
    }
    [alert, at(fast, 1), at(slow, 1), at(balance, 2)]
}

// Gate alerts on error-budget burn in both a short and a long window.
// Returns [alert, short burn, long burn, long-window excess failures]. The short window must be a subset of the long window, including its good events.
pub fn plover_alert(fast_bad: f64, fast_total: f64, slow_bad: f64, slow_total: f64, allowed: f64, trigger: f64) -> vector {
    if !(fast_bad >= 0.0 && fast_bad <= 9007199254740991.0 && fast_bad % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(fast_total >= 1.0 && fast_total <= 9007199254740991.0 && fast_total % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(slow_bad >= 0.0 && slow_bad <= 9007199254740991.0 && slow_bad % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(slow_total >= 1.0 && slow_total <= 9007199254740991.0 && slow_total % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(allowed > 0.0 && allowed - allowed == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(trigger > 0.0 && trigger - trigger == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = plover_compute(fast_bad, fast_total, slow_bad, slow_total, allowed, trigger);
    if !plover_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let fast_bad = 2.0;
    let fast_total = 10.0;
    let slow_bad = 10.0;
    let slow_total = 100.0;
    let allowed = 0.05;
    let trigger = 2.0;
    let result = plover_alert(fast_bad, fast_total, slow_bad, slow_total, allowed, trigger);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
1
4
2
5
```

#### Practice

Change slow_bad = 5.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [alert, short burn, long burn, long-window excess failures]. The short window must be a subset of the long window, including its good events.

Solution

The result vector is [0, 4, 1, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let slow_bad = 10.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let slow_bad = 5.0;
```

Output after the change

```
0
4
1
0
```

### [Jacana · Compare a crude rate with a standardized rate](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/jacana)

Compare a crude event rate with a directly standardized rate.

#### Compare a crude rate with a standardized rate

A change in the mix of observed groups can move the pooled rate. Recalculate rates against fixed reference weights before comparing populations. The crude event rate is 0.75. Equal reference weights give each stratum the same influence and reduce the standardized rate to 0.5.

[NCI SEER, direct age adjustment](https://seer.cancer.gov/seerstat/tutorials/aarates/definition.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.1 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-jacana.git
cd blyx-jacana
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0,6" "2,6" "1,1"
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-jacana/blob/v0.1.1/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [crude rate, standardized rate, standardized minus crude, total observations]. Each reported stratum needs observations for the crude comparison. Causal interpretation depends on study design. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| events | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| trials | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| weights | Vector of: nonnegative finite number |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[StrataMean](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/stratamean) · [StdWeight](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/stdweight) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/jacana)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Jacana 0.1.1 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-jacana/tree/v0.1.1

fn stratamean_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn stratamean_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn stratamean_compute(events: vector, trials: vector) -> vector {
    if len(events) == 0 || len(events) != len(trials) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(events) {
        if at(trials, i) == 0.0 || at(events, i) > at(trials, i) {
            return [];
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    let n = sum(trials);
    if n > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let successes = sum(events);
    [successes, n, successes / n]
}

// Pool event counts and expose the crude observed rate.
// Returns [total events, total trials, crude rate]. Every stratum must have observations and events cannot exceed trials.
pub fn stratamean_pooled(events: vector, trials: vector) -> vector {
    if !stratamean_counts(events) { return []; }
    if !stratamean_counts(trials) { return []; }
    let result = stratamean_compute(events, trials);
    if !stratamean_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn stdweight_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn stdweight_magnitudes(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn stdweight_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn stdweight_compute(events: vector, trials: vector, weights: vector) -> vector {
    if len(events) != len(trials) || len(events) != len(weights) {
        return [];
    }
    let w = sum(weights);
    if w <= 0.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut result = 0.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(events) {
        let n = at(trials, i);
        let e = at(events, i);
        let part = at(weights, i);
        if e > n || (part > 0.0 && n == 0.0) {
            return [];
        }
        if part > 0.0 {
            result += (part / w) * (e / n);
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [result, w]
}

// Directly standardize stratum-specific rates to a reference population.
// Returns [standardized rate, total reference weight]. Positive-weight strata require observations. Zero-weight strata may be empty.
pub fn stdweight_direct(events: vector, trials: vector, weights: vector) -> vector {
    if !stdweight_counts(events) { return []; }
    if !stdweight_counts(trials) { return []; }
    if !stdweight_magnitudes(weights) { return []; }
    let result = stdweight_compute(events, trials, weights);
    if !stdweight_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn jacana_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn jacana_magnitudes(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn jacana_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn jacana_compute(events: vector, trials: vector, weights: vector) -> vector {
    let pooled = stratamean_pooled(events, trials);
    let std = stdweight_direct(events, trials, weights);
    if len(pooled) == 0 || len(std) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(pooled, 2), at(std, 0), at(std, 0) - at(pooled, 2), at(pooled, 1)]
}

// Compare a crude event rate with a directly standardized rate.
// Returns [crude rate, standardized rate, standardized minus crude, total observations]. Each reported stratum needs observations for the crude comparison. Causal interpretation depends on study design.
pub fn jacana_standardize(events: vector, trials: vector, weights: vector) -> vector {
    if !jacana_counts(events) { return []; }
    if !jacana_counts(trials) { return []; }
    if !jacana_magnitudes(weights) { return []; }
    let result = jacana_compute(events, trials, weights);
    if !jacana_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let events = [0, 6];
    let trials = [2, 6];
    let weights = [1, 1];
    let result = jacana_standardize(events, trials, weights);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0.75
0.5
-0.25
8
```

#### Practice

Hint

Returns [crude rate, standardized rate, standardized minus crude, total observations]. Each reported stratum needs observations for the crude comparison. Causal interpretation depends on study design.

Solution

The result vector is [0.5, 0.5, 0, 4]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx

```

Replace with

```blyx
    let events = [1, 1];
```

Find

```blyx
    let trials = [2, 6];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let trials = [2, 2];
```

Find

```blyx
    let weights = [1, 1];
```

Replace with

```blyx

```

