
### [Redstart · Update a binary-event probability after observations](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/redstart)

Update a binary-event model and report uncertainty in its probability.

#### Update a binary-event probability after observations

A point estimate alone hides the difference between two observations and two thousand. Return posterior variance with the updated mean. One success and one failure update a uniform prior to Beta(2,2). The posterior mean is 0.5 and its variance is 0.05.

[PyMC, Beta distribution](https://www.pymc.io/projects/docs/en/stable/api/distributions/generated/pymc.Beta.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-redstart.git
cd blyx-redstart
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 1 1 1 1
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-redstart/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [posterior mean, posterior variance, posterior alpha, posterior beta]. This conjugate model assumes exchangeable Bernoulli observations. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| alpha | positive finite number |
| beta | positive finite number |
| positive | nonnegative exact integer |
| negative | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[BetaUpdate](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/betaupdate) · [BetaMoment](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/betamoment) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/redstart)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Redstart 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-redstart/tree/v0.1.0

fn betaupdate_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn betaupdate_compute(alpha: f64, beta: f64, positive: f64, negative: f64) -> vector {
    [alpha + positive, beta + negative]
}

// Update a Beta prior with Bernoulli counts.
// Returns [posterior alpha, posterior beta]. Use one count for each independent binary observation.
pub fn betaupdate_observe(alpha: f64, beta: f64, positive: f64, negative: f64) -> vector {
    if !(alpha > 0.0 && alpha - alpha == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(beta > 0.0 && beta - beta == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(positive >= 0.0 && positive <= 9007199254740991.0 && positive % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(negative >= 0.0 && negative <= 9007199254740991.0 && negative % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = betaupdate_compute(alpha, beta, positive, negative);
    if !betaupdate_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn betamoment_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn betamoment_compute(alpha: f64, beta: f64) -> vector {
    let total = alpha + beta;
    let mean = alpha / total;
    [mean, mean * (beta / total) / (total + 1.0), total]
}

// Calculate the mean and variance of a Beta distribution.
// Returns [mean, variance, concentration]. Uses mean times its complement divided by concentration plus one.
pub fn betamoment_summary(alpha: f64, beta: f64) -> vector {
    if !(alpha > 0.0 && alpha - alpha == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(beta > 0.0 && beta - beta == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = betamoment_compute(alpha, beta);
    if !betamoment_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn redstart_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn redstart_compute(alpha: f64, beta: f64, positive: f64, negative: f64) -> vector {
    let next = betaupdate_observe(alpha, beta, positive, negative);
    if len(next) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let stats = betamoment_summary(at(next, 0), at(next, 1));
    if len(stats) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(stats, 0), at(stats, 1), at(next, 0), at(next, 1)]
}

// Update a binary-event model and report uncertainty in its probability.
// Returns [posterior mean, posterior variance, posterior alpha, posterior beta]. This conjugate model assumes exchangeable Bernoulli observations.
pub fn redstart_posterior(alpha: f64, beta: f64, positive: f64, negative: f64) -> vector {
    if !(alpha > 0.0 && alpha - alpha == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(beta > 0.0 && beta - beta == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(positive >= 0.0 && positive <= 9007199254740991.0 && positive % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(negative >= 0.0 && negative <= 9007199254740991.0 && negative % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = redstart_compute(alpha, beta, positive, negative);
    if !redstart_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let alpha = 1.0;
    let beta = 1.0;
    let positive = 1.0;
    let negative = 1.0;
    let result = redstart_posterior(alpha, beta, positive, negative);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0.5
0.05
2
2
```

#### Practice

Change positive = 0.0, negative = 0.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [posterior mean, posterior variance, posterior alpha, posterior beta]. This conjugate model assumes exchangeable Bernoulli observations.

Solution

The result vector is [0.5, 0.08333333333333333, 1, 1]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let positive = 1.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let positive = 0.0;
```

Find

```blyx
    let negative = 1.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let negative = 0.0;
```

Output after the change

```
0.5
0.08333333333333333
1
1
```

### [Quail · Compare a real-qubit circuit with observed shots](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/quail)

Simulate a short real-amplitude single-qubit circuit and compare shot counts.

#### Compare a real-qubit circuit with observed shots

Shot frequencies can differ from circuit predictions. Keep amplitudes through the gate sequence and compare probabilities only at readout. The X and Z sequence prepares a state whose probability of one is 1. Six ones in eight measured shots give a 0.25 discrepancy.

[IBM Quantum, single-system quantum information](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/learning/en/courses/basics-of-quantum-information/single-systems/quantum-information)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-quail.git
cd blyx-quail
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "1,0" "1,2" 2 6
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-quail/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [predicted P(1), observed P(1), absolute discrepancy]. Gates are applied left to right. Complex phase gates and hardware execution require a different state representation. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| state | Vector of: finite number |
| gates | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| zero | nonnegative exact integer |
| one | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[RealQubit](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/realqubit) · [ReadoutFreq](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/readoutfreq) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/quail)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Quail 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-quail/tree/v0.1.0

fn realqubit_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn realqubit_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn realqubit_compute(state: vector, gate: f64) -> vector {
    if len(state) != 2 || realqubit_absolute(dot(state, state) - 1.0) > 0.000000001 || gate > 3.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let a = at(state, 0);
    let b = at(state, 1);
    if gate == 0.0 {
        return [a, b];
    }
    if gate == 1.0 {
        return [b, a];
    }
    if gate == 2.0 {
        return [a, -b];
    }
    let scale = 0.7071067811865475;
    [(a + b) * scale, (a - b) * scale]
}

// Apply I, X, Z or Hadamard to a normalized real-amplitude qubit.
// Input [a,b] must have unit squared norm within 1e-9. Gate IDs 0,1,2,3 denote I,X,Z,H. Returns transformed amplitudes.
pub fn realqubit_gate(state: vector, gate: f64) -> vector {
    if !realqubit_finite(state) { return []; }
    if !(gate >= 0.0 && gate <= 9007199254740991.0 && gate % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = realqubit_compute(state, gate);
    if !realqubit_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn readoutfreq_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn readoutfreq_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn readoutfreq_compute(state: vector, zero: f64, one: f64) -> vector {
    if len(state) != 2 || readoutfreq_absolute(dot(state, state) - 1.0) > 0.000000001 || zero + one <= 0.0 || zero + one > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let prob = at(state, 1) * at(state, 1);
    let seen = one / (zero + one);
    [prob, seen, readoutfreq_absolute(prob - seen)]
}

// Compare computational-basis shot frequencies to a real qubit's probabilities.
// Returns [predicted P(1), observed P(1), absolute difference]. At least one observed shot and a normalized two-amplitude state are required.
pub fn readoutfreq_compare(state: vector, zero: f64, one: f64) -> vector {
    if !readoutfreq_finite(state) { return []; }
    if !(zero >= 0.0 && zero <= 9007199254740991.0 && zero % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(one >= 0.0 && one <= 9007199254740991.0 && one % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = readoutfreq_compute(state, zero, one);
    if !readoutfreq_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn quail_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn quail_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn quail_compute(state: vector, gates: vector, zero: f64, one: f64) -> vector {
    let mut wave = realqubit_gate(state, 0.0);
    if len(wave) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(gates) {
        wave = realqubit_gate(wave, at(gates, i));
        if len(wave) == 0 {
            return [];
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    readoutfreq_compare(wave, zero, one)
}

// Simulate a short real-amplitude single-qubit circuit and compare shot counts.
// Returns [predicted P(1), observed P(1), absolute discrepancy]. Gates are applied left to right. Complex phase gates and hardware execution require a different state representation.
pub fn quail_experiment(state: vector, gates: vector, zero: f64, one: f64) -> vector {
    if !quail_finite(state) { return []; }
    if !quail_counts(gates) { return []; }
    if !(zero >= 0.0 && zero <= 9007199254740991.0 && zero % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(one >= 0.0 && one <= 9007199254740991.0 && one % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = quail_compute(state, gates, zero, one);
    if !quail_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let state = [1, 0];
    let gates = [1, 2];
    let zero = 2.0;
    let one = 6.0;
    let result = quail_experiment(state, gates, zero, one);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
1
0.75
0.25
```

#### Practice

Hint

Solution

The result vector is [0, 0, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.


Replace with


Find


Replace with

```blyx

```

Find

```blyx

```

Replace with

### [Skimmer · Read parity alongside two-bit marginals](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/skimmer)

Compare parity and marginal balance in two-bit shot data.

#### Read parity alongside two-bit marginals

Balanced single-bit frequencies can mask different joint outcomes. Inspect parity alongside both marginals. Four 00 and four 11 shots have equally balanced individual bits, while every shot has even parity.

[IBM Quantum, multiple systems](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/learning/en/courses/basics-of-quantum-information/multiple-systems/quantum-information)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-skimmer.git
cd blyx-skimmer
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "4,0,0,4" 1 0.1
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-skimmer/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [parity expectation, left-one frequency, right-one frequency, parity matches target]. A single measurement basis characterizes this histogram only. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| counts | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| expected_even | probability in [0,1] |
| tolerance | probability in [0,1] |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[BitParity](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/bitparity) · [ShotMargins](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/shotmargins) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/skimmer)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Skimmer 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-skimmer/tree/v0.1.0

fn bitparity_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn bitparity_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn bitparity_compute(counts: vector) -> vector {
    if len(counts) != 4 {
        return [];
    }
    let total = sum(counts);
    if total <= 0.0 || total > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let even = (at(counts, 0) + at(counts, 3)) / total;
    let odd = (at(counts, 1) + at(counts, 2)) / total;
    [even, odd, even - odd]
}

// Measure even/odd parity from a two-bit measurement histogram.
// Bin order is 00,01,10,11. Returns [even frequency, odd frequency, parity expectation]. At least one shot is required.
pub fn bitparity_measure(counts: vector) -> vector {
    if !bitparity_counts(counts) { return []; }
    let result = bitparity_compute(counts);
    if !bitparity_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn shotmargins_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn shotmargins_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn shotmargins_compute(counts: vector) -> vector {
    if len(counts) != 4 {
        return [];
    }
    let total = sum(counts);
    if total <= 0.0 || total > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    [(at(counts, 2) + at(counts, 3)) / total, (at(counts, 1) + at(counts, 3)) / total, total]
}

// Extract both individual bit frequencies from joint two-bit shots.
// Bin order is 00,01,10,11. Returns [P(left=1), P(right=1), shots]. At least one shot is required.
pub fn shotmargins_bits(counts: vector) -> vector {
    if !shotmargins_counts(counts) { return []; }
    let result = shotmargins_compute(counts);
    if !shotmargins_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn skimmer_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn skimmer_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn skimmer_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn skimmer_compute(counts: vector, expected_even: f64, tolerance: f64) -> vector {
    let joint = bitparity_measure(counts);
    let margins = shotmargins_bits(counts);
    if len(joint) == 0 || len(margins) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut good = 0;
    if skimmer_absolute(at(joint, 0) - expected_even) <= tolerance {
        good = 1;
    }
    [at(joint, 2), at(margins, 0), at(margins, 1), good]
}

// Compare parity and marginal balance in two-bit shot data.
// Returns [parity expectation, left-one frequency, right-one frequency, parity matches target]. A single measurement basis characterizes this histogram only.
pub fn skimmer_characterize(counts: vector, expected_even: f64, tolerance: f64) -> vector {
    if !skimmer_counts(counts) { return []; }
    if !(expected_even >= 0.0 && expected_even <= 1.0) { return []; }
    if !(tolerance >= 0.0 && tolerance <= 1.0) { return []; }
    let result = skimmer_compute(counts, expected_even, tolerance);
    if !skimmer_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let counts = [4, 0, 0, 4];
    let expected_even = 1.0;
    let tolerance = 0.1;
    let result = skimmer_characterize(counts, expected_even, tolerance);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
1
0.5
0.5
1
```

#### Practice

Change counts = [2, 2, 2, 2]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [parity expectation, left-one frequency, right-one frequency, parity matches target]. A single measurement basis characterizes this histogram only.

Solution

The result vector is [0, 0.5, 0.5, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let counts = [4, 0, 0, 4];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let counts = [2, 2, 2, 2];
```

Output after the change

```
0
0.5
0.5
0
```

### [Magpie · Integrate unevenly spaced observations](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/magpie)

Integrate an increasing sample grid and flag under-sampled sections.

#### Integrate unevenly spaced observations

An arithmetic average ignores the spacing between measurements. Integrate on the supplied time grid and flag large gaps. A constant value of two across four time units gives an area of eight. The largest interval exceeds the allowed two-unit gap.

[NumPy, composite trapezoidal integration](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.trapezoid.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-magpie.git
cd blyx-magpie
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0,1,4" "2,2,2" 2
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-magpie/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [area, span-weighted mean, widest gap, exceeds gap limit]. Rejects duplicate or reversed sample times. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| x | Vector of: finite number |
| y | Vector of: finite number |
| max_gap | positive finite number |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[Trapezoid](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/trapezoid) · [GridGap](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/gridgap) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/magpie)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Magpie 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-magpie/tree/v0.1.0

fn trapezoid_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn trapezoid_compute(x: vector, y: vector) -> vector {
    if len(x) < 2 || len(x) != len(y) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut area = 0.0;
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(x) {
        let width = at(x, i) - at(x, i - 1);
        let middle = at(y, i) * 0.5 + at(y, i - 1) * 0.5;
        area += width * middle;
        i += 1;
    }
    [area, at(x, len(x) - 1) - at(x, 0)]
}

// Integrate sampled values by the composite trapezoidal rule in input order.
// Returns [signed integral, signed span]. A descending grid reverses the integral sign. At least two paired samples are required.
pub fn trapezoid_integrate(x: vector, y: vector) -> vector {
    if !trapezoid_finite(x) { return []; }
    if !trapezoid_finite(y) { return []; }
    let result = trapezoid_compute(x, y);
    if !trapezoid_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn gridgap_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn gridgap_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn gridgap_compute(x: vector) -> vector {
    if len(x) < 2 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut widest = -1.0;
    let mut idx = -1;
    let mut bad = 0;
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(x) {
        let step = at(x, i) - at(x, i - 1);
        if step <= 0.0 {
            bad += 1;
        }
        if gridgap_absolute(step) > widest {
            widest = gridgap_absolute(step);
            idx = i;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [widest, idx, bad]
}

// Locate the coarsest gap and count nonincreasing steps in a sample grid.
// Returns [largest absolute step, right index of the first largest step, nonincreasing steps]. At least two points are required.
pub fn gridgap_inspect(x: vector) -> vector {
    if !gridgap_finite(x) { return []; }
    let result = gridgap_compute(x);
    if !gridgap_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn magpie_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn magpie_compute(x: vector, y: vector, max_gap: f64) -> vector {
    let gaps = gridgap_inspect(x);
    if len(gaps) == 0 || at(gaps, 2) > 0.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let result = trapezoid_integrate(x, y);
    if len(result) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut sparse = 0;
    if at(gaps, 0) > max_gap {
        sparse = 1;
    }
    [at(result, 0), at(result, 0) / at(result, 1), at(gaps, 0), sparse]
}

// Integrate an increasing sample grid and flag under-sampled sections.
// Returns [area, span-weighted mean, widest gap, exceeds gap limit]. Rejects duplicate or reversed sample times.
pub fn magpie_integrate(x: vector, y: vector, max_gap: f64) -> vector {
    if !magpie_finite(x) { return []; }
    if !magpie_finite(y) { return []; }
    if !(max_gap > 0.0 && max_gap - max_gap == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = magpie_compute(x, y, max_gap);
    if !magpie_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let x = [0, 1, 4];
    let y = [2, 2, 2];
    let max_gap = 2.0;
    let result = magpie_integrate(x, y, max_gap);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
8
2
3
1
```

#### Practice

Change x = [0, 2], y = [0, 2]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [area, span-weighted mean, widest gap, exceeds gap limit]. Rejects duplicate or reversed sample times.

Solution

The result vector is [2, 1, 2, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let x = [0, 1, 4];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let x = [0, 2];
```

Find

```blyx
    let y = [2, 2, 2];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let y = [0, 2];
```

Output after the change

```
2
1
2
0
```

### [Flamingo · Choose chart ticks for an observed range](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/flamingo)

Produce chart-ready axis limits and labeled tick spacing from raw data.

#### Choose chart ticks for an observed range

A constant series collapses a chart axis; raw decimal steps make labels hard to read. Expand the domain before choosing a tick lattice. Including zero extends the data range to 0–11. A five-unit tick step covers that range through 15.

[D3, ticks and steps](https://d3js.org/d3-array/ticks)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-flamingo.git
cd blyx-flamingo
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "3,11" 1 4
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-flamingo/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [first tick, last tick, step, tick count]. The tick count can differ from the requested interval target. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| samples | Vector of: finite number |
| include_zero | nonnegative exact integer |
| intervals | positive exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[AxisRange](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/axisrange) · [TickStep](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/tickstep) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/flamingo)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Flamingo 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-flamingo/tree/v0.1.0

fn axisrange_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn axisrange_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn axisrange_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn axisrange_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn axisrange_compute(samples: vector, zero: f64) -> vector {
    if len(samples) == 0 || zero > 1.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut lo = at(samples, 0);
    let mut hi = lo;
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(samples) {
        lo = axisrange_min2(lo, at(samples, i));
        hi = axisrange_max2(hi, at(samples, i));
        i += 1;
    }
    if zero == 1.0 {
        lo = axisrange_min2(lo, 0.0);
        hi = axisrange_max2(hi, 0.0);
    }
    if hi == lo {
        let pad = axisrange_max2(0.5, axisrange_absolute(lo) * 0.05);
        lo -= pad;
        hi += pad;
    }
    [lo, hi]
}

// Compute a chart domain and expand a constant-valued series.
// Returns [lower, upper]. Set zero to 1 to include the origin. A constant domain receives ±0.5 or ±5% of its magnitude, whichever is larger.
pub fn axisrange_extent(samples: vector, zero: f64) -> vector {
    if !axisrange_finite(samples) { return []; }
    if !(zero >= 0.0 && zero <= 9007199254740991.0 && zero % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = axisrange_compute(samples, zero);
    if !axisrange_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn tickstep_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn tickstep_floorreal(value: f64) -> f64 {
    let trunc = value - value % 1.0;
    if trunc > value {
        return trunc - 1.0;
    }
    trunc
}

fn tickstep_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn tickstep_compute(lo: f64, hi: f64, intervals: f64) -> vector {
    if hi <= lo {
        return [];
    }
    let raw = (hi - lo) / intervals;
    if raw < 1.0e-100 || raw > 1.0e100 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut unit = 1.0;
    while unit * 10.0 <= raw {
        unit *= 10.0;
    }
    while unit > raw {
        unit /= 10.0;
    }
    let ratio = raw / unit;
    let mut step = unit;
    if ratio > 5.0 {
        step *= 10.0;
    } else {
        if ratio > 2.0 {
            step *= 5.0;
        } else {
            if ratio > 1.0 {
                step *= 2.0;
            }
        }
    }
    let first = tickstep_floorreal(lo / step);
    let last = -tickstep_floorreal(-hi / step);
    if tickstep_absolute(first) > 9007199254740991.0 || tickstep_absolute(last) > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    [first * step, last * step, step, last - first + 1.0]
}

// Choose a covering linear tick lattice using steps 1, 2, 5 or 10 times a power of ten.
// Returns [first tick, last tick, step, tick count]. Interval count is a target. Supported raw steps range from 1e-100 to 1e100.
pub fn tickstep_cover(lo: f64, hi: f64, intervals: f64) -> vector {
    if !(lo - lo == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(hi - hi == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(intervals >= 1.0 && intervals <= 9007199254740991.0 && intervals % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = tickstep_compute(lo, hi, intervals);
    if !tickstep_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn flamingo_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn flamingo_compute(samples: vector, include_zero: f64, intervals: f64) -> vector {
    let domain = axisrange_extent(samples, include_zero);
    if len(domain) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    tickstep_cover(at(domain, 0), at(domain, 1), intervals)
}

// Produce chart-ready axis limits and labeled tick spacing from raw data.
// Returns [first tick, last tick, step, tick count]. The tick count can differ from the requested interval target.
pub fn flamingo_axis(samples: vector, include_zero: f64, intervals: f64) -> vector {
    if !flamingo_finite(samples) { return []; }
    if !(include_zero >= 0.0 && include_zero <= 9007199254740991.0 && include_zero % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(intervals >= 1.0 && intervals <= 9007199254740991.0 && intervals % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = flamingo_compute(samples, include_zero, intervals);
    if !flamingo_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let samples = [3, 11];
    let include_zero = 1.0;
    let intervals = 4.0;
    let result = flamingo_axis(samples, include_zero, intervals);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0
15
5
4
```

#### Practice

Change samples = [0, 0], include_zero = 0.0, intervals = 2.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Solution

The result vector is [-0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 3]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.


Replace with

```blyx

```

Find

```blyx
    let include_zero = 1.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let include_zero = 0.0;
```

Find

```blyx
    let intervals = 4.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let intervals = 2.0;
```

Output after the change

```
-0.5
0.5
0.5
3
```

### [Bittern · Decide whether the next database migration can run](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/bittern)

Plan the next migration only after history, fingerprints and dirty state agree.

#### Decide whether the next database migration can run

A version number can match even when a previous migration changed. Check the applied prefix and recorded fingerprints before planning the next step. The two applied versions form an exact prefix with matching fingerprints. Version 5 is ready to apply.

[Flyway, schema history table](https://documentation.red-gate.com/flyway/flyway-concepts/migrations/flyway-schema-history-table)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-bittern.git
cd blyx-bittern
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "1,2,5" "1,2" "10,20" "10,20" 0
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-bittern/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [can apply next, next available version, pending count, changed fingerprints]. This preflight consumes an exported history and executes no SQL. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| available | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| applied | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| expected | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| actual | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| dirty | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[VersionChain](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/versionchain) · [SchemaGuard](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/schemaguard) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/bittern)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Bittern 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-bittern/tree/v0.1.0

fn versionchain_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn versionchain_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn versionchain_compute(available: vector, applied: vector) -> vector {
    if len(applied) > len(available) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(available) {
        if i > 0 && at(available, i) <= at(available, i - 1) {
            return [];
        }
        if i < len(applied) && at(available, i) != at(applied, i) {
            return [];
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    let mut next = -1.0;
    if len(applied) < len(available) {
        next = at(available, len(applied));
    }
    [len(applied), len(available) - len(applied), next]
}

// Validate an applied migration log against a strictly increasing release manifest.
// Returns [applied prefix length, pending count, next version or -1]. Every applied version must match the corresponding release entry.
pub fn versionchain_prefix(available: vector, applied: vector) -> vector {
    if !versionchain_counts(available) { return []; }
    if !versionchain_counts(applied) { return []; }
    let result = versionchain_compute(available, applied);
    if !versionchain_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn schemaguard_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn schemaguard_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn schemaguard_compute(expected: vector, actual: vector) -> vector {
    if len(expected) != len(actual) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut first = -1;
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(expected) {
        if at(expected, i) != at(actual, i) {
            if first < 0 {
                first = i;
            }
            count += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [first, count]
}

// Detect changed fingerprints for previously applied migrations.
// Returns [first mismatch index, mismatch count]. Supply aligned integer fingerprint IDs derived by a trusted host, with one ID per applied migration.
pub fn schemaguard_drift(expected: vector, actual: vector) -> vector {
    if !schemaguard_counts(expected) { return []; }
    if !schemaguard_counts(actual) { return []; }
    let result = schemaguard_compute(expected, actual);
    if !schemaguard_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn bittern_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn bittern_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn bittern_compute(available: vector, applied: vector, expected: vector, actual: vector, dirty: f64) -> vector {
    if dirty > 1.0 || len(expected) != len(applied) {
        return [];
    }
    let chain = versionchain_prefix(available, applied);
    let drift = schemaguard_drift(expected, actual);
    if len(chain) == 0 || len(drift) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut ready = 0;
    if dirty == 0.0 && at(drift, 1) == 0.0 && at(chain, 1) > 0.0 {
        ready = 1;
    }
    [ready, at(chain, 2), at(chain, 1), at(drift, 1)]
}

// Plan the next migration only after history, fingerprints and dirty state agree.
// Returns [can apply next, next available version, pending count, changed fingerprints]. This preflight consumes an exported history and executes no SQL.
pub fn bittern_preflight(available: vector, applied: vector, expected: vector, actual: vector, dirty: f64) -> vector {
    if !bittern_counts(available) { return []; }
    if !bittern_counts(applied) { return []; }
    if !bittern_counts(expected) { return []; }
    if !bittern_counts(actual) { return []; }
    if !(dirty >= 0.0 && dirty <= 9007199254740991.0 && dirty % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = bittern_compute(available, applied, expected, actual, dirty);
    if !bittern_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let available = [1, 2, 5];
    let applied = [1, 2];
    let expected = [10, 20];
    let actual = [10, 20];
    let dirty = 0.0;
    let result = bittern_preflight(available, applied, expected, actual, dirty);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
1
5
1
0
```

#### Practice

Change available = [1, 2], applied = [1], expected = [4], actual = [7]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [can apply next, next available version, pending count, changed fingerprints]. This preflight consumes an exported history and executes no SQL.

Solution

The result vector is [0, 2, 1, 1]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.


Replace with

```blyx

```

Find

```blyx
    let applied = [1, 2];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let applied = [1];
```

Find

```blyx
    let expected = [10, 20];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let expected = [4];
```

Find

```blyx
    let actual = [10, 20];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let actual = [7];
```

Output after the change

```

1

```

### [Grebe · Resume a keyset page from its last emitted key](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/grebe)

Build a repeatable keyset page and return the exact next cursor.

#### Resume a keyset page from its last emitted key

Offset pagination on changing data can repeat records. Validate the ordered key and return the final emitted key for the next request. A cursor between keys selects 20 and 30. Returning 30 lets the next page start at 40.

[PostgreSQL, ordered pagination](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/queries-limit.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-grebe.git
cd blyx-grebe
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "10,20,30,40" 15 2
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-grebe/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [first index, exclusive end, resume key, has more]. On an empty result the input cursor is retained. Supply stable unique numeric keys from a consistent snapshot. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| keys | Vector of: exact signed integer |
| cursor | exact signed integer |
| size | positive exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[KeyOrders](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/keyorders) · [PageCursor](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/pagecursor) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/grebe)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Grebe 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-grebe/tree/v0.1.0

fn keyorders_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn keyorders_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn keyorders_compute(keys: vector) -> vector {
    let mut equal = 0;
    let mut down = 0;
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(keys) {
        if at(keys, i) == at(keys, i - 1) {
            equal += 1;
        }
        if at(keys, i) < at(keys, i - 1) {
            down += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    if equal == 0 && down == 0 {
        return [1, 0, 0];
    }
    [0, equal, down]
}

// Check a cursor key sequence for repeated and descending adjacent values.
// Returns [strictly increasing, adjacent duplicates, descending pairs]. Intended for unique ordered numeric keys.
pub fn keyorders_strict(keys: vector) -> vector {
    if !keyorders_integers(keys) { return []; }
    let result = keyorders_compute(keys);
    if !keyorders_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn pagecursor_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn pagecursor_num(value: i64) -> f64 {
    at([value], 0)
}

fn pagecursor_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn pagecursor_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn pagecursor_compute(keys: vector, cursor: f64, size: f64) -> vector {
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(keys) {
        if at(keys, i) <= at(keys, i - 1) {
            return [];
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    let mut low = 0;
    let mut high = len(keys);
    while low < high {
        let mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
        if at(keys, mid) <= cursor {
            low = mid + 1;
        } else {
            high = mid;
        }
    }
    let end = pagecursor_min2(pagecursor_num(len(keys)), pagecursor_num(low) + size);
    let mut more = 0;
    if end < pagecursor_num(len(keys)) {
        more = 1;
    }
    [low, end, more]
}

// Find a keyset page strictly after a cursor in sorted keys.
// Returns [first index, exclusive end, has more]. Verifies strict ordering, then uses binary search. An absent cursor is valid.
pub fn pagecursor_after(keys: vector, cursor: f64, size: f64) -> vector {
    if !pagecursor_integers(keys) { return []; }
    if !(cursor >= -9007199254740991.0 && cursor <= 9007199254740991.0 && cursor % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(size >= 1.0 && size <= 9007199254740991.0 && size % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = pagecursor_compute(keys, cursor, size);
    if !pagecursor_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn grebe_num(value: i64) -> f64 {
    at([value], 0)
}

fn grebe_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn grebe_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn grebe_compute(keys: vector, cursor: f64, size: f64) -> vector {
    let quality = keyorders_strict(keys);
    if len(quality) == 0 || at(quality, 0) != 1.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let page = pagecursor_after(keys, cursor, size);
    if len(page) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut resume = cursor;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(keys) && grebe_num(i) < at(page, 1) {
        if grebe_num(i) >= at(page, 0) {
            resume = at(keys, i);
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [at(page, 0), at(page, 1), resume, at(page, 2)]
}

// Build a repeatable keyset page and return the exact next cursor.
// Returns [first index, exclusive end, resume key, has more]. On an empty result the input cursor is retained. Supply stable unique numeric keys from a consistent snapshot.
pub fn grebe_page(keys: vector, cursor: f64, size: f64) -> vector {
    if !grebe_integers(keys) { return []; }
    if !(cursor >= -9007199254740991.0 && cursor <= 9007199254740991.0 && cursor % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(size >= 1.0 && size <= 9007199254740991.0 && size % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = grebe_compute(keys, cursor, size);
    if !grebe_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let keys = [10, 20, 30, 40];
    let cursor = 15.0;
    let size = 2.0;
    let result = grebe_page(keys, cursor, size);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
1
3
30
1
```

#### Practice

Change keys = [1, 2], cursor = 3.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [first index, exclusive end, resume key, has more]. On an empty result the input cursor is retained. Supply stable unique numeric keys from a consistent snapshot.

Solution

The result vector is [2, 2, 3, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let keys = [10, 20, 30, 40];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let keys = [1, 2];
```

Find

```blyx
    let cursor = 15.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let cursor = 3.0;
```

Output after the change

```
2
2
3
0
```

### [Dunlin · Audit a parent and child table before import](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/dunlin)

Audit a table export for duplicate parents and orphaned child rows.

#### Audit a parent and child table before import

A child reference can look valid while the parent key is duplicated. Check uniqueness and referential integrity before a bulk import. The parent export repeats ID 1. Two child rows reference the missing ID 2.

[PostgreSQL, unique and foreign key constraints](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-dunlin.git
cd blyx-dunlin
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "1,1,3" "1,2,2"
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-dunlin/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [load acceptable, duplicate parent rows, orphan child rows, first orphan row]. This local check complements database-enforced constraints. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| parents | Vector of: exact signed integer |
| children | Vector of: exact signed integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[KeyDuplicates](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/keyduplicates) · [ForeignMiss](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/foreignmiss) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/dunlin)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Dunlin 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-dunlin/tree/v0.1.0

fn keyduplicates_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn keyduplicates_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn keyduplicates_compute(keys: vector) -> vector {
    let mut duplicates = 0;
    let mut first = -1;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(keys) {
        let mut j = 0;
        while j < i {
            if at(keys, j) == at(keys, i) {
                duplicates += 1;
                if first < 0 {
                    first = i;
                }
                break;
            }
            j += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [duplicates, first, len(keys) - duplicates]
}

// Find repeated primary-key occurrences in an offline table export.
// Returns [duplicate rows beyond first occurrence, first duplicate row, unique keys]. Uses pairwise comparison on a small batch.
pub fn keyduplicates_count(keys: vector) -> vector {
    if !keyduplicates_integers(keys) { return []; }
    let result = keyduplicates_compute(keys);
    if !keyduplicates_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn foreignmiss_hasid(values: vector, key: f64) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        if at(values, i) == key {
            return true;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    false
}

fn foreignmiss_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn foreignmiss_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn foreignmiss_compute(parents: vector, children: vector) -> vector {
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut first = -1;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(children) {
        if !foreignmiss_hasid(parents, at(children, i)) {
            if first < 0 {
                first = i;
            }
            count += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [count, first]
}

// Count child rows referencing absent numeric parent keys.
// Returns [orphan rows, first orphan row]. Repeated child references are checked independently; represent missing/null separately.
pub fn foreignmiss_count(parents: vector, children: vector) -> vector {
    if !foreignmiss_integers(parents) { return []; }
    if !foreignmiss_integers(children) { return []; }
    let result = foreignmiss_compute(parents, children);
    if !foreignmiss_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn dunlin_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn dunlin_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn dunlin_compute(parents: vector, children: vector) -> vector {
    let dup = keyduplicates_count(parents);
    let missing = foreignmiss_count(parents, children);
    if len(dup) == 0 || len(missing) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut ok = 0;
    if at(dup, 0) == 0.0 && at(missing, 0) == 0.0 {
        ok = 1;
    }
    [ok, at(dup, 0), at(missing, 0), at(missing, 1)]
}

// Audit a table export for duplicate parents and orphaned child rows.
// Returns [load acceptable, duplicate parent rows, orphan child rows, first orphan row]. This local check complements database-enforced constraints.
pub fn dunlin_check(parents: vector, children: vector) -> vector {
    if !dunlin_integers(parents) { return []; }
    if !dunlin_integers(children) { return []; }
    let result = dunlin_compute(parents, children);
    if !dunlin_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let parents = [1, 1, 3];
    let children = [1, 2, 2];
    let result = dunlin_check(parents, children);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0
1
2
1
```

#### Practice

Change parents = [1, 3], children = [3, 1]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [load acceptable, duplicate parent rows, orphan child rows, first orphan row]. This local check complements database-enforced constraints.

Solution

The result vector is [1, 0, 0, -1]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let parents = [1, 1, 3];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let parents = [1, 3];
```

Find

```blyx
    let children = [1, 2, 2];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let children = [3, 1];
```

```
0
0
-1
```

### [Sanderling · Carry cache age across a local storage interval](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/sanderling)

Choose a cache serving mode from stored age, local elapsed time and grace policy.

#### Carry cache age across a local storage interval

Starting freshness at zero on every cache hop can keep stale content alive. Carry the stored age forward before applying grace. An entry stored at age eight reaches age thirteen after five more ticks. Three ticks of its stale-serving grace remain.

[IETF RFC 9111, freshness](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html#section-4.2)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-sanderling.git
cd blyx-sanderling
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 8 100 105 10 6 0
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-sanderling/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [mode, current age, ticks until mode changes]. Mode 0 serves fresh, 1 serves under explicit stale grace, and 2 requires validation. The host parses and enforces other cache directives. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| age_at_store | nonnegative finite number |
| stored | nonnegative finite number |
| now | nonnegative finite number |
| lifetime | nonnegative finite number |
| grace | nonnegative finite number |
| mandatory | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[FreshClock](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/freshclock) · [StaleWindow](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/stalewindow) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/sanderling)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Sanderling 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-sanderling/tree/v0.1.0

fn freshclock_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn freshclock_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn freshclock_compute(age_at_store: f64, stored: f64, now: f64, lifetime: f64) -> vector {
    if now < stored {
        return [];
    }
    let age = age_at_store + (now - stored);
    [age, freshclock_max2(0.0, lifetime - age), freshclock_max2(0.0, age - lifetime)]
}

// Advance an already calculated HTTP cache age on a monotonic clock.
// Returns [current age, remaining freshness, stale age]. Supply corrected initial age. Equality with freshness lifetime is stale.
pub fn freshclock_age(age_at_store: f64, stored: f64, now: f64, lifetime: f64) -> vector {
    if !(age_at_store >= 0.0 && age_at_store - age_at_store == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(stored >= 0.0 && stored - stored == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(now >= 0.0 && now - now == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(lifetime >= 0.0 && lifetime - lifetime == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = freshclock_compute(age_at_store, stored, now, lifetime);
    if !freshclock_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn stalewindow_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn stalewindow_compute(age: f64, lifetime: f64, grace: f64, mandatory: f64) -> vector {
    if mandatory > 1.0 {
        return [];
    }
    if age < lifetime {
        return [0, lifetime - age];
    }
    if mandatory == 0.0 && age - lifetime < grace {
        return [1, grace - (age - lifetime)];
    }
    [2, 0]
}

// Classify a cache entry under an explicit stale-serving policy.
// Returns [mode, ticks remaining in current window]. Mode 0 is fresh, 1 is stale within grace, 2 requires validation. Mandatory validation disables grace for stale entries.
pub fn stalewindow_classify(age: f64, lifetime: f64, grace: f64, mandatory: f64) -> vector {
    if !(age >= 0.0 && age - age == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(lifetime >= 0.0 && lifetime - lifetime == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(grace >= 0.0 && grace - grace == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(mandatory >= 0.0 && mandatory <= 9007199254740991.0 && mandatory % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = stalewindow_compute(age, lifetime, grace, mandatory);
    if !stalewindow_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn sanderling_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn sanderling_compute(age_at_store: f64, stored: f64, now: f64, lifetime: f64, grace: f64, mandatory: f64) -> vector {
    let clock = freshclock_age(age_at_store, stored, now, lifetime);
    if len(clock) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let policy = stalewindow_classify(at(clock, 0), lifetime, grace, mandatory);
    if len(policy) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(policy, 0), at(clock, 0), at(policy, 1)]
}

// Choose a cache serving mode from stored age, local elapsed time and grace policy.
// Returns [mode, current age, ticks until mode changes]. Mode 0 serves fresh, 1 serves under explicit stale grace, and 2 requires validation. The host parses and enforces other cache directives.
pub fn sanderling_lookup(age_at_store: f64, stored: f64, now: f64, lifetime: f64, grace: f64, mandatory: f64) -> vector {
    if !(age_at_store >= 0.0 && age_at_store - age_at_store == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(stored >= 0.0 && stored - stored == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(now >= 0.0 && now - now == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(lifetime >= 0.0 && lifetime - lifetime == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(grace >= 0.0 && grace - grace == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(mandatory >= 0.0 && mandatory <= 9007199254740991.0 && mandatory % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = sanderling_compute(age_at_store, stored, now, lifetime, grace, mandatory);
    if !sanderling_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let age_at_store = 8.0;
    let stored = 100.0;
    let now = 105.0;
    let lifetime = 10.0;
    let grace = 6.0;
    let mandatory = 0.0;
    let result = sanderling_lookup(age_at_store, stored, now, lifetime, grace, mandatory);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
1
13
3
```

#### Practice

Change mandatory = 1.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [mode, current age, ticks until mode changes]. Mode 0 serves fresh, 1 serves under explicit stale grace, and 2 requires validation. The host parses and enforces other cache directives.

Solution

The result vector is [2, 13, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let mandatory = 0.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let mandatory = 1.0;
```

Output after the change

```
2
13
0
```

### [Cormorant · Separate packet jitter from a fixed clock offset](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/cormorant)

Separate variation in packet delivery from a constant difference between clocks.

#### Separate packet jitter from a fixed clock offset

Absolute one-way delay depends on clock alignment. Changes in transit can still reveal jitter when the clock offset is stable. Transit changes by 32 ticks. Starting from zero, the one-sixteenth update yields two ticks of smoothed jitter.

[IETF RFC 3550, interarrival jitter](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3550.html#appendix-A.8)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-cormorant.git
cd blyx-cormorant
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0,16" "100,148" 0
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-cormorant/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [transit range, smoothed jitter, adjacent pairs]. Input rows must be in arrival order and use unwrapped sender timestamps. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| sent | Vector of: exact signed integer |
| arrived | Vector of: exact signed integer |
| initial | nonnegative finite number |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[TransitSpan](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/transitspan) · [JitterMean](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/jittermean) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/cormorant)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Cormorant 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-cormorant/tree/v0.1.0

fn transitspan_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn transitspan_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn transitspan_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn transitspan_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn transitspan_compute(sent: vector, arrived: vector) -> vector {
    if len(sent) == 0 || len(sent) != len(arrived) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut lo = at(arrived, 0) - at(sent, 0);
    let mut hi = lo;
    let mut reversed = 0;
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(sent) {
        let d = at(arrived, i) - at(sent, i);
        lo = transitspan_min2(lo, d);
        hi = transitspan_max2(hi, d);
        if at(arrived, i) < at(arrived, i - 1) {
            reversed += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [lo, hi, reversed]
}

// Summarize observed packet transit differences and arrival reorderings.
// Returns [minimum arrival minus send, maximum, backward arrival steps]. Times use the same tick unit and a stable offset between clocks.
pub fn transitspan_profile(sent: vector, arrived: vector) -> vector {
    if !transitspan_integers(sent) { return []; }
    if !transitspan_integers(arrived) { return []; }
    let result = transitspan_compute(sent, arrived);
    if !transitspan_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn jittermean_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn jittermean_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn jittermean_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn jittermean_compute(sent: vector, arrived: vector, initial: f64) -> vector {
    if len(sent) == 0 || len(sent) != len(arrived) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut jitter = initial;
    let mut prev = at(arrived, 0) - at(sent, 0);
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < len(sent) {
        let transit = at(arrived, i) - at(sent, i);
        jitter += (jittermean_absolute(transit - prev) - jitter) / 16.0;
        prev = transit;
        i += 1;
    }
    [jitter, len(sent) - 1]
}

// Estimate interarrival jitter with the RFC 3550 one-sixteenth update.
// Returns [updated jitter, adjacent pairs]. Supply arrival-order packets in the same unwrapped timestamp units; the first observation establishes transit.
pub fn jittermean_rtp(sent: vector, arrived: vector, initial: f64) -> vector {
    if !jittermean_integers(sent) { return []; }
    if !jittermean_integers(arrived) { return []; }
    if !(initial >= 0.0 && initial - initial == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = jittermean_compute(sent, arrived, initial);
    if !jittermean_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn cormorant_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn cormorant_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn cormorant_compute(sent: vector, arrived: vector, initial: f64) -> vector {
    let span = transitspan_profile(sent, arrived);
    if len(span) == 0 || at(span, 2) > 0.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let j = jittermean_rtp(sent, arrived, initial);
    if len(j) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(span, 1) - at(span, 0), at(j, 0), at(j, 1)]
}

// Separate variation in packet delivery from a constant difference between clocks.
// Returns [transit range, smoothed jitter, adjacent pairs]. Input rows must be in arrival order and use unwrapped sender timestamps.
pub fn cormorant_trace(sent: vector, arrived: vector, initial: f64) -> vector {
    if !cormorant_integers(sent) { return []; }
    if !cormorant_integers(arrived) { return []; }
    if !(initial >= 0.0 && initial - initial == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = cormorant_compute(sent, arrived, initial);
    if !cormorant_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let sent = [0, 16];
    let arrived = [100, 148];
    let initial = 0.0;
    let result = cormorant_trace(sent, arrived, initial);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
32
2
1
```

#### Practice

Change sent = [0, 10], arrived = [3, 13]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Solution

The result vector is [0, 0, 1]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx

```

Replace with

```blyx
    let sent = [0, 10];
```

Find

```blyx
    let arrived = [100, 148];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let arrived = [3, 13];
```

Output after the change

```
0
0
```
