
### [Bulbul · Validate required and extra object fields](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/bulbul)

Check required and extra fields in an already parsed object.

#### Validate required and extra object fields

Rejecting unknown fields and enforcing required fields are independent policy choices. Return both diagnostics in one pass through the workflow. The example both omits required field 2 and supplies unrecognized field 9. The report retains both counts.

[JSON Schema, object properties](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/object)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-bulbul.git
cd blyx-bulbul
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "1,9" "1,2" "1,2" 1
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-bulbul/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [accepted, missing count, extra count, first missing ID]. Use an explicit field-name-to-ID map. Closed mode rejects extra fields; required IDs must be in the declared allowed set. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| present | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| allowed | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| required | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| closed | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[AllowFields](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/allowfields) · [RequiredSet](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/requiredset) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/bulbul)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Bulbul 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-bulbul/tree/v0.1.0

fn allowfields_hasid(values: vector, key: f64) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        if at(values, i) == key {
            return true;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    false
}

fn allowfields_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn allowfields_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn allowfields_compute(present: vector, allowed: vector) -> vector {
    let mut extras = 0;
    let mut first = -1;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(present) {
        if !allowfields_hasid(allowed, at(present, i)) {
            if first < 0 {
                first = i;
            }
            extras += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [extras, first]
}

// Find unrecognized fields after mapping schema keys to stable IDs.
// Returns [extra occurrences, first extra position]. Required-property presence is a separate check.
pub fn allowfields_extra(present: vector, allowed: vector) -> vector {
    if !allowfields_counts(present) { return []; }
    if !allowfields_counts(allowed) { return []; }
    let result = allowfields_compute(present, allowed);
    if !allowfields_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn requiredset_hasid(values: vector, key: f64) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        if at(values, i) == key {
            return true;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    false
}

fn requiredset_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn requiredset_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn requiredset_compute(present: vector, required: vector) -> vector {
    let mut missing = 0;
    let mut first = -1.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(required) {
        let id = at(required, i);
        let mut j = 0;
        while j < i {
            if at(required, j) == id {
                return [];
            }
            j += 1;
        }
        if !requiredset_hasid(present, id) {
            if missing == 0 {
                first = id;
            }
            missing += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [missing, first]
}

// Find missing unique required keys in an object shape.
// Returns [missing keys, first missing key ID]. Duplicate requirements are rejected as a malformed schema.
pub fn requiredset_missing(present: vector, required: vector) -> vector {
    if !requiredset_counts(present) { return []; }
    if !requiredset_counts(required) { return []; }
    let result = requiredset_compute(present, required);
    if !requiredset_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn bulbul_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn bulbul_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn bulbul_compute(present: vector, allowed: vector, required: vector, closed: f64) -> vector {
    if closed > 1.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let schema = allowfields_extra(required, allowed);
    if len(schema) == 0 || at(schema, 0) > 0.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let extra = allowfields_extra(present, allowed);
    let needed = requiredset_missing(present, required);
    if len(extra) == 0 || len(needed) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut ok = 0;
    if at(needed, 0) == 0.0 && (closed == 0.0 || at(extra, 0) == 0.0) {
        ok = 1;
    }
    [ok, at(needed, 0), at(extra, 0), at(needed, 1)]
}

// Check required and extra fields in an already parsed object.
// Returns [accepted, missing count, extra count, first missing ID]. Use an explicit field-name-to-ID map. Closed mode rejects extra fields; required IDs must be in the declared allowed set.
pub fn bulbul_shape(present: vector, allowed: vector, required: vector, closed: f64) -> vector {
    if !bulbul_counts(present) { return []; }
    if !bulbul_counts(allowed) { return []; }
    if !bulbul_counts(required) { return []; }
    if !(closed >= 0.0 && closed <= 9007199254740991.0 && closed % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = bulbul_compute(present, allowed, required, closed);
    if !bulbul_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let present = [1, 9];
    let allowed = [1, 2];
    let required = [1, 2];
    let closed = 1.0;
    let result = bulbul_shape(present, allowed, required, closed);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0
1
1
2
```

#### Practice

Change allowed = [1], required = [1], closed = 0.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [accepted, missing count, extra count, first missing ID]. Use an explicit field-name-to-ID map. Closed mode rejects extra fields; required IDs must be in the declared allowed set.

Solution

The result vector is [1, 0, 1, -1]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let allowed = [1, 2];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let allowed = [1];
```

Find

```blyx
    let required = [1, 2];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let required = [1];
```

Find

```blyx
    let closed = 1.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let closed = 0.0;
```

```
1
0
1
-1
```

### [Fantail · Find which settings layer supplied an invalid override](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/fantail)

Resolve a layered setting and report where an invalid override came from.

#### Find which settings layer supplied an invalid override

Treating zero as an absent setting silently restores older values. Carry a presence flag and the identity of the winning layer. The second layer sets the value to 15 and the last layer has no value. The effective override is five above the limit.

[Python, configuration defaults and overrides](https://docs.python.org/3/library/configparser.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-fantail.git
cd blyx-fantail
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "2,15,0" "1,1,0" 5 0 10
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-fantail/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [accepted, selected value, winning layer, distance outside bounds]. An invalid override remains visible for diagnosis. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| values | Vector of: finite number |
| present | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| fallback | finite number |
| minimum | finite number |
| maximum | finite number |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[OptionLayer](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/optionlayer) · [ValueBounds](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/valuebounds) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/fantail)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Fantail 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-fantail/tree/v0.1.0

fn optionlayer_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn optionlayer_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn optionlayer_compute(values: vector, present: vector, fallback: f64) -> vector {
    if len(values) != len(present) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut chosen = fallback;
    let mut layer = -1;
    let mut supplied = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let flag = at(present, i);
        if flag > 1.0 {
            return [];
        }
        if flag == 1.0 {
            chosen = at(values, i);
            layer = i;
            supplied += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [chosen, layer, supplied]
}

// Resolve a numeric setting across ordered configuration layers.
// Returns [effective value, winning layer index, number of supplied values]. Later layers win; presence flags distinguish zero from an unset value.
pub fn optionlayer_resolve(values: vector, present: vector, fallback: f64) -> vector {
    if !optionlayer_finite(values) { return []; }
    if !optionlayer_counts(present) { return []; }
    if !(fallback - fallback == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = optionlayer_compute(values, present, fallback);
    if !optionlayer_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn valuebounds_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn valuebounds_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn valuebounds_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn valuebounds_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn valuebounds_compute(value: f64, minimum: f64, maximum: f64) -> vector {
    if minimum > maximum {
        return [];
    }
    let nearest = valuebounds_min2(valuebounds_max2(value, minimum), maximum);
    if nearest == value {
        return [1, value, 0];
    }
    [0, nearest, valuebounds_absolute(nearest - value)]
}

// Check a numeric setting against inclusive bounds and explain the violation.
// Returns [in bounds, nearest legal value, absolute distance outside]. Reversed bounds are invalid.
pub fn valuebounds_check(value: f64, minimum: f64, maximum: f64) -> vector {
    if !(value - value == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(minimum - minimum == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(maximum - maximum == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = valuebounds_compute(value, minimum, maximum);
    if !valuebounds_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn fantail_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn fantail_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn fantail_compute(values: vector, present: vector, fallback: f64, minimum: f64, maximum: f64) -> vector {
    let layer = optionlayer_resolve(values, present, fallback);
    if len(layer) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let rule = valuebounds_check(at(layer, 0), minimum, maximum);
    if len(rule) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(rule, 0), at(layer, 0), at(layer, 1), at(rule, 2)]
}

// Resolve a layered setting and report where an invalid override came from.
// Returns [accepted, selected value, winning layer, distance outside bounds]. An invalid override remains visible for diagnosis.
pub fn fantail_setting(values: vector, present: vector, fallback: f64, minimum: f64, maximum: f64) -> vector {
    if !fantail_finite(values) { return []; }
    if !fantail_counts(present) { return []; }
    if !(fallback - fallback == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(minimum - minimum == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(maximum - maximum == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = fantail_compute(values, present, fallback, minimum, maximum);
    if !fantail_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let values = [2, 15, 0];
    let present = [1, 1, 0];
    let fallback = 5.0;
    let minimum = 0.0;
    let maximum = 10.0;
    let result = fantail_setting(values, present, fallback, minimum, maximum);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0
15
1
5
```

#### Practice

Change values = [3, 0], present = [1, 1]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Solution

The result vector is [1, 0, 1, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx

```

Replace with

```blyx
    let values = [3, 0];
```

Find

```blyx
    let present = [1, 1, 0];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let present = [1, 1];
```

Output after the change

```
1
0
1
0
```

### [Swallow · Verify a record table before interpreting a byte offset](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/swallow)

Validate an exported payload's declared spans and checksum, then locate a byte.

#### Verify a record table before interpreting a byte offset

A valid byte offset can point into the wrong serialized record if lengths have drifted. Verify the table and payload before interpreting the offset. The payload bytes 65 and 66 yield checksum 12976260. Offset 1 is the first byte of the second record.

[IETF RFC 1950, Adler-32](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1950)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-swallow.git
cd blyx-swallow
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "1,1" "65,66" 1 12976260
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-swallow/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [checksum matches, actual Adler-32, record index, in-record offset]. The sum of payload lengths must equal the byte count. Use a verified cryptographic signature when authenticity is required. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| lengths | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| payload | Vector of: whole byte in [0,255] |
| offset | nonnegative exact integer |
| checksum | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[RecordSpan](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/recordspan) · [AdlerBytes](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/adlerbytes) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/swallow)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Swallow 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-swallow/tree/v0.1.0

fn recordspan_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn recordspan_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn recordspan_compute(lengths: vector, offset: f64) -> vector {
    let mut start = 0.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(lengths) {
        let size = at(lengths, i);
        let end = start + size;
        if end > 9007199254740991.0 {
            return [];
        }
        if offset >= start && offset < end {
            return [i, offset - start, size];
        }
        start = end;
        i += 1;
    }
    if offset == start {
        return [-1, 0, 0];
    }
    []
}

// Locate the nonempty length-prefixed record containing a byte offset.
// Returns [record index, in-record offset, record length]. At end of stream the index is -1; an offset beyond the end is invalid. Lengths describe decoded payload spans.
pub fn recordspan_locate(lengths: vector, offset: f64) -> vector {
    if !recordspan_counts(lengths) { return []; }
    if !(offset >= 0.0 && offset <= 9007199254740991.0 && offset % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = recordspan_compute(lengths, offset);
    if !recordspan_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn adlerbytes_bytes(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 255.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn adlerbytes_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn adlerbytes_compute(bytes: vector) -> vector {
    let mut a = 1.0;
    let mut b = 0.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(bytes) {
        a = (a + at(bytes, i)) % 65521.0;
        b = (b + a) % 65521.0;
        i += 1;
    }
    [b * 65536.0 + a, a, b]
}

// Compute the RFC 1950 Adler-32 checksum over a sequence of bytes.
// Returns [unsigned checksum, rolling low accumulator, rolling high accumulator]. The empty digest is 1. Use for accidental corruption detection.
pub fn adlerbytes_digest(bytes: vector) -> vector {
    if !adlerbytes_bytes(bytes) { return []; }
    let result = adlerbytes_compute(bytes);
    if !adlerbytes_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn swallow_num(value: i64) -> f64 {
    at([value], 0)
}

fn swallow_bytes(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 255.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn swallow_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn swallow_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn swallow_compute(lengths: vector, payload: vector, offset: f64, checksum: f64) -> vector {
    if checksum > 4294967295.0 || sum(lengths) != swallow_num(len(payload)) {
        return [];
    }
    let record = recordspan_locate(lengths, offset);
    let digest = adlerbytes_digest(payload);
    if len(record) == 0 || len(digest) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut same = 0;
    if at(digest, 0) == checksum {
        same = 1;
    }
    [same, at(digest, 0), at(record, 0), at(record, 1)]
}

// Validate an exported payload's declared spans and checksum, then locate a byte.
// Returns [checksum matches, actual Adler-32, record index, in-record offset]. The sum of payload lengths must equal the byte count. Use a verified cryptographic signature when authenticity is required.
pub fn swallow_inspect(lengths: vector, payload: vector, offset: f64, checksum: f64) -> vector {
    if !swallow_counts(lengths) { return []; }
    if !swallow_bytes(payload) { return []; }
    if !(offset >= 0.0 && offset <= 9007199254740991.0 && offset % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(checksum >= 0.0 && checksum <= 9007199254740991.0 && checksum % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = swallow_compute(lengths, payload, offset, checksum);
    if !swallow_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let lengths = [1, 1];
    let payload = [65, 66];
    let offset = 1.0;
    let checksum = 12976260.0;
    let result = swallow_inspect(lengths, payload, offset, checksum);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
1
12976260
1
0
```

#### Practice

Change lengths = [1], payload = [0], offset = 0.0, checksum = 0.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [checksum matches, actual Adler-32, record index, in-record offset]. The sum of payload lengths must equal the byte count. Use a verified cryptographic signature when authenticity is required.

Solution

The result vector is [0, 65537, 0, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx

```

Replace with

```blyx
    let lengths = [1];
```

Find

```blyx
    let payload = [65, 66];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let payload = [0];
```

Find

```blyx
    let offset = 1.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let offset = 0.0;
```

Find

```blyx
    let checksum = 12976260.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let checksum = 0.0;
```

Output after the change

```

65537
0
0
```

### [Lapwing · Paginate a report with indivisible paragraphs](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/lapwing)

Preflight fixed-line document pagination with indivisible paragraphs.

#### Paginate a report with indivisible paragraphs

A report can fit in aggregate yet overflow when a paragraph must stay together. Pack the measured paragraphs into the usable page area. The first two paragraphs fill a ten-line page. Three lines move to the second page and leave seven available there.

[W3C, CSS fragmentation](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-break-3/)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-lapwing.git
cd blyx-lapwing
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "4,6,3" 120 10 10 10
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-lapwing/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [pages, lines used on final page, unused line slots, printable lines per page]. Blocks are positive paragraph line counts. The host measures text and renders the resulting pages. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| blocks | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| paper | positive finite number |
| top | nonnegative finite number |
| bottom | nonnegative finite number |
| line | positive finite number |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[PageBreaks](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/pagebreaks) · [LineFit](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/linefit) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/lapwing)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Lapwing 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-lapwing/tree/v0.1.0

fn pagebreaks_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn pagebreaks_num(value: i64) -> f64 {
    at([value], 0)
}

fn pagebreaks_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn pagebreaks_magnitudes(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn pagebreaks_compute(heights: vector, page: f64) -> vector {
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut used = 0.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(heights) {
        let h = at(heights, i);
        if h <= 0.0 || h > page {
            return [];
        }
        if pages == 0 || used + h > page {
            pages += 1;
            used = 0.0;
        }
        used += h;
        i += 1;
    }
    [pages, used, pagebreaks_max2(0.0, pagebreaks_num(pages) * page - sum(heights))]
}

// Place unsplittable document blocks on successive pages in input order.
// Returns [pages used, occupied height on final page, total unused height]. Positive block heights must fit individually. Empty input uses zero pages.
pub fn pagebreaks_pack(heights: vector, page: f64) -> vector {
    if !pagebreaks_magnitudes(heights) { return []; }
    if !(page > 0.0 && page - page == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = pagebreaks_compute(heights, page);
    if !pagebreaks_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn linefit_floorpos(value: f64) -> f64 {
    value - value % 1.0
}

fn linefit_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn linefit_compute(paper: f64, top: f64, bottom: f64, line: f64) -> vector {
    let area = paper - top - bottom;
    if area <= 0.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let lines = linefit_floorpos(area / line);
    [area, lines, area - lines * line]
}

// Compute the usable print area and whole lines per page.
// Returns [usable height, whole-line capacity, residual height]. All dimensions use the same unit; a page with no usable height is invalid.
pub fn linefit_capacity(paper: f64, top: f64, bottom: f64, line: f64) -> vector {
    if !(paper > 0.0 && paper - paper == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(top >= 0.0 && top - top == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(bottom >= 0.0 && bottom - bottom == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(line > 0.0 && line - line == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = linefit_compute(paper, top, bottom, line);
    if !linefit_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn lapwing_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn lapwing_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn lapwing_compute(blocks: vector, paper: f64, top: f64, bottom: f64, line: f64) -> vector {
    let area = linefit_capacity(paper, top, bottom, line);
    if len(area) == 0 || at(area, 1) < 1.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let pages = pagebreaks_pack(blocks, at(area, 1));
    if len(pages) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(pages, 0), at(pages, 1), at(pages, 2), at(area, 1)]
}

// Preflight fixed-line document pagination with indivisible paragraphs.
// Returns [pages, lines used on final page, unused line slots, printable lines per page]. Blocks are positive paragraph line counts. The host measures text and renders the resulting pages.
pub fn lapwing_paginate(blocks: vector, paper: f64, top: f64, bottom: f64, line: f64) -> vector {
    if !lapwing_counts(blocks) { return []; }
    if !(paper > 0.0 && paper - paper == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(top >= 0.0 && top - top == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(bottom >= 0.0 && bottom - bottom == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(line > 0.0 && line - line == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = lapwing_compute(blocks, paper, top, bottom, line);
    if !lapwing_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let blocks = [4, 6, 3];
    let paper = 120.0;
    let top = 10.0;
    let bottom = 10.0;
    let line = 10.0;
    let result = lapwing_paginate(blocks, paper, top, bottom, line);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
2
3
7
10
```

#### Practice

Change blocks = [], paper = 40.0, top = 0.0, bottom = 0.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

### [Hoopoe · Check a thumbnail buffer before allocation](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/hoopoe)

Plan a thumbnail and check the decoded pixel buffer against a byte budget.

#### Check a thumbnail buffer before allocation

Encoded file size gives a poor estimate of decoded thumbnail memory. Account for output dimensions and scanline padding before allocating. A 400×200 image fits into 100×50 pixels. Three channels and four-byte alignment require 15,000 bytes, above the given budget.

[Pillow, aspect-preserving containment](https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/ImageOps.html#PIL.ImageOps.contain)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-hoopoe.git
cd blyx-hoopoe
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 400 200 100 100 3 4 14000
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-hoopoe/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [output width, output height, aligned stride, bytes, fits budget]. Includes one output buffer with one byte per channel. Decoder and encoder overhead are outside this estimate. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| width | positive exact integer |
| height | positive exact integer |
| box_w | positive exact integer |
| box_h | positive exact integer |
| channels | positive exact integer |
| align | positive exact integer |
| memory | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[AspectFit](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/aspectfit) · [RasterBytes](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/rasterbytes) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/hoopoe)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Hoopoe 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-hoopoe/tree/v0.1.0

fn aspectfit_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn aspectfit_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn aspectfit_floorpos(value: f64) -> f64 {
    value - value % 1.0
}

fn aspectfit_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn aspectfit_compute(width: f64, height: f64, box_w: f64, box_h: f64, upscale: f64) -> vector {
    if upscale > 1.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut scale = aspectfit_min2(box_w / width, box_h / height);
    if upscale == 0.0 {
        scale = aspectfit_min2(scale, 1.0);
    }
    [aspectfit_max2(1.0, aspectfit_min2(box_w, aspectfit_floorpos(width * scale))), aspectfit_max2(1.0, aspectfit_min2(box_h, aspectfit_floorpos(height * scale))), scale]
}

// Fit an image inside a box while preserving aspect ratio.
// Returns [integer output width, height, scale]. Downward rounding and a one-pixel minimum preserve a nonempty raster. Set upscale to 0 to keep small images at native size.
pub fn aspectfit_contain(width: f64, height: f64, box_w: f64, box_h: f64, upscale: f64) -> vector {
    if !(width >= 1.0 && width <= 9007199254740991.0 && width % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(height >= 1.0 && height <= 9007199254740991.0 && height % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(box_w >= 1.0 && box_w <= 9007199254740991.0 && box_w % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(box_h >= 1.0 && box_h <= 9007199254740991.0 && box_h % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(upscale >= 0.0 && upscale <= 9007199254740991.0 && upscale % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = aspectfit_compute(width, height, box_w, box_h, upscale);
    if !aspectfit_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn rasterbytes_ceilpos(value: f64) -> f64 {
    let rest = value % 1.0;
    if rest > 0.0 {
        return value - rest + 1.0;
    }
    value
}

fn rasterbytes_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn rasterbytes_compute(width: f64, height: f64, channels: f64, alignment: f64) -> vector {
    let raw = width * channels;
    let stride = rasterbytes_ceilpos(raw / alignment) * alignment;
    let bytes = stride * height;
    if bytes > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    [raw, stride, bytes]
}

// Estimate uncompressed raster storage with aligned scanlines.
// Returns [bytes per unpadded row, aligned stride, total bytes]. Each channel takes one byte. Counts must stay in the exact integer range.
pub fn rasterbytes_storage(width: f64, height: f64, channels: f64, alignment: f64) -> vector {
    if !(width >= 1.0 && width <= 9007199254740991.0 && width % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(height >= 1.0 && height <= 9007199254740991.0 && height % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(channels >= 1.0 && channels <= 9007199254740991.0 && channels % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(alignment >= 1.0 && alignment <= 9007199254740991.0 && alignment % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = rasterbytes_compute(width, height, channels, alignment);
    if !rasterbytes_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn hoopoe_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn hoopoe_compute(width: f64, height: f64, box_w: f64, box_h: f64, channels: f64, align: f64, memory: f64) -> vector {
    let fit = aspectfit_contain(width, height, box_w, box_h, 0.0);
    if len(fit) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let cost = rasterbytes_storage(at(fit, 0), at(fit, 1), channels, align);
    if len(cost) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut ok = 0;
    if at(cost, 2) <= memory {
        ok = 1;
    }
    [at(fit, 0), at(fit, 1), at(cost, 1), at(cost, 2), ok]
}

// Plan a thumbnail and check the decoded pixel buffer against a byte budget.
// Returns [output width, output height, aligned stride, bytes, fits budget]. Includes one output buffer with one byte per channel. Decoder and encoder overhead are outside this estimate.
pub fn hoopoe_thumbnail(width: f64, height: f64, box_w: f64, box_h: f64, channels: f64, align: f64, memory: f64) -> vector {
    if !(width >= 1.0 && width <= 9007199254740991.0 && width % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(height >= 1.0 && height <= 9007199254740991.0 && height % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(box_w >= 1.0 && box_w <= 9007199254740991.0 && box_w % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(box_h >= 1.0 && box_h <= 9007199254740991.0 && box_h % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(channels >= 1.0 && channels <= 9007199254740991.0 && channels % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(align >= 1.0 && align <= 9007199254740991.0 && align % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(memory >= 0.0 && memory <= 9007199254740991.0 && memory % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = hoopoe_compute(width, height, box_w, box_h, channels, align, memory);
    if !hoopoe_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let width = 400.0;
    let height = 200.0;
    let box_w = 100.0;
    let box_h = 100.0;
    let channels = 3.0;
    let align = 4.0;
    let memory = 14000.0;
    let result = hoopoe_thumbnail(width, height, box_w, box_h, channels, align, memory);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
100
50
300
15000
0
```

```blyx
    let box_w = 100.0;
```

Replace with


Find


Replace with


### [Spoonbill · Detect overlapping captions in a rational time base](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/spoonbill)

Preflight caption cue timings against an explicit overlap policy.

#### Detect overlapping captions in a rational time base

Two cues touching at one endpoint are consecutive; two cues occupying the same frame overlap. Apply a policy using exact tick boundaries. At 30 ticks per second the track spans two seconds. The second cue begins before the first one finishes.

[W3C, WebVTT cues](https://www.w3.org/TR/webvtt1/)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-spoonbill.git
cd blyx-spoonbill
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0,20" "30,60" 1 30 0
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-spoonbill/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [accepted, overlapping cue count, first overlap index, cue-track span in seconds]. Some subtitle tracks allow overlaps; the caller chooses the policy. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| starts | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| ends | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| numerator | positive exact integer |
| denominator | positive exact integer |
| allow_overlap | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[TimeBase](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/timebase) · [CueOverlap](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/cueoverlap) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/spoonbill)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Spoonbill 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-spoonbill/tree/v0.1.0

fn timebase_floorpos(value: f64) -> f64 {
    value - value % 1.0
}

fn timebase_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn timebase_compute(tick: f64, numerator: f64, denominator: f64) -> vector {
    let seconds = (tick / denominator) * numerator;
    let whole = timebase_floorpos(seconds);
    [seconds, whole, seconds - whole]
}

// Convert a nonnegative frame tick to seconds using a rational time base.
// Returns [seconds, whole seconds, fractional remainder]. numerator/denominator is seconds per tick.
pub fn timebase_frame(tick: f64, numerator: f64, denominator: f64) -> vector {
    if !(tick >= 0.0 && tick <= 9007199254740991.0 && tick % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(numerator >= 1.0 && numerator <= 9007199254740991.0 && numerator % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(denominator >= 1.0 && denominator <= 9007199254740991.0 && denominator % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = timebase_compute(tick, numerator, denominator);
    if !timebase_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn cueoverlap_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn cueoverlap_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn cueoverlap_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn cueoverlap_compute(starts: vector, ends: vector) -> vector {
    if len(starts) != len(ends) {
        return [];
    }
    if len(starts) == 0 {
        return [0, -1, 0];
    }
    let mut furthest = at(starts, 0);
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut first = -1;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(starts) {
        let a = at(starts, i);
        let b = at(ends, i);
        if b <= a || (i > 0 && a < at(starts, i - 1)) {
            return [];
        }
        if a < furthest {
            if first < 0 {
                first = i;
            }
            count += 1;
        }
        furthest = cueoverlap_max2(furthest, b);
        i += 1;
    }
    [count, first, furthest - at(starts, 0)]
}

// Audit a sorted list of half-open subtitle cue intervals.
// Returns [cues that start before a previous cue has ended, first overlapping cue index, total span in ticks]. Rejects nonpositive durations and unsorted starts.
pub fn cueoverlap_trace(starts: vector, ends: vector) -> vector {
    if !cueoverlap_counts(starts) { return []; }
    if !cueoverlap_counts(ends) { return []; }
    let result = cueoverlap_compute(starts, ends);
    if !cueoverlap_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn spoonbill_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn spoonbill_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn spoonbill_compute(starts: vector, ends: vector, numerator: f64, denominator: f64, allow_overlap: f64) -> vector {
    if allow_overlap > 1.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let cues = cueoverlap_trace(starts, ends);
    if len(cues) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let duration = timebase_frame(at(cues, 2), numerator, denominator);
    if len(duration) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut ok = 0;
    if allow_overlap == 1.0 || at(cues, 0) == 0.0 {
        ok = 1;
    }
    [ok, at(cues, 0), at(cues, 1), at(duration, 0)]
}

// Preflight caption cue timings against an explicit overlap policy.
// Returns [accepted, overlapping cue count, first overlap index, cue-track span in seconds]. Some subtitle tracks allow overlaps; the caller chooses the policy.
pub fn spoonbill_captions(starts: vector, ends: vector, numerator: f64, denominator: f64, allow_overlap: f64) -> vector {
    if !spoonbill_counts(starts) { return []; }
    if !spoonbill_counts(ends) { return []; }
    if !(numerator >= 1.0 && numerator <= 9007199254740991.0 && numerator % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(denominator >= 1.0 && denominator <= 9007199254740991.0 && denominator % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(allow_overlap >= 0.0 && allow_overlap <= 9007199254740991.0 && allow_overlap % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = spoonbill_compute(starts, ends, numerator, denominator, allow_overlap);
    if !spoonbill_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let starts = [0, 20];
    let ends = [30, 60];
    let numerator = 1.0;
    let denominator = 30.0;
    let allow_overlap = 0.0;
    let result = spoonbill_captions(starts, ends, numerator, denominator, allow_overlap);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
0
1
1
2
```

#### Practice

Change allow_overlap = 1.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [accepted, overlapping cue count, first overlap index, cue-track span in seconds]. Some subtitle tracks allow overlaps; the caller chooses the policy.

Solution

The result vector is [1, 1, 1, 2]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let allow_overlap = 0.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let allow_overlap = 1.0;
```

Output after the change

```

1
1
2
```

### [Raven · Budget a log buffer during an error burst](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/raven)

Budget a bounded log buffer while preserving higher-severity events first.

#### Budget a log buffer during an error burst

A burst of low-severity messages can consume all available slots. Quantify how much high-severity evidence a bounded buffer would retain. Three records cross the importance threshold, but the buffer has two slots. One high-severity record must be dropped.

[OpenTelemetry, logs data model](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/logs/data-model/)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-raven.git
cd blyx-raven
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "9,17,9,21,21" 17 2
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-raven/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [important retained, ordinary retained, dropped, high-severity drops]. Use the plan to allocate slots in a host logger. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| severity | Vector of: nonnegative exact integer |
| threshold | nonnegative exact integer |
| capacity | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[EventLevels](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/eventlevels) · [SampleQuota](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/samplequota) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/raven)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Raven 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-raven/tree/v0.1.0

fn eventlevels_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn eventlevels_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn eventlevels_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn eventlevels_compute(severity: vector, threshold: f64) -> vector {
    if threshold > 24.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut first = -1;
    let mut peak = -1.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(severity) {
        let level = at(severity, i);
        if level > 24.0 {
            return [];
        }
        peak = eventlevels_max2(peak, level);
        if level >= threshold {
            if first < 0 {
                first = i;
            }
            count += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [count, peak, first]
}

// Count log records at or above an OpenTelemetry severity number.
// Returns [qualifying records, greatest severity, first qualifying index]. Valid severity numbers are 0–24, with 0 unspecified. Empty streams use -1 for the maximum.
pub fn eventlevels_count(severity: vector, threshold: f64) -> vector {
    if !eventlevels_counts(severity) { return []; }
    if !(threshold >= 0.0 && threshold <= 9007199254740991.0 && threshold % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = eventlevels_compute(severity, threshold);
    if !eventlevels_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn samplequota_min2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn samplequota_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn samplequota_compute(important: f64, ordinary: f64, capacity: f64) -> vector {
    if important + ordinary > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let first = samplequota_min2(important, capacity);
    let rest = samplequota_min2(ordinary, capacity - first);
    [first, rest, important + ordinary - first - rest]
}

// Allocate a bounded log buffer with higher priority for important records.
// Returns [important retained, ordinary retained, dropped]. This computes counts for a host that selects individual records in arrival order.
pub fn samplequota_plan(important: f64, ordinary: f64, capacity: f64) -> vector {
    if !(important >= 0.0 && important <= 9007199254740991.0 && important % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(ordinary >= 0.0 && ordinary <= 9007199254740991.0 && ordinary % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(capacity >= 0.0 && capacity <= 9007199254740991.0 && capacity % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = samplequota_compute(important, ordinary, capacity);
    if !samplequota_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn raven_num(value: i64) -> f64 {
    at([value], 0)
}

fn raven_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn raven_counts(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= 0.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn raven_compute(severity: vector, threshold: f64, capacity: f64) -> vector {
    let levels = eventlevels_count(severity, threshold);
    if len(levels) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let important = at(levels, 0);
    let slots = samplequota_plan(important, raven_num(len(severity)) - important, capacity);
    if len(slots) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(slots, 0), at(slots, 1), at(slots, 2), important - at(slots, 0)]
}

// Budget a bounded log buffer while preserving higher-severity events first.
// Returns [important retained, ordinary retained, dropped, high-severity drops]. Use the plan to allocate slots in a host logger.
pub fn raven_buffer(severity: vector, threshold: f64, capacity: f64) -> vector {
    if !raven_counts(severity) { return []; }
    if !(threshold >= 0.0 && threshold <= 9007199254740991.0 && threshold % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(capacity >= 0.0 && capacity <= 9007199254740991.0 && capacity % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = raven_compute(severity, threshold, capacity);
    if !raven_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let severity = [9, 17, 9, 21, 21];
    let threshold = 17.0;
    let capacity = 2.0;
    let result = raven_buffer(severity, threshold, capacity);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
2
0
3
1
```

#### Practice

Change severity = [9, 17, 9]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [important retained, ordinary retained, dropped, high-severity drops]. Use the plan to allocate slots in a host logger.

Solution

The result vector is [1, 1, 1, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let severity = [9, 17, 9, 21, 21];
```

Replace with

```blyx

```

```

1
1
0
```

### [Robin · Convert a civil date into comparable day numbers](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/robin)

Convert a validated civil date into an ordinal, weekday and comparable day number.

#### Convert a civil date into comparable day numbers

Month lengths and century leap rules affect both date validation and weekday calculations. Resolve both from the same Gregorian day number. January 1, 1970 has day number 719163 and Monday-zero weekday 3. Century years follow the full Gregorian leap rule.

[Python, proleptic Gregorian calendar](https://docs.python.org/3/library/calendar.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-robin.git
cd blyx-robin
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 1970 1 1
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-robin/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [day number with 0001-01-01 = 1, Monday-zero weekday, day-of-year, days in month]. This is a calendar computation independent of machine locale. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| year | positive exact integer |
| month | positive exact integer |
| day | positive exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[GregorianDay](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/gregorianday) · [YearOrigin](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/yearorigin) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/robin)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Robin 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-robin/tree/v0.1.0

fn gregorianday_num(value: i64) -> f64 {
    at([value], 0)
}

fn gregorianday_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn gregorianday_compute(year: f64, month: f64, day: f64) -> vector {
    if year > 9999.0 || month > 12.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let mut leap = 0.0;
    if year % 4.0 == 0.0 && (year % 100.0 != 0.0 || year % 400.0 == 0.0) {
        leap = 1.0;
    }
    let months = [31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31];
    let mut i = 0;
    let mut ordinal = day;
    while gregorianday_num(i) + 1.0 < month {
        ordinal += at(months, i);
        if i == 1 {
            ordinal += leap;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    let mut limit = at(months, i);
    if i == 1 {
        limit += leap;
    }
    if day > limit {
        return [];
    }
    [ordinal, leap, limit]
}

// Validate a proleptic Gregorian date and calculate its day-of-year.
// Returns [ordinal starting at 1, leap-year flag, days in month]. Supported years are 1–9999.
pub fn gregorianday_ordinal(year: f64, month: f64, day: f64) -> vector {
    if !(year >= 1.0 && year <= 9007199254740991.0 && year % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(month >= 1.0 && month <= 9007199254740991.0 && month % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(day >= 1.0 && day <= 9007199254740991.0 && day % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = gregorianday_compute(year, month, day);
    if !gregorianday_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn yearorigin_floorpos(value: f64) -> f64 {
    value - value % 1.0
}

fn yearorigin_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn yearorigin_compute(year: f64) -> vector {
    if year > 9999.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let y = year - 1.0;
    let days = y * 365.0 + yearorigin_floorpos(y / 4.0) - yearorigin_floorpos(y / 100.0) + yearorigin_floorpos(y / 400.0);
    [days, days % 7.0]
}

// Count Gregorian days before January 1 of a year.
// Returns [days before year, weekday of January 1]. Monday is zero; year 1 begins on Monday. Supported years are 1–9999.
pub fn yearorigin_offset(year: f64) -> vector {
    if !(year >= 1.0 && year <= 9007199254740991.0 && year % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = yearorigin_compute(year);
    if !yearorigin_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn robin_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn robin_compute(year: f64, month: f64, day: f64) -> vector {
    let date = gregorianday_ordinal(year, month, day);
    let origin = yearorigin_offset(year);
    if len(date) == 0 || len(origin) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    let index = at(origin, 0) + at(date, 0);
    [index, (index - 1.0) % 7.0, at(date, 0), at(date, 2)]
}

// Convert a validated civil date into an ordinal, weekday and comparable day number.
// Returns [day number with 0001-01-01 = 1, Monday-zero weekday, day-of-year, days in month]. This is a calendar computation independent of machine locale.
pub fn robin_date(year: f64, month: f64, day: f64) -> vector {
    if !(year >= 1.0 && year <= 9007199254740991.0 && year % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(month >= 1.0 && month <= 9007199254740991.0 && month % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(day >= 1.0 && day <= 9007199254740991.0 && day % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = robin_compute(year, month, day);
    if !robin_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let year = 1970.0;
    let month = 1.0;
    let day = 1.0;
    let result = robin_date(year, month, day);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
719163
3
1
31
```

#### Practice

Change year = 1.0. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [day number with 0001-01-01 = 1, Monday-zero weekday, day-of-year, days in month]. This is a calendar computation independent of machine locale.

Solution

The result vector is [1, 0, 1, 31]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let year = 1970.0;
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let year = 1.0;
```

```

0
1

```

### [Starling · Size a resource pool from overlapping bookings](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/starling)

Estimate resource capacity and actual occupied time from a booking schedule.

#### Size a resource pool from overlapping bookings

Summing all booking durations double-counts overlap. Measure occupied time separately from peak resource demand. Three bookings cover seven ticks and reach two simultaneous users. A pool of one is short by one resource.

[PostgreSQL, range types](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/rangetypes.html)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-starling.git
cd blyx-starling
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0,2,4" "4,5,7" 1
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-starling/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [covered ticks, peak simultaneous bookings, earliest peak, capacity shortfall]. Starts must be sorted; adjacent bookings can share a resource. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| starts | Vector of: exact signed integer |
| ends | Vector of: exact signed integer |
| capacity | positive exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[IntervalUnion](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/intervalunion) · [PeakSlots](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/peakslots) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/starling)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Starling 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-starling/tree/v0.1.0

fn intervalunion_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn intervalunion_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn intervalunion_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn intervalunion_compute(starts: vector, ends: vector) -> vector {
    if len(starts) != len(ends) {
        return [];
    }
    if len(starts) == 0 {
        return [0, 0, 0];
    }
    let mut end = at(starts, 0);
    let mut length = 0.0;
    let mut components = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(starts) {
        let a = at(starts, i);
        let b = at(ends, i);
        if b <= a || (i > 0 && a < at(starts, i - 1)) {
            return [];
        }
        if i == 0 || a > end {
            components += 1;
        }
        length += intervalunion_max2(0.0, b - intervalunion_max2(a, end));
        end = intervalunion_max2(end, b);
        i += 1;
    }
    [length, components, end - at(starts, 0)]
}

// Measure union length and coverage components of sorted half-open intervals.
// Returns [covered ticks, connected components, enclosing span]. Touching intervals are merged. Empty input has zero span.
pub fn intervalunion_measure(starts: vector, ends: vector) -> vector {
    if !intervalunion_integers(starts) { return []; }
    if !intervalunion_integers(ends) { return []; }
    let result = intervalunion_compute(starts, ends);
    if !intervalunion_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn peakslots_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn peakslots_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn peakslots_compute(starts: vector, ends: vector) -> vector {
    if len(starts) != len(ends) {
        return [];
    }
    let mut best = 0;
    let mut when = 0.0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(starts) {
        if at(ends, i) <= at(starts, i) {
            return [];
        }
        let t = at(starts, i);
        let mut count = 0;
        let mut j = 0;
        while j < len(starts) {
            if at(starts, j) <= t && t < at(ends, j) {
                count += 1;
            }
            j += 1;
        }
        if count > best || (count == best && t < when) {
            best = count;
            when = t;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    [best, when]
}

// Find peak simultaneous occupancy of half-open intervals.
// Returns [peak active intervals, earliest tick at that peak]. Empty input returns [0,0]. Counts exactly at starts, where occupancy can increase; short batches use quadratic time.
pub fn peakslots_overlap(starts: vector, ends: vector) -> vector {
    if !peakslots_integers(starts) { return []; }
    if !peakslots_integers(ends) { return []; }
    let result = peakslots_compute(starts, ends);
    if !peakslots_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn starling_max2(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b {
        return a;
    }
    b
}

fn starling_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn starling_integers(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value >= -9007199254740991.0 && value <= 9007199254740991.0 && value % 1.0 == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn starling_compute(starts: vector, ends: vector, capacity: f64) -> vector {
    let union = intervalunion_measure(starts, ends);
    let peak = peakslots_overlap(starts, ends);
    if len(union) == 0 || len(peak) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(union, 0), at(peak, 0), at(peak, 1), starling_max2(0.0, at(peak, 0) - capacity)]
}

// Estimate resource capacity and actual occupied time from a booking schedule.
// Returns [covered ticks, peak simultaneous bookings, earliest peak, capacity shortfall]. Starts must be sorted; adjacent bookings can share a resource.
pub fn starling_capacity(starts: vector, ends: vector, capacity: f64) -> vector {
    if !starling_integers(starts) { return []; }
    if !starling_integers(ends) { return []; }
    if !(capacity >= 1.0 && capacity <= 9007199254740991.0 && capacity % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = starling_compute(starts, ends, capacity);
    if !starling_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let starts = [0, 2, 4];
    let ends = [4, 5, 7];
    let capacity = 1.0;
    let result = starling_capacity(starts, ends, capacity);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
7
2
2
1
```

#### Practice

Change starts = [1, 3], ends = [3, 5]. Predict the result, then run the program.

Hint

Returns [covered ticks, peak simultaneous bookings, earliest peak, capacity shortfall]. Starts must be sorted; adjacent bookings can share a resource.

Solution

The result vector is [4, 1, 1, 0]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.

Find

```blyx
    let starts = [0, 2, 4];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let starts = [1, 3];
```

Find

```blyx
    let ends = [4, 5, 7];
```

Replace with

```blyx
    let ends = [3, 5];
```

```

1
1
0
```

### [Blackbird · Resolve both occurrences of an ambiguous wall time](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/blackbird)

Resolve a wall-clock timestamp at a known gap or fold without guessing its offset.

#### Resolve both occurrences of an ambiguous wall time

One wall time can occur twice during a fall-back transition and disappear entirely during a forward jump. Expose the number of valid UTC candidates. After the offset moves back, local tick 11000 has two UTC candidates. Fold 1 selects the later occurrence.

[PEP 495, local time disambiguation](https://peps.python.org/pep-0495/)

#### Run the framework with your own input

Install Blyx 0.2.1 and a Rust toolchain with a host linker, then run the versioned project. Each positional argument is a number or a comma-separated numerical vector. The CLI accepts up to 16 entries per vector. The imported module accepts longer inputs.

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-blackbird.git
cd blyx-blackbird
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 11000 10000 3600 0 1
```

[Project source](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-blackbird/blob/v0.1.0/project.blyx) · [Native CLI downloads](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/releases/tag/ecosystem-v0.1.0)

#### API and return values

Returns [candidate count, selected UTC, selected offset]. For a gap the latter two values are zero. Fold 0 chooses the earlier occurrence and fold 1 the later. Supply transition data from a trusted timezone database. Invalid input returns an empty vector.

| Argument | Accepted input |
| --- | --- |
| local | exact signed integer |
| transition | exact signed integer |
| before | exact signed integer |
| after | exact signed integer |
| fold | nonnegative exact integer |

#### Use the libraries independently

The framework vendors the same library source published in these two repositories. Each module has its own package page, input contract and regression suite.

[CivilOffset](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/civiloffset) · [ClockFold](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/clockfold) · [Framework installation](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages/blackbird)

#### Worked program

```blyx
// Blackbird 0.1.0 · MIT OR Apache-2.0
// https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-blackbird/tree/v0.1.0

fn civiloffset_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn civiloffset_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn civiloffset_compute(local: f64, offset: f64) -> vector {
    if civiloffset_absolute(offset) >= 86400.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let utc = local - offset;
    if civiloffset_absolute(utc) > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    [utc, offset]
}

// Convert a local tick to a candidate UTC tick for a supplied offset.
// Returns [candidate UTC, offset]. Offsets use seconds and must lie strictly within ±24 hours. Local ticks use the same epoch and unit.
pub fn civiloffset_candidate(local: f64, offset: f64) -> vector {
    if !(local >= -9007199254740991.0 && local <= 9007199254740991.0 && local % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(offset >= -9007199254740991.0 && offset <= 9007199254740991.0 && offset % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = civiloffset_compute(local, offset);
    if !civiloffset_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn clockfold_absolute(value: f64) -> f64 {
    if value < 0.0 {
        return - value;
    }
    value
}

fn clockfold_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn clockfold_compute(local: f64, transition: f64, before: f64, after: f64) -> vector {
    if clockfold_absolute(before) >= 86400.0 || clockfold_absolute(after) >= 86400.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let old = local - before;
    let next = local - after;
    if clockfold_absolute(old) > 9007199254740991.0 || clockfold_absolute(next) > 9007199254740991.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let a = old < transition;
    let b = next >= transition;
    if a && b {
        return [2, old, next];
    }
    if a {
        return [1, old, old];
    }
    if b {
        return [1, next, next];
    }
    [0, 0, 0]
}

// Classify a local time around one supplied offset transition.
// Returns [number of valid UTC candidates, earliest candidate, latest candidate]. A forward gap yields [0,0,0]; a backward fold yields two candidates.
pub fn clockfold_classify(local: f64, transition: f64, before: f64, after: f64) -> vector {
    if !(local >= -9007199254740991.0 && local <= 9007199254740991.0 && local % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(transition >= -9007199254740991.0 && transition <= 9007199254740991.0 && transition % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(before >= -9007199254740991.0 && before <= 9007199254740991.0 && before % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(after >= -9007199254740991.0 && after <= 9007199254740991.0 && after % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = clockfold_compute(local, transition, before, after);
    if !clockfold_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn blackbird_finite(values: vector) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(values) {
        let value = at(values, i);
        if !(value - value == 0.0) {
            return false;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    true
}

fn blackbird_compute(local: f64, transition: f64, before: f64, after: f64, fold: f64) -> vector {
    if fold > 1.0 {
        return [];
    }
    let c = clockfold_classify(local, transition, before, after);
    if len(c) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    if at(c, 0) == 0.0 {
        return [0, 0, 0];
    }
    let mut utc = at(c, 1);
    if fold == 1.0 {
        utc = at(c, 2);
    }
    let offset = local - utc;
    let point = civiloffset_candidate(local, offset);
    if len(point) == 0 {
        return [];
    }
    [at(c, 0), at(point, 0), at(point, 1)]
}

// Resolve a wall-clock timestamp at a known gap or fold without guessing its offset.
// Returns [candidate count, selected UTC, selected offset]. For a gap the latter two values are zero. Fold 0 chooses the earlier occurrence and fold 1 the later. Supply transition data from a trusted timezone database.
pub fn blackbird_resolve(local: f64, transition: f64, before: f64, after: f64, fold: f64) -> vector {
    if !(local >= -9007199254740991.0 && local <= 9007199254740991.0 && local % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(transition >= -9007199254740991.0 && transition <= 9007199254740991.0 && transition % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(before >= -9007199254740991.0 && before <= 9007199254740991.0 && before % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(after >= -9007199254740991.0 && after <= 9007199254740991.0 && after % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    if !(fold >= 0.0 && fold <= 9007199254740991.0 && fold % 1.0 == 0.0) { return []; }
    let result = blackbird_compute(local, transition, before, after, fold);
    if !blackbird_finite(result) { return []; }
    result
}

fn main() {
    let local = 11000.0;
    let transition = 10000.0;
    let before = 3600.0;
    let after = 0.0;
    let fold = 1.0;
    let result = blackbird_resolve(local, transition, before, after, fold);
    if len(result) == 0 { println!("invalid"); return; }
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len(result) {
        println!(at(result, i));
        i += 1;
    }
}
```

Expected output

```
2
11000
0
```

Solution

The result vector is [2, 7400, 3600]. Compare its fields with the return layout in the API section.


